![Inside the locked dorm sanctuary of Bennett Hall Room 214 on an October morning, eighteen-year-old Jordan Fuller sits upright in his manual wheelchair wearing his maroon CPI hoodie with his black laptop angled toward his face as he presses the execute key to declare 'I'm staying here,' surrounded in a fiercely protective circle by Aubrie Jean Kelly, Madison Scott, Zoë Wren Brooks, Lauren, and Hannah.]({{CDN}}/raggiesoft-books/images/scenes/aubrie/e001/c007/p003/the-choice-bennett-hall.jpg)

Less than ninety seconds after Zoë alerted the first-floor front desk, **Kelsey Brennan**, **Isabel Dawson**, and **Henry Walsh** stepped out through the lower-level exterior glass doors of Bennett Hall onto the brick inner-quad walkway—pulling the heavy doors firmly shut behind them until the magnetic locks clicked—and intercepted **Aubrie Sinclair** twenty feet before she could even reach the card reader.

Up inside the warm, locked sanctuary of Room 214, Jordan sat in his wheelchair surrounded by **Aubrie Kelly**, **Madison**, **Zoë**, **Lauren**, and **Hannah**, listening through the open speakerphone connection on Zoë’s mPhone as Kelsey’s voice rang out across the crisp October air outside.

The instant Aubrie Sinclair saw a professional adult staff member wearing an official CPI Residence Life lanyard step onto the walkway, she put her hands to her chest, her voice shifting back into theatrical, martyred distress.

"Oh, thank goodness an actual adult is finally out here!" Aubrie Sinclair exclaimed, gesturing dramatically toward the locked exterior doors of Bennett Hall. "Are you in charge of this building? Your doors are locked and a rude student just slammed the upper entrance in my face! My son, Aubrey, is severely disabled and is being held inside Room 214 against his will by a group of girls! They've brainwashed him, and you need to unlock this door and bring him out to my car so he can come home to Virginia Beach with me immediately!"

Kelsey didn't even flinch at Aubrie Sinclair’s performance.

Standing shoulder-to-shoulder on the brick walkway with Isabel and Henry flanking her like an impenetrable wall in front of the locked lower entrance, Kelsey held up her own phone—already conferenced into Room 214’s speakerphone—and spoke directly to Jordan inside his room.

"Jordan, this is Kelsey Brennan outside the first-floor entrance with Isabel and Henry," Kelsey said, her voice crystal clear, measured, and carrying the full legal weight of Commonwealth Polytechnic Institute through the speaker in Room 214. "Your mother is out here on the walkway, and the building is completely secured. You are eighteen years old. You are a legal adult, and you are a contracted resident of this university. Our residence halls are remaining open for Fall Break. Under university policy and Virginia law, it is entirely your decision whether you wish to stay safely inside Room 214 or leave with your mother for the break. No one can force you to do anything you do not want to do."

Kelsey paused, holding the speakerphone up on the exterior walkway so both she and Aubrie Sinclair could hear Room 214 clearly.

"What do you want to do, Jordan?"

Inside Room 214, all five women held their breath.

This was it—the final threshold between the eighteen years behind him and the rest of his life ahead of him.

Jordan looked at the glowing speakerphone on his desk—knowing his mother was standing outside the locked doors of Bennett Hall, the woman who had denied him glasses so the world stayed a blur, denied him hearing aids so voices stayed muffled, forced him to carry her own name so he could never be a separate human being, and tried to convince him that no one on earth could ever love him without considering him a crushing burden.

Then Jordan turned his head and looked at the five women standing around his wheelchair inside his warm, impregnable room—**Aubrie Kelly**, **Madison**, **Zoë**, **Lauren**, and **Hannah**—knowing that **Mark**, **Sarah**, and **Jessica** were part of this unbreakable circle too, and knowing that **Kelsey**, **Isabel**, and **Henry** were standing outside the locked doors of Bennett Hall like a wall of iron so his mother could never set a single foot inside his home. In less than two months, these people had given him more unconditional love, dignity, and freedom than he had ever known existed.

He looked up at Aubrie Jean Kelly, whose warm hand had never left his shoulder. He saw a future completely free from his mother’s cage—a future where he could study the stars, live in the light as Jordan Fuller, and maybe one day, when they were older, ask Aubrie Jean to marry him and seal his freedom forever.

Jordan looked straight down at his keyboard. His hands didn't shake at all as he typed three words into EchoType and pressed the execute key, sending his clear synthesized baritone ringing through the speakerphone out onto the brick walkway of Bennett Hall:

<aac>I'm staying here.</aac>

Out on the walkway, a strangled, furious gasp tore from his mother’s throat. "You cannot do this to me, Aubrey! I am your mother!"

Now—and only now—did Kelsey Brennan look squarely at Aubrie Sinclair. Her expression was cool, immovable granite.

"His name is **Jordan**," Kelsey said evenly, her voice carrying clearly over the open line into Room 214. "And as an adult resident of this university, he has made his decision. Furthermore, you are flagged on our Residence Life security portal as an unauthorized visitor, you have zero permission to enter Bennett Hall, and every exterior door of this building will remain locked to you."

Kelsey gestured cleanly up the brick path toward Washington Street SW.

"You need to leave the grounds of Bennett Hall right now, ma'am," Kelsey stated flatly. "Henry and Isabel will walk parallel to you along the exterior sidewalk back up to Washington Street to make sure you reach your vehicle. If you refuse to leave the exterior walkway, or if you attempt to tailgate through any door of Bennett Hall, I will have the CPI Police Department arrest you for criminal trespass."

For five trembling seconds, Aubrie Sinclair glared at Kelsey, Isabel, and Henry standing in front of the locked glass doors—realizing that she hadn't even been able to set foot inside the building, and that her tantrums and threats had zero leverage left. Shaking with silent, humiliated rage, she spun on her heel and marched back up the exterior sidewalk toward Washington Street SW while Henry and Isabel watched from the top of the path until she climbed into her sedan.

"She's heading back to her car right now, Jordan," Kelsey said warmly into the phone before ending the conference call. "You are 100% safe inside Room 214. Take all the time you need with your friends today. We've got the doors."

For a heartbeat after the call clicked off, a profound, shuddering silence filled the small cinderblock room.

Then Jordan let out a long, ragged exhale he felt like he had been holding in his lungs for eighteen years. His hands were trembling from the adrenaline dump, and his eyes burned behind his glasses—but his mother had never even made it through the front door, and he was free.

Before the first tear could even reach his cheek, all five women moved at once. Aubrie knelt at his front, wrapping her arms tightly around his neck; Madison and Lauren threw their arms around his shoulders from either side; and Hannah and Zoë closed the circle around them, wrapping Jordan in a massive, fiercely protective group hug that anchored him in the joyful, undeniable truth of his new life.

His mother was gone, Bennett Hall was locked down tight, and he was finally home.

### Part 4: The Cut Cord

**Date:** 2014-10-18 at 10:45 America/New_York

An hour after Aubrie Sinclair had stormed off the exterior walkway outside Bennett Hall without ever setting foot inside the building, a fragile, hard-won peace had settled over Suite 214/216.

Around ten-forty-five, a gentle, rhythmic three-beat knock—the familiar signal **Isabel Dawson** and **Henry Walsh** always used so Jordan knew it was them—sounded on the door of Room 214. Lauren pressed the interior **PUSH TO OPEN** button, and Isabel and Henry stepped just inside the threshold.

"Just wanted to give you guys the official all-clear," Henry said with a reassuring smile. "Kelsey and I watched from the atrium windows—your mom got into her sedan on Washington Street and drove off campus toward Route 460 about forty-five minutes ago. And Kelsey already sent a reminder flash to every resident in Bennett Hall about zero tailgating at the corridor doors."

"You were incredible in here today, Jordan," Isabel said warmly.

Jordan released his wheel locks and rolled across the linoleum to the doorway, opening his arms in silent gratitude.

Isabel smiled, stepping smoothly beside his wheelchair and leaning down to wrap both arms across his shoulders in her warm, strictly platonic big-sister hug, patting the back of his shoulder twice before straightening up beside Henry.

"Enjoy your Fall Break, guys," Isabel said cheerfully. "We'll see you later!"

Once the ten-second timer eased the door shut and locked it behind their RAs, **Madison** clapped her hands together in the center of the room, determined to chase away the last lingering shadow of the morning’s confrontation.

"Okay, I am officially declaring October eighteenth a suite holiday," Madison announced brightly. "Happy **Jordan's Independence Day**, everybody! And every real holiday requires celebratory pizza. A massive amount of celebratory pizza."

A chorus of cheers went up from Aubrie, Lauren, and Hannah.

Jordan felt a small, tired, genuine smile tug at the corners of his mouth. Wanting to contribute to the celebration, he typed a quick line on his Vanguard Pro before reaching for his mPhone on the corner of his desk:

<aac>I can place the order from my phone. Campus Pizza lets you text or dial in the suite order.</aac>

He picked up his mPhone, woke the screen, and tapped the saved number for Campus Pizza—hitting **Send** to test the line before routing his laptop audio.

Instead of ringing, the screen flashed a stark red banner accompanied by three flat, descending digital tones:

**Call Ended**

Jordan frowned behind his glasses. Assuming the thick cinderblock walls of Bennett Hall had caused a momentary hiccup, he tapped **Redial**.

The call failed instantaneously a second time.

Jordan’s eyes drifted up to the top-left corner of the glass display. Where the familiar stair-stepped cellular signal bars and carrier name usually sat, the status bar was completely blank—replaced by two cold, gray words:

**No Service**

He typed into EchoType, his brow furrowing in confusion:

<aac>That's weird. My phone says No Service. It won't connect at all.</aac>

"Try restarting it, J," Lauren suggested gently from the edge of the lower bunk. "Sometimes the cell towers around Commonwealth Green glitch out and a reboot fixes the handshake."

Jordan held down the power button, slid the prompt to power off, waited ten seconds, and booted the mPhone back up. For a few seconds, the carrier search spinner rotated in the top corner of the glass—and then snapped straight back to **No Service**.

He held the screen up so the five women could see the dead status bar.

"Wait a minute—that makes zero sense," **Zoë** said, her analytical instincts immediately going on alert as she pulled her own mPhone from her pocket. "You and I are on the exact same cellular carrier, Jordan. Let me check the local tower signal."

She unlocked her screen and glanced at the top corner.

"My carrier connection is completely normal," Zoë reported, her voice dropping half an octave as her logical mind systematically eliminated every technical hardware or tower failure. "I have three full bars of LTE right here in Room 214."

The room went dead silent.

The implication of Zoë’s diagnosis landed in the center of the floor like a slab of cold iron. Slowly, Zoë lowered her phone and looked directly at Jordan, her gray eyes grave as she asked the single question that was suddenly on everyone’s mind:

"Jordan... who pays your cell phone bill?"

Jordan’s hands went still on his armrests. With a single tap of his index finger on the keyboard, the answer echoed softly through the quiet room:

<aac>My mother.</aac>

"That spiteful, vindictive witch!" Madison gasped, her hands balling into fists at her sides as her face flushed with outrage. "She couldn't drag you back to Virginia Beach in her car, so before she even hit the highway, she called the carrier and shut off your phone?!"

The cold, calculated cruelty of the move sank in across the room.

It wasn't a network outage, and it wasn't a broken SIM card. On early move-in day, his mother had ordered him to keep that phone charged in his pocket so he could answer her on the first ring. Now that he had defied her in front of five witnesses and chosen to stay at CPI, she had immediately executed a retaliatory strike from the driver’s seat of her car—terminating his cellular line to cut his digital cord to the outside world.

It was a punishment designed to prove her thesis: that without her money and her permission, he was stranded, helpless, and isolated.

"This is a critical safety vulnerability," Zoë stated immediately, her mind bypassing anger and locking straight into defensive engineering. "Inside Bennett Hall or the main academic buildings, your mPhone and your Vanguard Pro can communicate over the university's encrypted WiFi network. However, the moment you are in transit between buildings, on a bus, or anywhere off a WiFi node, you now have zero emergency communication capability. That is completely unacceptable."

"What do we do?" Lauren asked, her eyes wide with worry as she looked at Jordan. "We can figure out how to get him onto a prepaid or separate line eventually, but none of us have the money for a whole new cellular contract today."

"Then until we solve the phone line, he is never out there alone," **Aubrie Kelly** said, her voice ringing with fierce, immovable certainty as she stepped up beside Jordan’s chair and took his hand. "Not for a single minute. Whenever Jordan leaves this suite, at least one of us is with him at all times."

"The **Buddy System**," Madison nodded, her eyes lighting up with tactical resolve as she pulled her own phone out of her back pocket. "And we set up a dedicated dispatch group chat right now. Whoever is Jordan's buddy at any given hour drops a check-in text whenever they move: <sms>Got Jordan, heading to Pendleton Library,</sms> or <sms>With J at Kincaid Hall.</sms> That way, even when Jordan is between WiFi zones, all nine of us know his exact location and whose phone to call if we need to reach him!"

"I'm texting **Mark**, **Sarah**, and **Jessica** right now to add them to the chat," Hannah said, her thumbs already flying across her screen. "You know they'll be 100% in."

Sitting in his wheelchair with his Pinnacle Vanguard Pro across his knees, Jordan thought about the three Bennett Hall staff members who had just stood like a wall of iron outside the locked exterior doors of the building an hour ago—and especially about **Isabel Dawson** right across the hall in Room 215. Over the past two months, Isabel had quietly become his favorite CPI staff member by a mile, and the one authority figure on campus he had started to trust with even his most private, vulnerable details. He completely understood the professional boundary between an RA and a resident, and he would never ask her to cross it—but when it came to keeping him safe, he wanted her, **Henry**, and **Kelsey** inside the loop too.

His fingers moved across the keyboard and hit execute:

<aac>Can we add Isabel, Henry, and Kelsey into the group chat too? After what my mom just did, I want them to know where I am and who I'm with, too.</aac>

Aubrie Kelly’s eyes softened with pride as she squeezed his hand, while Zoë gave an immediate, approving nod.

"That is a remarkably sound tactical addition, Jordan," Zoë agreed. "Integrating Residence Life command directly into our dispatch channel means that if your mother—or anyone acting on her behalf—ever returns to campus, Kelsey, Henry, and Isabel will know your real-time location and escort status instantly."

"Adding Izzy, Henry, and Kelsey right now!" Madison grinned, her thumbs tapping rapidly as she built the twelve-person roster.

Jordan sat in his wheelchair, looking down at the dead **No Service** banner at the top of his mPhone—and then looking up at the five women rallying around him in a blur of fierce, coordinated devotion.

Yes, it was an inconvenience. Yes, his mother had tried to hurt him where she thought he was most vulnerable.

Yet as Jordan watched Madison type **[Jordan Comms]** into the header of the brand-new group chat while Aubrie laced her fingers tightly through his, a look of pure awe settled over his face. His mother had severed his cellular line to isolate him and punish him for choosing his new family. And in doing so, all she had accomplished was giving that family—and the trusted guardians of Bennett Hall—a reason to wrap themselves around him ten times tighter, weaving a human network of care so strong that nothing she did could ever cut him off again.

### Part 5: The New Lifeline and a Winter Pact & The Thanksgiving Ultimatum

**Date:** 2014-10-18 at 13:00 America/New_York

#### October 18, 2014 • 1:00 PM — The New Lifeline and a Winter Pact

By one o'clock on Saturday afternoon, with the boxes from their celebratory pizza lunch stacked neatly on the dresser and **Mark**, **Sarah**, and **Jessica** having joined the suite in Room 214, the mood had shifted from righteous outrage to focused, collaborative engineering.

"Okay, let's look at the board," **Madison** said, pacing across the rug with a slice of pepperoni crust in hand. "Getting Jordan onto a brand-new standalone cell plan is obviously the long-term goal, but carrier deposits and monthly lines are expensive, and none of us have that kind of spare cash sitting around right this second. So how do we get his phone working *now*, for Fall Break?"

"His physical handset is 100% functional; it is strictly the cellular SIM authentication that has been terminated," **Zoë** stated from her desk chair, her fingers already flying across the keyboard of her laptop. "Therefore, a Voice-over-IP service is the most logical interim architecture."

She swiveled her laptop screen ninety degrees so Jordan and the rest of the circle could see the interface.

"There are encrypted VoIP applications that assign a real, local area-code telephone number that routes entirely over the internet rather than cellular towers," Zoë explained, looking directly at Jordan to make sure every step was clear. "As long as your mPhone or your Vanguard Pro is connected to WiFi—here in Bennett Hall, in Pendleton Library, at Kincaid Hall, in any lecture hall, or at any coffee shop downtown with public wireless—you will be able to send and receive texts and place calls normally. It completely bypasses your mother's cellular carrier."

A collective grin broke out across the room.

Working side-by-side at Jordan’s desk, Zoë and **Aubrie Kelly** downloaded the VoIP client onto Jordan’s mPhone over the CPI campus wireless network, linked a synchronized desktop client onto his Vanguard Pro, and configured the text-to-speech bridge so EchoType could route straight across the line if he ever needed voice relay. Within ten minutes, a brand-new (540) Blacksburg exchange number glowed at the top of his screen.

"Okay," Aubrie said, her expression turning serious as she looked around the circle of nine. "Now for the most important security rule. Since Jordan already gave permission to include **Isabel**, **Henry**, and **Kelsey** in **Jordan Comms**, this new number does *not* go to anyone outside of the twelve people in that chat. Especially not your mother. As far as she knows, cutting your phone line left you completely unreachable except by email—and when she emails you, *you* decide if and when you ever answer."

Jordan looked down at the new (540) number on his screen and gave a firm, grateful nod. For the first time in his life, he had a telephone number that Aubrie Sinclair hadn't paid for, didn't own, and didn't even know existed.

"The VoIP deployment solves all stationary communication inside campus WiFi zones," Zoë continued, adjusting her glasses as she returned to the core safety equation. "However, the transit gap between buildings and off-campus remains. Therefore, the **Buddy System** and the **Jordan Comms** dispatch channel Madison initialized—with Kelsey, Henry, and Isabel monitoring alongside us—are mandatory whenever Jordan is on the move."

As Madison finished adding Jordan’s new VoIP number into the **Jordan Comms** group chat, **Lauren** looked up from the foot of the bed and voiced the heavier question that had been quietly forming in the back of everyone’s mind.

"Guys, this is a brilliant plan for this four-day break," Lauren said softly. "Because the dorms stay open for Fall Break. But... what about **Winter Break** in December? That's almost a full month long, and all the residence halls lock down completely. She's going to expect you to come back to Virginia Beach for a month."

For a moment, the air in Room 214 grew heavy. The thought of Jordan being forced back behind the closed blinds of that house in Virginia Beach for three-plus weeks after everything that had just happened made everyone’s stomach tighten.

"No," Aubrie said, her voice quiet but absolute as her fingers tightened around Jordan’s hand. "He isn't going back there. Not for a month, not for a day."

"Then where will we go?" Lauren asked gently.

"Well," **Hannah** spoke up thoughtfully from her spot beside Mark on the floor, "my parents' house is only twenty minutes from campus, so I'll be staying there. Mark and Sarah are both local to the New River Valley, too, Jessica's family is just forty minutes up I-81 in Roanoke, and Zoë's family lives right down Route 460 in Christiansburg."

It was a geographic reality the group knew in passing but hadn't fully weighed until now: five of their nine-person circle lived in the dorms for the freshman independence and campus experience rather than distance, while the other four—Jordan from Virginia Beach, Aubrie from Chesapeake, Madison from Bluewater, and Lauren from Gander, Newfoundland—were hours or countries away from home.

"Then the four of you who aren't local will establish a forward operating base right here in town," Zoë declared, her analytical mind immediately shifting into long-range logistics. "The logical solution is an extended-stay hotel near campus—one of the residential suites equipped with a full kitchenette and a living area. If we pool our resources and book early, it can serve as our headquarters for the break."

Madison’s face lit up instantly. "Yes! One of those extended-stay suites with two queen beds would be amazing! Jordan and one of us take one queen bed, the other two share the second queen bed, and we rotate nights just like our Nightly Pact here in the suite!"

Before Hannah even finished typing the idea into **Jordan Comms** so everyone had it in writing, Mark, Sarah, and Jessica were already chiming in out loud and on the screen at the same time:

> **Mark:** <sms>My folks will be happy to have me home for dinner, but fair warning—I'm basically gonna live at your hotel suite all break. Don't even think you're getting out of Monday Night WAR.</sms><br>
> **Sarah:** <sms>Same!! My house in Radford gets boring after two days. I'm bringing sleeping bags and all the snacks.</sms><br>
> **Jessica:** <sms>Roanoke is an easy drive down 81—count me in for the slumber party rotation!</sms><br>
> **Zoë:** <sms>I will compile a comparative budget spreadsheet and an accessibility audit of local extended-stay properties tonight.</sms>

Jordan looked around at the eight faces in Room 214 and down at the buzzing **Jordan Comms** thread in his hand.

They weren't just improvising a patch for Saturday afternoon. Without a second of hesitation, they were already building a fortress around his future—planning months ahead to make sure his mother could never trap him during a holiday shutdown.

"Okay!" Madison grinned, clapping her hands together with infectious energy. "The Winter Pact is officially ratified, and VoIP is live. Now for the **Fall Break Relay**. Who's up first?"

***

#### October 19, 2014 • 10:30 AM — The Daily Grind

The Fall Break weekend unfolded as a masterclass in compassionate, seamless logistics. Born out of his mother’s attempt to isolate him, the **Buddy System** and the **Jordan Comms** group chat instantly became the central nervous system of their nine-person family—plus **Kelsey Brennan**, **Isabel Dawson**, and **Henry Walsh**, whom Jordan had explicitly invited into the channel.

On Sunday morning at ten-thirty, the first official dispatch of the day chimed across every phone in the pact:

> **Aubrie:** <sms>[LOGISTICS] With Jordan! Heading over to 'The Daily Grind' in Kincaid Hall for lattes and a change of scenery.</sms>

As Jordan and **Aubrie Kelly** rolled out of Room 214 into the second-floor hallway, **Isabel Dawson** was stepping out of Room 215 with a canvas tote bag slung over her shoulder on her way to the quiet study lounge, her own phone still in her hand from reading Aubrie’s dispatch.

Spotting her, Jordan immediately slowed his chair, clicked his brakes, and opened his arms with a bright morning grin behind his glasses.

"Good morning, Jordan!" Isabel laughed softly, her eyes crinkling with warmth. Stepping smoothly to the side of his wheelchair, she leaned down and gave him her gentle, strictly platonic one-armed hug across the shoulders, patting the back of his maroon Forgers hoodie twice before straightening back up. "I just saw Aubrie's check-in pop up on **Jordan Comms**! Did Zoë get your new WiFi number up and running cleanly?"

Jordan held up his mPhone proudly, showing her the active **Jordan Comms** thread on his screen.

"Thank you for letting me, Henry, and Kelsey be part of your chat, Jordan," Isabel said, her voice softening with genuine gratitude as she tapped her own screen. "We saved your new VoIP number into our duty phones last night, and we won't share it with a soul. Have a wonderful time at Kincaid Hall, you two!"

As they rolled toward the elevator, Jordan felt a quiet warmth settle in his chest. He understood the professional Residence Life boundary completely—Isabel was his Resident Advisor, and he would never do a single thing to blur that line or risk the job she depended on. Yet out of every staff member at CPI, Isabel had unmistakably become his favorite, and the one person in a position of university authority he was beginning to trust with his most private, unguarded truths.

For over an hour, Jordan and Aubrie sat at a sunlit corner table inside **The Daily Grind**, sipping warm vanilla lattes and splitting a cinnamon roll. Surrounded by **Kincaid Hall**’s high-output campus WiFi routers, Jordan’s mPhone worked flawlessly, chiming with banter and photos from the rest of the group while he and Aubrie talked and people-watched through the tall arched windows.

Right around noon, a new chain of messages lit up **Jordan Comms**:

> **Madison:** <sms>Okay, I am officially going stir-crazy in the dorm. Anyone up for an afternoon expedition into downtown Blacksburg?</sms><br>
> **Lauren:** <sms>YES! The autumn leaves on Main Street are gorgeous right now. I'm in!</sms><br>
> **Zoë:** <sms>I will accompany you. I need to pick up a reference volume from the downtown bookshop anyway.</sms><br>
> **Aubrie:** <sms>Perfect timing! Hannah and I have our HLTH 201 midterm review at 12:30. J and I are at Kincaid Hall—meet us at the Commonwealth Mall bus stop beneath The Keystone Bridge in fifteen!</sms>

***

#### October 19, 2014 • 12:15 PM — The Real BT

The noon handoff along **Commonwealth Mall** beneath the limestone arch of **The Keystone Bridge** across the street from **Kincaid Hall** was executed with clockwork precision. **Aubrie Kelly** gave Jordan a warm kiss on the cheek before heading off across **Commonwealth Green** to meet **Hannah**, while **Madison**, **Lauren**, and **Zoë** stepped in as his designated afternoon buddies.

All around them along the unmarked Commonwealth Mall curb—where there were no bus bays at all and buses simply lined up one behind the other in a disorganized free-for-all—clusters of students were grumbling as usual, craning their necks toward the **Business 460** intersection because nobody ever knew which route would be the next to turn onto the boulevard. Moments later, a forty-foot low-floor **Blue Ridge Transit** city bus swung off Business 460 and glided up to the curb, its white-and-pine-green livery and prominent **BT** emblem gleaming in the crisp October sun. With a soft hiss of air brakes, the front suspension kneeled toward the concrete and the front passenger boarding doors folded wide, deploying the yellow-edged aluminum ADA wheelchair ramp directly onto the sidewalk from the front doorway.

As Jordan rolled smoothly up the front ramp and backed into the forward wheelchair securement bay while Lauren and Zoë clicked the four-point retractors onto his frame, Madison stepped up beside the farebox and held up her **Poly Pass** so the driver could see it—getting a wickedly mischievous glint in her eye.

Leaning slightly toward the driver, a good-natured man in his mid-fifties wearing a short-sleeved transit shirt, Madison flashed a playful grin.

"Just so you know," Madison said conversationally, "we all know the *real* BT is the one back in my hometown—**Bluewater Transit**."

The driver didn't miss a single beat. Glancing up at her in his wide overhead rearview mirror, he offered a dry, amused smirk.

"That's funny, honey," the driver drawled. "My paycheck says **Blue Ridge Transit**, and we're the only ones hauling sixty thousand people up this mountain on game day. Sounds pretty real to me." He jerked a thumb good-naturedly toward the open seats beside Jordan’s bay. "Now find yourself a seat before you hold up my whole schedule."

Madison burst out laughing, completely delighted by the banter as she slid onto the fold-down bench right beside Jordan’s chair.

As the bus pulled out of the campus lineup and rolled down toward the historic heart of downtown Blacksburg, the university’s WiFi signal faded from the top of Jordan’s screen. Twenty-four hours ago, watching that connection indicator disappear would have sent a spike of panic through his chest. Today, with Madison grinning on his left, Lauren sitting on his right, and Zoë standing steady at the stanchion in front of him, Jordan felt zero anxiety at all. He wasn't disconnected; his network was sitting right beside him.

When the bus pulled up to the Main Street stop downtown and the driver deployed the front-door ramp again, Madison paused by the driver’s window on her way out.

"Sorry for calling you the fake BT," she whispered conspiratorially with a grin.

The driver shook his head, chuckling warmly as he retracted the ramp. "Have a good afternoon, Bluewater."

***

#### October 19, 2014 • 2:00 PM — Main Street

Jordan, **Madison**, **Lauren**, and **Zoë** spent the next two hours wandering the brick sidewalks of downtown Blacksburg beneath a canopy of scarlet and gold October maples, browsing the quirky shop windows along Main Street until they ducked into a sprawling, two-story independent bookstore lined with worn leather armchairs, the smell of espresso, and—best of all—a free public WiFi network.

While Lauren browsed the typography shelves and Zoë tracked down her systems-engineering reference volume, Jordan wheeled over to a low oak display table near the architecture and history section. Resting on top of the stack was an oversized, richly illustrated hardcover titled ***"Civitas: A Story of Roman Planning and Engineering"*** by **Arthur MacAllister**.

Curious, Jordan picked it up and rested it across his lap, leaning in close behind his glasses to study the intricate black-and-white pen-and-ink cross-sections. Page after page showed how Roman military surveyors and civil engineers planned an entire city from scratch—laying out the perpendicular grid of the *cardo* and *decumanus*, bridging valleys with multi-tiered stone aqueducts, and engineering vaulted baths, forums, and underground drainage tunnels that lasted for two thousand years. To Jordan’s structured, pattern-seeking mind, the idea that an ancient civilization had brought that level of geometric order and permanence to the physical world was completely mesmerizing. He didn't purchase the book—setting it carefully back onto the display table so he wouldn't spend his emergency cash—but as he wheeled over to join Madison and Lauren by the leather armchairs, his mind was buzzing with a brand-new curiosity about **Ancient Rome**.

The instant Jordan’s mPhone authenticated to the bookstore’s wireless router, his handset chimed with a rapid-fire cascade of notifications from **Jordan Comms** that had queued up while they were strolling down Main Street:

> **Hannah:** <sms>Mark says to tell you Dr. Destruction's cage-match promo last night was an all-time classic and he can't wait to break it down with you tonight.</sms><br>
> **Zoë:** <sms>[Attached: NRV_Extended_Stay_Audit_v1.pdf] Initial matrix of wheelchair-accessible hotel suites for December. Top three candidates highlighted in green.</sms><br>
> **Aubrie:** <sms>[Photo Attachment: A remarkably round campus gray squirrel glaring down from a low oak branch] I think this guy is trying to mug me for my HLTH 201 flashcards.</sms>

Jordan let out a silent, shaking laugh, turning his screen to show the squirrel photo to Lauren and Madison. His mother had cut off his cellular service to make his world small and silent—and instead, his world was overflowing with laughter, autumn sunlight, and constant connection.

At four-fifteen, one more message popped up at the bottom of the chat:

> **Mark:** <sms>[LOGISTICS] Just clocked out of my shift at the Campus Bookstore. I've got my car downtown—want me to swing by Main Street and give the four of you a lift back up the hill to Bennett Hall?</sms>

Fifteen minutes later, with Jordan transferred into the front passenger seat of Mark’s slightly beat-up but rock-solid sedan and his folded wheelchair stowed carefully in the trunk alongside Madison, Lauren, and Zoë’s bookstore bags, the five of them cruised back up the hill toward campus.

The Fall Break trial run of the Buddy System wasn't just working; it was a triumph.

***

#### October 20, 2014 • 8:30 PM — The Thanksgiving Ultimatum

On Monday night of Fall Break, all nine members of the pact—Jordan, Aubrie, Madison, Zoë, Lauren, Hannah, Mark, Sarah, and Jessica—were gathered on the couches of the first-floor lobby of Bennett Hall for their weekly **AWE Monday Night WAR** wrestling tradition when a new email notification chimed on Jordan’s Pinnacle Vanguard Pro.

The message had been sent to his original university email identifier—afuller001, the default account CPI’s servers had generated back in the summer from his legal first name—and the subject line made the cheerful warmth around the lobby couches evaporate in an instant:

> **To:** Aubrey Fuller (afuller001)<br>
> **From:** Aubrie Sinclair<br>
> **Date:** Monday, October 20, 2014 — 20:28 EDT<br>
> **Subject:** Thanksgiving Break Pickup — Wednesday, November 26 at 9:00 AM
>
> Aubrey,
>
> You may have hid behind your little friends and that dormitory woman this weekend because the building stayed open, but I have already looked up the university academic calendar.
>
> Every residence hall at Commonwealth Polytechnic Institute closes for Thanksgiving Break from Wednesday, November 26 at 1:00 PM until Sunday, November 30 at 4:00 PM. Students are not permitted to remain in the building.
>
> You WILL be coming home for Thanksgiving. I will be outside Bennett Hall at 9:00 AM sharp on Wednesday morning to bring you back to Virginia Beach, and we will discuss whether you are returning at all. Do not test me again.
>
> — Mom

Jordan’s hands went cold on the keyboard as the rest of the circle leaned in to read the screen over his shoulder.

"Wait—do the dorms really lock down for Thanksgiving too?" Lauren asked, her eyes darting to Zoë.

"Unfortunately, her citation of the housing calendar is accurate," **Zoë** confirmed, her expression serious. "Unlike Fall Break, the residence halls close completely for Thanksgiving from Wednesday at 1:00 PM until Sunday at 4:00 PM. Card access is suspended for all regular residents during that window."

"Okay," **Mark** said immediately, leaning forward with his elbows on his knees and his jaw set. "He's obviously not going within a hundred miles of her car on Wednesday morning. And booking a hotel for Thanksgiving week AND three weeks of Winter Break is gonna wipe out everything we have. Where can all nine of us go for Thanksgiving?"

Zoë didn't even need three seconds to calculate the answer. Her calm, pragmatic voice cut cleanly through the tension.

"My parents live twelve minutes down Route 460 in **Christiansburg**," Zoë stated simply. "Our house on Geneva Street is built into a hillside, and we have a massive, fully finished walk-out basement. It has its own living room, kitchenette, bathroom, and a wide sliding glass door that opens directly onto the backyard path—meaning there are zero interior stairs for Jordan to contend with."

She looked around the circle of couches, her invitation encompassing every single person in their chosen family.

"There is a pull-out sofa down there, and my parents have four queen-sized air mattresses and plenty of sleeping bags," Zoë continued. "You can all come stay with us in Christiansburg for Thanksgiving. All nine of us."

A wave of pure, electric relief washed over the group.

"**Sarah**, didn't you say your family's right over in Radford?" Madison asked.

Sarah grinned from ear to ear. "Yeah, my parents are fifteen minutes away, which means I can pop over for an hour on Thursday morning and spend the rest of the whole week crashing in a giant basement slumber party with you guys! I'm 100% in!"

"Same here!" **Jessica** added warmly from the arm of the sofa. "My folks in Roanoke are doing Thanksgiving lunch at noon on Thursday, so I can drive up 81 for three hours and spend the rest of the entire break in Christiansburg with you guys!"

"Perfect!" **Hannah** beamed, squeezing Mark’s hand. "Mark and I can visit our parents here in Blacksburg for lunch and spend the whole break at Zoë's with the group!"

Zoë pulled out her mPhone and stepped ten feet toward the quiet alcove by Kelsey’s office to call her mother, **Laura Brooks**. Less than three minutes later, she walked back to the couches and slid her phone into her pocket with a satisfied nod.

"The Christiansburg Sanctuary Plan is officially confirmed," Zoë announced. "My parents are completely on board. In fact, my mum is genuinely thrilled. She said—and I quote verbatim—*'A full house for Thanksgiving! Wonderful!'* She simply requested an accurate headcount so she knows how many pies to bake."

"Wait—what about helping Jordan with practical stuff at your parents' house, like getting in and out of the shower?" Madison asked, thinking through the daily care routines they shared so effortlessly in Suite 214. "That'll just be us girls handling that down in the basement, right?"

Mark let out a warm, genuine laugh, shaking his head with total affection. "Madison, you guys do whatever you need to do to take care of Jordan. Honestly, the fact that an insecure idiot like Tom ever freaked out about something so basic just proves what a loser he is. I trust Hannah, and I trust all of you completely."

Hannah looked at Mark, her eyes shining with love and pride.

Then Zoë added the final tactical stroke: "And rather than waiting until Wednesday when the dorms close at 1:00 PM, all nine of us will head out to Christiansburg on **Tuesday afternoon**, a full day before your mother plans to arrive. And before we leave campus next month, Jordan, we will stop by Kelsey's office and **CPI Campus Police** just like Kelsey suggested, so your no-contact statement and my parents' address are officially on file. When your mother pulls up on Wednesday morning, she will find an empty room and a locked building."

### Part 6: The Digital Wall & A Continent of Their Own

**Date:** 2014-10-20 at 20:50 America/New_York

#### October 20, 2014 • 8:50 PM — The Digital Wall

Twenty minutes later, back upstairs in the quiet safety of **Room 214**, the wrestling match on TV was forgotten.

Jordan sat in front of his Vanguard Pro, staring at the cold words of his mother’s email still open on his screen: *Aubrey, you WILL be coming home...*

He looked at the legal first name she used like a leash, and at the afuller001 identifier at the top of the window. Thanks to Zoë and the Brooks family, they had a physical fortress for Thanksgiving—and thanks to Zoë’s VoIP setup, his mother no longer had his phone number. Now, sitting at his desk, Jordan realized he needed to brick up the last digital window she was using to throw stones at him.

He opened EchoType, his fingers steady and resolute on the keys:

<aac>I don't want to get emails from her anymore. Not like this. Not ever again.</aac>

**Zoë**, who was sitting at her own desk five feet away, swiveled her chair around immediately.

"We can engineer a permanent fix for that tonight," Zoë said crisply. "University mail servers do not permit blocking external senders at the student level, *but* we can permanently decommission the address she knows about. Because your preferred name—**Jordan Fuller**—is already officially recorded with the University Registrar and the FERPA block Kelsey filed for you, you are entitled to have your primary student username regenerated to match your preferred name."

She rolled her chair beside his wheelchair and guided him to the **CPI Information Technology Support Portal**. Together, with **Aubrie Kelly** resting her chin warmly on Jordan’s shoulder as she watched, Jordan typed out the formal support ticket:

> **From:** Jordan Fuller (afuller001)<br>
> **To:** CPI Information Technology — Account Management & Identity Services<br>
> **Date:** Monday, October 20, 2014 — 20:54 EDT<br>
> **Subject:** Primary Student Identifier & Email Alias Replacement (Active FERPA Hold)<br>
>
> Hello,
>
> I am writing to request an immediate change to my primary student email identifier. My current account (afuller001) was automatically generated from my legal first name, *Aubrey*, which I do not use. My preferred name, **Jordan Fuller**, and my FERPA Directory Non-Disclosure hold are already on file with the Office of the University Registrar.
>
> An external family member is using the old afuller001 identifier to send harassing and coercive messages. To protect my safety and privacy, I request that a new primary student email identifier be generated under my preferred name (**Jordan Fuller**) and that the legacy afuller001 alias be permanently deactivated so any messages sent to it bounce back as undeliverable.
>
> Thank you,<br>
> Jordan Fuller

Jordan read the ticket over one last time, took a deep breath, and clicked **Submit Ticket**.

Because his active FERPA confidentiality flag was already linked in the university identity database, the automated identity-services script processed the preferred-name regeneration within seconds—flashing a green confirmation banner across the portal screen:

**PRIMARY IDENTIFIER UPDATED: jfuller004 — LEGACY ALIAS (afuller001) QUEUED FOR PERMANENT DEACTIVATION**

It was a small, bureaucratic click of a trackpad, but to Jordan, watching **jfuller004** appear at the top of his student profile felt like slamming a six-inch steel vault door shut.

Aubrie Jean reached down and covered his hand on the keyboard with hers. "Good," she whispered softly. "One less way for her to ever reach you."

***

#### October 21, 2014 • 10:00 PM — A Continent of Their Own

On Tuesday night—the final evening of Fall Break before Wednesday morning classes resumed—the air in Suite 214/216 was warm with the lazy, contented satisfaction of a four-day holiday well spent.

All nine of them were piled into Room 214, sprawled across the unbunked beds and the braided rug, finishing off the last slices of cold pizza from an afternoon movie marathon.

Around ten o'clock, **Mark** stretched his long legs and stood up, reaching down to pull **Hannah** to her feet. "Alright, we gotta jet so everybody gets some sleep before eight-o'clock lectures tomorrow."

"Thank you guys for this weekend," **Sarah** said warmly as she and **Jessica** gave Lauren, Madison, and Aubrie each a tight hug before squeezing Jordan’s shoulder. "Seriously—best Fall Break ever."

When Hannah pressed the square **PUSH TO OPEN** button to let Mark, Sarah, and Jessica out into the second-floor corridor, **Isabel Dawson** and **Henry Walsh** were just walking past Room 214 on their ten-o'clock evening floor rounds.

"Evening, Suite 214!" Henry grinned, giving Mark, Sarah, and Jessica a wave as they headed for the stairwell. "Everybody ready for classes tomorrow?"

Before the ten-second door timer could begin its closing cycle, Jordan wheeled straight up to the threshold, set his brakes, and opened his arms toward Isabel with a warm, happy smile.

Isabel’s face lit up. Stepping smoothly beside his wheelchair in the doorway, she leaned down and wrapped both arms around his shoulders in her gentle, strictly platonic big-sister hug, patting the back of his hoodie twice before stepping back beside Henry.

"You handled this whole weekend like a total champion, Jordan," Isabel said warmly. "And Kelsey told us earlier how glad she was to hear that you guys already have a plan for Thanksgiving. Sleep well tonight, everybody!"

"Night, guys!" Henry added, tapping Jordan’s fist before the two RAs continued down the hall and the heavy oak door eased shut, clicking locked automatically behind them.

With Hannah, Lauren, and Zoë retreating through the connecting bathroom into Room 216 to brush their teeth and get ready for bed, a peaceful, familiar quiet settled over Room 214.

Later, changed into his cotton pajamas and sitting in his wheelchair beside his bed before transferring onto the mattress, Jordan picked up his mPhone. Connected to Bennett Hall’s wireless network, the screen glowed softly in his hands.

He opened the **Jordan Comms** group chat and slid his thumb upward—scrolling up, and up, and up through the four-day log of his newfound freedom:

> **Zoë [Sun 14:10]:** <sms>With Jordan. Heading to the third floor of Pendleton Library so he can work on his astrophysics problem set.</sms><br>
> **Madison [Mon 11:25]:** <sms>Got him! We're out on Commonwealth Green soaking up the sun! ☀️</sms><br>
> **Hannah [Mon 17:40]:** <sms>Everyone's back at the suite. Pizza run is a go—Mark is bringing it up now.</sms><br>
> **Mark [Mon 19:50]:** <sms>We've secured the prime lobby couches. AWE Monday Night WAR is a go. Tell J that Dr. Destruction is going down tonight.</sms><br>
> **Lauren [Tue 14:15]:** <sms>[Photo Attachment: Jordan sitting in his wheelchair in a sunny field of orange pumpkins, holding a wonderfully lopsided pumpkin in his lap with a huge grin behind his glasses] Sarah, Jessica, and I have Jordan! Pumpkin patch expedition is a complete success!</sms><br>
> **Isabel [Tue 14:17]:** <sms>That pumpkin is a 10/10, Jordan!! 🎃 Henry and Kelsey are on duty at the desk and say it has been 100% quiet at Bennett Hall all week.</sms><br>
> **Aubrie [Tue 18:30]:** <sms>Just me and J now. Grabbing hot chocolate at the dining hall before we head back up the hill to The Old Lady.</sms>

Jordan stared at the glowing stream of check-ins, candid photos, and effortless handoffs, and a quiet, overwhelming realization washed over him.

On Saturday morning, his mother had tried to punish him for choosing his own life. When she couldn't force him into her car, she had severed his cellular service to make his world small, silent, and frightening—to prove that without her permission and her money, he was stranded on a lonely island.

She had failed spectacularly.

All her act of spite had accomplished was giving his chosen family a reason to draw him in even closer. They had taken her malice and transformed it into an intricate, joyful dance of care—engineering a communication network over campus WiFi, building the Buddy System, shutting down his old afuller001 email alias, and already planning a Thanksgiving sanctuary at **Daniel and Laura Brooks**’s house in Christiansburg.

And sitting there in the quiet glow of Room 214, Jordan realized something else.

Three weeks ago in **Kelsey Brennan**’s lamp-lit office—the room down on the first floor that he now thought of as one of his **Safe Places**—he had asked Kelsey to hold his **Emergency Contact Change Form** and his **CPI Campus Police** statement in her locked top drawer until he knew which trusted adults he wanted to name in his mother’s place.

Remembering the unconditional kindness in **Daniel Brooks**’s voice on move-in day when he had knelt beside Jordan’s chair, and thinking of **Laura Brooks** enthusiastically welcoming all nine of them into her home for Thanksgiving (*"A full house for Thanksgiving! Wonderful!"*), Jordan knew that his wait was almost over. Next month, right before they boarded the bus to Christiansburg for Thanksgiving, he was going to walk into Kelsey’s office and the CPI Campus Police station—and he was going to put Daniel and Laura Brooks on the record as his official emergency contacts.

His mother had tried to leave him stranded on an island. In response, his family had built him a continent.

Jordan lowered his phone and looked up. **Aubrie Jean Kelly** was watching him from the edge of their bed, a soft, knowing smile on her face as she held the covers open for him.

Jordan smiled back—a peaceful, unburdened smile that didn't need a single word—transferred onto the mattress beside her, and let her wrap him in her arms for the night.

### Part 7: Mark's Hometown Trail, The Blue Ridge Regional Aquatic Center & A Neighbor's Wave on the Huckleberry Trail

**Date:** 2014-10-21 at 14:30 America/New_York

#### October 21, 2014 • 2:30 PM — The Local From Radford Takes Command

Tuesday afternoon was the final day of **Commonwealth Polytechnic Institute**’s four-day **Fall Break** before classes resumed on Wednesday morning—and for **Jordan**, it was Day Four of his new life after telling his mother *"I'm staying here"* outside Bennett Hall.

At `14:30`, **Mark Anderson** walked into Room 214 wearing his maroon CPI hoodie with a rolled-up towel slung over his shoulder and a look of mock local indignation on his face.

Having grown up right down the river in **Radford** and spent every summer of his childhood attending youth engineering and sports camps on the CPI campus, Mark knew every back road, bus route, and trail in Montgomery County by heart.

"Okay, hold everything," Mark announced, looking around the suite at **Jordan**, **Aubrie Jean**, **Madison**, **Zoë**, **Lauren**, **Hannah**, **Sarah**, **Jessica**, and **Isabel**. "You guys have been living in the New River Valley for two full months, the leaves are at absolute peak October color, and none of you have ever been on the **Huckleberry Trail** OR inside the **Blue Ridge Regional Aquatic Center**?"

"I know the trailhead starts over by the **Pendleton Library** lawn," Hannah said, looking up from her sketchbook, "but how far does it go?"

"Six miles of paved, car-free rail-trail all the way from the library lawn to **Christiansburg**," Mark grinned. "Built right over the bed of the old nineteenth-century **Huckleberry Train** that used to chug between **Cambria Depot** and campus until 1958. And right at the Christiansburg end off **Mill Lane** and **North Franklin Street** is the **Blue Ridge Regional Aquatic Center**—where the **CPI Forgers** swim team races, AND where they have a ninety-five-point-five-degree warm water therapy pool called **The Cove**."

At the words *ninety-five-point-five-degree warm water therapy pool*, Jordan’s eyes lit up behind his rectangular polycarbonate glasses. Ever since the October mountain chill had settled over Blacksburg, the cerebral palsy spasticity in his calves and hamstrings had been noticeably tighter in the mornings.

Tap-tap-tap went Jordan’s fingers on the keyboard of his `Vanguard Pro`:

**"Do they let Blacksburg students use the therapy pool? How much is a membership?"**

"Because it’s owned and operated by the **Town of Christiansburg**, Town of Christiansburg residents get resident rates, and those of us living in **Blacksburg** or **Radford** pay the **Non-Resident Monthly Membership**," Mark explained. "Thirty bucks a month for unlimited thirty-day access—or ten bucks for a day pass—and it has zero-depth ramps and private accessible family changing rooms. Grab your swimsuits and your hoodies. We’re taking **Blue Ridge Transit Route 1** and **Route 2** down to the Aquatic Center first while our muscles are warm, and then we’re walking and rolling the **Huckleberry Trail** back to campus at sunset!"

***

#### 3:15 PM — *The Cove* (`95.5°F`) at the Blue Ridge Regional Aquatic Center

Forty minutes later, after flashing their **Poly Passes** on **Blue Ridge Transit** down to Christiansburg and signing up for their **`$30.00/month` Town of Christiansburg Non-Resident** barcode keytags at the front desk (`$30.00` loaded neatly into `Fin#` under `Recreation & Physical Therapy`), the ten of them stepped into the sixty-four-thousand-square-foot natatorium of the **Blue Ridge Regional Aquatic Center**.

Jordan had never seen an indoor pool complex like it in his life. To their left stretched the massive **50-Meter Olympic Competition Pool** (*The Forger Natatorium*) beneath a ten-meter concrete diving tower and a thousand-seat spectator gallery; straight ahead was the **Leisure Pool** with its zero-depth beach entry and two-story triple-loop yellow water slide; and tucked into a warm, sunlit alcove to the right was **The Cove**.

After changing inside one of the private, wheelchair-accessible **Family Changing Suites** (equipped with a roll-in shower, grab bars, and a fold-down padded transfer bench) with **Aubrie Jean**’s help, Jordan transferred into one of the facility’s waterproof PVC deck wheelchairs and rolled straight down the gentle, non-slip zero-depth ramp into **The Cove**.

The instant the **`95.5°F`** water enveloped his legs and hips, Jordan let out a long, shaky breath of pure relief.

On land, cerebral palsy meant gravity was a constant negotiation—a low-level static of involuntary muscle tone in his legs and lower back. In `95.5°F` water, gravity simply ceased to exist. As Aubrie Jean stepped into the warm water beside him and wrapped her arms around his waist to float with him near the hydrotherapy jets—joined by Madison, Zoë, Lauren, Hannah, Mark, Sarah, Jessica, and Isabel—Jordan’s tight hamstrings and calves unknotted completely, floating weightless and warm while Zoë logged the thermal metrics with a contented sigh:

> `[ZOË.Systems.Logs // 2014-10-21 15:40:12 EDT]`<br>
> `FACILITY: Blue Ridge Regional Aquatic Center (Town of Christiansburg — Non-Resident Tier: $30.00/mo)`<br>
> `POOL_ZONE: "The Cove" Warm Water Therapy Pool (Temp: 95.5°F / Zero-Depth Ramp Entry)`<br>
> `BIOMETRIC_OBSERVATION: Jordan Fuller lower-extremity spasticity index reduced by ~78%. Zero acoustic echoing in alcove. Optimal aquatic sanctuary confirmed.`

***

#### 5:30 PM — The Huckleberry Trail & The Unwritten Rule of Blacksburg

By `17:00`, thoroughly warmed from the `95.5°F` pool, showered, and dressed in their warm fleece layers and maroon-and-orange **CPI** hoodies, the group decided to walk and roll the northern half of the **Huckleberry Trail** together from the **Pendleton Library** lawn out past the agricultural pastures and back at dusk.

As they rolled south from the **Pendleton Library** trailhead along the ten-foot-wide paved asphalt path, Jordan fell in love with the trail immediately.

Unlike a city street, there were no cars, no curbs, no diesel exhaust, and no steep cross-slopes—just smooth, level black asphalt winding along the gentle grade where the old **Huckleberry Train** had rolled for half a century, bordered by weathered wooden split-rail fences, grazing cattle in rolling green pastures, and a blazing autumn canopy of crimson sugar maples and burnt-orange oaks overhead.

At **`5:30 PM`**, as the air turned crisp (`48°F`) and woodsmoke curled in a silver wisp from a farmhouse chimney across the pasture, Mark glanced fifty yards down the paved path toward Christiansburg—and stopped talking mid-sentence.

Coming northbound up the Huckleberry Trail straight toward them were two figures moving side by side at an easy, rhythmic pace: a woman in her mid-forties with glasses and a maroon CPI jacket riding a vintage touring bicycle with a glowing front dynamo lamp, and right beside her, a man in a matte-black titanium manual wheelchair pushing his handrims with effortless, powerful strokes through the golden leaves.

Madison’s breath caught in her throat. She whispered so softly only their group could hear:

*"Wait... is that—"*

"Shh—yep," Mark whispered back with a proud local’s grin, keeping his voice low and his stride completely natural. "That’s **Ryan and Cassidy O'Connell**. **The Stardust Engine**. They live right here in Blacksburg on **Progress Street**, and they swim down at the Aquatic Center all the time. Remember the rule of the Huckleberry Trail: out here, they aren’t rock stars. They’re our neighbors. Don't stare, don't pull out a phone, and don't ask for an autograph—just give 'em a neighbor's wave."

Jordan’s heart gave a warm, astonished thump. Here were the creators of *"Electric Color"*, *"My Anchor Holds"*, and *"Safe Person"*—riding a bicycle and pushing a manual wheelchair up a six-mile community bike path with zero bodyguards, zero limousines, and zero walls between them and the town they loved.

As the distance between them closed between the split-rail pasture fences, Ryan O'Connell looked directly across the asphalt at Jordan’s manual wheelchair, noticed Jordan’s maroon CPI hoodie and his gloved hands on his handrims, and broke into a warm, genuine smile.

Jordan smiled back and raised his right hand from his handrim in a quiet, respectful neighbor’s wave.

Ryan tapped two fingers to his temple in a fellow wheelchair user’s salute. "Evening, guys! Beautiful night for a roll!"

"Evening!" Mark nodded warmly with a smile, while Aubrie Jean, Madison, Zoë, Lauren, Hannah, Sarah, Jessica, and Isabel waved back as Cassidy chimed her brass bicycle bell in a cheerful *ring-ring* and the brother and sister rolled smoothly past them toward campus.

Less than a minute later, after Jordan and his friends turned around to head back north toward **Pendleton Library** behind them, the sun dipped low behind **Price Mountain’s crest**—and up ahead against the darkening purple sky, all four massive **Ironstone** floodlight towers of **The Crucible** flickered on in the night, painting the valley in electric light.

Two hundred yards ahead of them under a crimson maple tree, Jordan and Aubrie Jean saw Cassidy pause her bicycle beside Ryan’s wheelchair for a minute, singing something softly into the autumn breeze while tapping her handlebars—before standing up on her pedals and calling back over her shoulder with a laugh that carried down the quiet trail:

***"Race you back to Progress Street!"***

***"You're on, Cass!"***

Listening to the laughter of brother and sister echo down the six-mile path under the glowing stadium towers, Jordan reached up from his left handrim and took Aubrie Jean’s hand. Neither of them had any way of knowing that they had just witnessed the birth of [**"Neon on the Huckleberry Trail"**](https://music.raggiesoft.com/artists/the-stardust-engine/2015-reignition?track=1-08-neon-on-the-huckleberry-trail)—or that nineteen months later inside **The Crucible**, sixty-five thousand **Forgers** would roar that exact song back to the stage as their own.

## The Thanksgiving Exodus & Sanctuary on Geneva Street

### Part 1: Setting the Board & The Maroon Express

**Date:** 2014-11-24 at 21:00 America/New_York

#### November 24, 2014 • 9:00 PM — Setting the Board

By Monday night of Thanksgiving week, the successful Fall Break relay a month earlier already felt like a rehearsal for a far more urgent deadline.

At 1:00 PM on Wednesday, November 26, every residence hall on the campus of Commonwealth Polytechnic Institute would officially close for the four-day Thanksgiving holiday, suspending student keycard access until Sunday afternoon. And according to the ultimatum **Aubrie Sinclair** had sent in October, she intended to pull up outside Bennett Hall at 9:00 AM sharp on Wednesday morning to force Jordan into her sedan and take him back to Virginia Beach.

Sitting in Room 214 on Monday evening with **Aubrie Kelly** and **Zoë** flanking his wheelchair, Jordan knew that simply leaving campus a day early on Tuesday afternoon wasn't a complete strategy.

"Just departing before Wednesday morning isn't enough," Zoë said, her gray eyes steady and analytical as she stood beside Jordan’s desk. "Your mother is manipulative. When she arrives on Wednesday morning and discovers that she cannot get to you, her immediate reflex will be to weaponize university administration or local law enforcement by claiming that a vulnerable, disabled freshman has vanished. We have to control the official record before she has a chance to invent a narrative."

She was right. It wasn't enough to slip away to Christiansburg; they had to build an iron legal wall behind them.

At nine o'clock that night, with Aubrie Jean’s warm hand resting on his shoulder and Zoë reviewing every clause over his other shoulder, Jordan drafted and transmitted a formal notice from his jfuller001 university account:

> **To:** Kelsey Brennan, Hall Director, Bennett Hall; Office of Housing and Residence Life<br>
> **From:** Jordan Fuller<br>
> **Date:** Monday, November 24, 2014 — 21:14 EST<br>
> **Subject:** Thanksgiving Break Plan & No-Contact Notice — Jordan Fuller, Bennett Hall Room 214
>
> Dear Hall Director Brennan and the Office of Housing and Residence Life,
>
> This email is to formally notify you that I, Jordan Fuller, will be departing campus on Tuesday afternoon, November 25, to spend the upcoming Thanksgiving holiday off-campus in Christiansburg with friends and their family. I am completely safe and will be well cared for throughout the break.
>
> I also want to advise you that my mother, Aubrie Sinclair, has stated her intention to arrive at Bennett Hall on Wednesday morning, November 26, under the false assumption that I will be going to Virginia Beach with her. She may refer to me by my legal first name, Aubrey. Please be advised that as a legal adult, I have chosen not to have contact with her. She does not have my permission to enter Bennett Hall, visit my room, or be granted access to any of my student or housing information under FERPA.
>
> Thank you for your continued support and for helping to protect my privacy and safety.
>
> Sincerely,<br>
> Jordan Fuller<br>
> Room 214, Eleanor Bennett Commonwealth Hall

Jordan pressed **Send**, setting the first brick of his Thanksgiving defense firmly into place.

***

#### November 25, 2014 • 9:00 AM — Locking the Record

At nine o'clock the next morning—Tuesday, November 25, just before his final day of pre-break classes—Jordan took the next two steps.

First, accompanied by **Aubrie Jean** and **Zoë**, he took the elevator down to the first floor of Bennett Hall and knocked on the door of **Room 104**—**Kelsey Brennan**’s warm, lamp-lit office, the quiet room beside the front desk that Jordan had long since cataloged in his heart as one of his **Safe Places**.

"Come right on in, Jordan!" Kelsey called out warmly, stepping around her desk to hold the door wide.

Once Jordan rolled up to her oak desk, Kelsey used a small brass key to unlock her top right-hand drawer and pulled out the crisp manila folder she had been safeguarding for him since September.

"I got your email last night, Jordan, and I already logged it into the central Residence Life portal," Kelsey said with a proud, reassuring smile as she laid the **Emergency Contact Change Form** across his lap tray and handed him a blue rollerball pen. "Are we ready to make the change official?"

Jordan nodded firmly, took the pen in his steady fingers, and neatly printed the names, address, and telephone numbers of **Daniel and Laura Brooks** on **Geneva Street in Christiansburg, Virginia** across the primary emergency contact lines—officially striking Aubrie Sinclair from his housing emergency file—before signing **Jordan Fuller** at the bottom.

"Done and time-stamped," Kelsey said, countersigning the form and scanning it directly into the encrypted student life system. "And just so you know, Jordan, we are completely ready for tomorrow morning. Yesterday I sent a mandatory security directive to every resident in Bennett Hall reminding them that propping or holding any exterior door for a non-resident is a strict housing violation. Every exterior door is staying on 24/7 card-access lockdown, and I've arranged for two uniformed **CPI Campus Police** officers to be stationed with me and Henry tomorrow morning. Your mother will not set a single foot inside this building."

Fifteen minutes later, with **Mark** and **Hannah** walking on either side of his wheelchair as his supportive escort, Jordan rolled through the automatic glass doors of **CPI Campus Police Headquarters**.

Stepping up to the front duty desk, Jordan angled the screen of his Pinnacle Vanguard Pro and pressed execute so EchoType spoke clearly and calmly across the lobby:

<aac>Good morning, Officer. My name is Jordan Fuller. I am an eighteen-year-old freshman resident of Bennett Hall, Room 214, and I would like to make a voluntary proactive statement for your records.</aac>

The desk sergeant—a veteran officer with kind eyes and gray at his temples—set down his clipboard and gave Jordan his full, respectful attention. "Go right ahead, Mr. Fuller. I'm listening."

<aac>I am leaving campus this afternoon to spend Thanksgiving Break in Christiansburg with my friends and their parents, Daniel and Laura Brooks, on Geneva Street,</aac> Jordan’s synthesized baritone continued steadily. <aac>However, I have reason to believe that tomorrow morning my mother, Aubrie Sinclair, may attempt to file a false missing-persons report or request a welfare check for me, likely using my legal first name, Aubrey Fuller. I want it officially on record with law enforcement that I am not missing, I am not in danger, and as a legal adult, I have voluntarily chosen not to have contact with her. My official emergency contacts with the university are now Daniel and Laura Brooks at this address and phone number.</aac>

Jordan handed across a neatly printed card containing his student ID number, his VoIP contact number, and Daniel and Laura Brooks’s full address and phone numbers on Geneva Street.

The sergeant read the card carefully and gave a slow, understanding nod. It was far from the first time university police had assisted an adult student protecting himself from an estranged or controlling family member.

"Thank you for coming in ahead of time and doing this the smart way, Jordan," the sergeant said kindly, typing the dispatch advisory directly into his terminal. "I'm entering a flagged proactive welfare note under both **Jordan Fuller** and **Aubrey Fuller** right now, and I'm pushing an interagency CAD bulletin over to the **Blacksburg Police Department**, the **Christiansburg Police Department**, and the **Montgomery County Sheriff's Office**. If she calls any dispatch center in the New River Valley tomorrow claiming you're missing, the dispatcher will see your signed adult statement on their screen before a cruiser ever leaves the lot. You go have yourself a safe, happy Thanksgiving with your friends."

Rolling back out into the crisp November sunshine between Mark and Hannah, Jordan felt an immense weight lift off his chest. He hadn't just run away from Wednesday morning. He had used his voice, his preparation, and his legal rights as an adult to lock every door before his mother even started her engine in Virginia Beach.

***

#### November 25, 2014 • 3:30 PM — The Final Hour

The instant their final Tuesday afternoon lectures wrapped up at three-thirty, all nine members of the pact converged on Suite 214/216 with a single, non-negotiable objective: get Jordan out of CPI and out of Bennett Hall before dusk, a full seventeen hours before his mother was scheduled to arrive on campus.

With all official housing and police notices filed, the mood inside Room 214 shifted from solemn legal preparation to a flurry of joyful, coordinated urgency.

"Okay, people," **Zoë** announced, checking the clock on her mPhone. "Our target departure window to Christiansburg is the four-forty-five bus window from the Commonwealth Mall stops, which gives us fifty-five minutes from right now. **Operation Thanksgiving Pack-Up** is officially a go."

What followed was a masterclass in nine-person teamwork. **Lauren**, **Sarah**, and **Jessica** took charge of gathering toiletries, medications, and travel snacks from both rooms. **Hannah** stood at Jordan’s open wardrobe, holding up warm knit sweaters two at a time for his approval—"Blue or charcoal grey, J?"—and folding each selection neatly into his rolling suitcase at his quick nod.

Without waiting to be asked, **Mark** reached up and effortlessly lifted a heavy crate of astrophysics reference books and star charts down from the top closet shelf that nobody else save Jessica could comfortably reach, setting it gently beside Jordan’s desk. As Mark worked alongside them, he made a quiet point of being completely relaxed, warm, and helpful. Watching Hannah laugh as she tucked a fleece scarf around Jordan’s shoulders, Mark felt nothing except genuine happiness and pride. He knew the "official" cover story about **Aubrie Jean** being Jordan’s girlfriend—and he saw how deeply real that bond had become—but he also understood the deeper truth of their circle: Jordan was family to every single one of them, and Mark had zero room in his heart for the kind of toxic, fragile insecurity that had poisoned Tom Lawson.

Meanwhile, Aubrie Jean and **Madison** ran a methodical two-person verification of Jordan’s essential gear.

"Power brick and charging cable for the Vanguard Pro?" Aubrie asked, holding open his padded backpack.

"Got it—coiled and hook-and-loop-strapped in the center compartment," Madison confirmed, holding up the cord before zipping the pouch. "Spare batteries for his hearing aids and his protective glasses case?"

"Right here in the top felt pocket," Aubrie smiled.

Sitting in the center of the room as the calm director of his own needs, Jordan watched his friends move around him with a quiet, glowing smile. He wasn't being treated like cargo or an obligation; he was being supported by a team—*his* team.

"Alright," Zoë called out at four-fifteen, zipping her own structured weekender bag shut. "We depart for Commonwealth Mall in twenty minutes. Final sweep of both rooms."

***

#### November 25, 2014 • 4:15 PM — One Last Hug

As the others double-checked wall outlets, windows, and bathroom counters inside Suite 214/216, Jordan’s eyes drifted toward the heavy oak door of Room 214.

Before he rolled out of Bennett Hall for the next five days, there was one last thing he needed to do.

He tapped **Aubrie Jean** lightly on the wrist and pointed toward the hallway. Understanding immediately, Aubrie smiled and pressed the interior **PUSH TO OPEN** button for him.

Jordan guided his wheelchair smoothly out into the second-floor corridor and turned toward **Room 215** right across the hall.

The door to Room 215 was propped partway open while **Isabel Dawson** finished zipping a plaid canvas duffel bag on her bed. Once she and Henry finished their early-evening pre-break floor checks, Isabel was heading northeast up I-81 and I-64 to **Charlottesville, Virginia**, to spend Thanksgiving with her parents and her younger sister, **Elana**.

Hearing the soft whir of wheelchair tires on the linoleum, Isabel looked up from her duffel bag—and the moment she saw Jordan sitting at her threshold, her whole face lit up with a radiant smile.

"Hey, Jordan!" Isabel said warmly, walking right over to the doorway. "Are you guys all packed and ready to roll out to Christiansburg?"

Jordan set his wheel brakes, looked up at her with a soft, earnest smile behind his glasses, and opened both arms wide.

"Aww, come here," Isabel murmured, her voice softening with genuine affection.

She stepped out into the hallway, knelt down beside his wheelchair so they were eye-to-eye instead of giving him a quick standing side-hug, and wrapped both arms warmly around his shoulders.

Jordan closed his eyes and hugged her back, resting his cheek briefly against the soft wool of her cardigan.

By now, Isabel meant the absolute world to him. Out of every single staff member, professor, or administrator at Commonwealth Polytechnic Institute, she was unmistakably his favorite CPI staffer. He had never forgotten—and knew he would never forget for as long as he lived—that back on that terrifying Friday afternoon of early move-in day in August, when his mother had dumped him alone in a barren room with a bare mattress, a taped-shut cardboard shipping box, and a dead laptop whose wall outlet he couldn't reach from his wheelchair, Isabel had been the very first person in a position of authority in his entire life who had ever shown him pure, unconditional kindness. Without making him feel broken or pitiful for a single second, she had secured his power strip right onto his desk so he could speak again, cut open his shipping box, made his bed with fresh sheets and blankets, unpacked his clothes into his dresser, and handed him the dignity of his own home.

Holding onto her warm hug in the quiet corridor, Jordan knew every line of the professional Residence Life boundary that had to stand between a Resident Advisor and a freshman resident. And he knew how excited she was to go home to Charlottesville to see her mom, her dad, and Elana.

Yet in the silent, unguarded sanctuary of his own mind, a single truth passed through Jordan’s heart: *if that professional boundary weren't a thing, and if she weren't going home to her family in Charlottesville, he would want Isabel right there on Geneva Street with them for Thanksgiving.*

He knew it could never happen. He respected Isabel, her integrity, and the housing scholarship she worked so hard to keep far too much to ever cross that line—and so he never asked her, and he never even typed a single syllable of that wish onto his keyboard. It stayed strictly an internal thought, tucked safely away in the quietest corner of his heart.

Instead, when they eased back from the hug, Jordan lowered his hands to his Vanguard Pro and typed a message he *could* share:

<aac>Thank you for everything you've done for me this semester, Isabel. Have a wonderful Thanksgiving in Charlottesville with your parents and Elana. I'll see you on Sunday.</aac>

Isabel’s eyes glistened warmly as she read his screen and heard his synthesized voice. She reached out and gave his shoulder one last gentle squeeze.

"Thank you, Jordan," Isabel said softly. "You have the best Thanksgiving ever on Geneva Street with Aubrie, Zoë, and the whole gang. Text **Jordan Comms** when you guys touch down at the Brooks house so I know you made it safely!"

Just then, the elevator doors chimed down the hall, and **Kelsey Brennan** stepped onto the second floor carrying a clipboard alongside **Henry Walsh**, who was walking up from the north stairwell.

"Catching you right before launch!" Henry grinned, walking over and giving Jordan a warm fist bump. "Have an awesome time in Christiansburg, man. Don't eat too much turkey—actually, scratch that, eat all the turkey."

"Have a wonderful, peaceful break, Jordan," Kelsey said, giving him a warm, steady nod as Aubrie, Zoë, Madison, Lauren, Hannah, Mark, Sarah, and Jessica wheeled their suitcases out of Suite 214/216 into the corridor. "Don't worry about a single thing back here tomorrow morning. Henry, campus police, and I have Bennett Hall locked down tight."

Jordan looked at Isabel, Henry, and Kelsey standing together in the corridor—his three guardians of The Old Lady—and gave them a grateful nod before releasing his wheel locks and leading his chosen family—all eight of them—toward the elevator and out into the cool November afternoon.

***

#### November 25, 2014 • 4:35 PM — The Maroon Express

The walk from Bennett Hall across campus to the transit stops along **Commonwealth Mall** outside **Kincaid Hall** was a sight to behold. All nine friends moved as a single, cohesive organism—a bustling caravan of rolling suitcases, overstuffed duffel bags, and cheerful pre-holiday chatter, with Jordan’s wheelchair right at the protected center of their formation.

They reached the crowded sidewalk along **Commonwealth Mall** across the street from **Kincaid Hall** at four-thirty-five. Unlike Christiansburg's sawtooth transfer islands or Radford's numbered stalls at McConnell Transit Center, Commonwealth Mall had **no bus bays at all**—just a long, unmarked stretch of granite curb beneath **The Keystone Bridge** where buses from every transit agency in the valley simply lined up one behind the other in a loud, disorganized free-for-all.

All around them on the brick sidewalk, dozens of CPI students with rolling suitcases and holiday duffels were grumbling under their breath and craning their necks toward the intersection at **Main Street (Business 460)**.

"Man, I cannot wait until they finally build a real transit center on this campus," an upperclassman in a Forgers beanie muttered nearby, shifting his heavy backpack as a sixty-foot **Blue Ridge Transit** articulated bus and a twenty-nine-foot **Radford Transit** bus idled bumper-to-bumper at the head of the curb. "You literally never know which bus is going to turn off Business 460 next or where in the conga line it's gonna stop."

According to the timetable on Zoë's mPhone, the next southbound **Blue Ridge Transit Route 1** local bus down Business 460 was due in about ten minutes. Just as the nine friends were settling in along the sidewalk and watching the Main Street corner like everyone else, however, a completely different vehicle swung wide off **Business 460** onto **Commonwealth Mall** and glided to the curb right behind the departing local buses with a deep, turbocharged diesel purr.

It wasn't a standard low-floor city transit bus. It was a towering over-the-road highway motorcoach, its destination sign above the panoramic windshield cycling cleanly between two displays (CBURG TC standing for Christiansburg Transit Center, and EXP for Express):

<led>MAROON EXPRESS</led>
<led>BLUEWATER EXP via CBURG TC</led>

With a sharp pneumatic hiss, the forward plug door swung outward, and a clear, automated female voice immediately began announcing the coach’s route on the exterior ADA speaker loop:

<pa>Bluewater Transit Maroon Express to Bluewater Transit Center via Christiansburg Transit Center</pa>
