Every clinical, academic, and operational metric in this presentation is 100% real data from the 2014–2015 academic year at CPI. However, to strictly protect the federal **FERPA** privacy and personal safety of the students involved, we have scrubbed all names, room numbers, and identifying biographical markers. Throughout this session, we will refer to this nine-student residential cohort simply as **Pilot Unit Alpha**."

Standing beside the easel, Isabel felt a quiet warmth in her chest. She had promised **Zoë** and **Jordan** in the Bennett Hall lobby that their privacy would be an impenetrable fortress today—and Kelsey had double-checked every slide to make sure no outsider could ever trace Pilot Unit Alpha back to Suite 214/216.

"Let's start with how Pilot Unit Alpha was born," Kelsey said, gesturing toward the screen. "Because I have a confession to make to every Housing Assignments officer in this room: we didn't plan it. In August 2014, CPI experienced a 150% freshman over-enrollment crisis that forced us to convert every two-person room in Bennett Hall into a three-person forced triple and lease three tiers of overflow hotels across Blacksburg, Christiansburg, and Radford. During that crunch, a manual ADA-hold spreadsheet that lacked a gender column collided with our automated room-assignment batch engine. A student with a unisex first name—a non-speaking, non-weight-bearing wheelchair user with cerebral palsy, autism, and bilateral hearing loss—was pinned into the accessible single bed of a two-room connecting suite, and the computer filled the remaining five beds of that suite with five freshman women. Henry?"

On the screen from London, **Henry's** voice came through the speakers crisp and clear, drawing sympathetic laughs from the RAs in the audience.

"I was the RA on rounds on Move-In Saturday when one of the female suitemates pulled me into the room and showed me the door card," Henry said with a self-deprecating grin. "And I won't lie to you—as a junior RA trained on traditional single-gender suite policies, my first instinct was pure panic. I radioed Kelsey thinking we had a five-alarm compliance disaster on our hands. Here was a young man in a wheelchair who had just survived a severe sensory meltdown on Move-In morning, surrounded by five female suitemates he had met three hours earlier."

"And normally," Kelsey picked up, "Central Housing would have relocated those five women within the hour. Except every female bed on campus and in two neighboring towns was at 100% capacity, moving the disabled student out of his designated ADA room would have violated federal law, and—most importantly—when our Director of Housing, our Director of Educational Accessibility, and I sat down inside that room to interview all six students individually without coercion, all six of them looked us in the eye and asked to stay together."

Kelsey stepped back and nodded to **Isabel**.

Stepping up to the second microphone, Isabel looked out over the sea of housing professionals. For a second, she pictured Jordan sitting in Room 214 back in Blacksburg, and her voice steadied with quiet conviction.

"When we talk about **Gender-Inclusive Housing**, most campus policy proposals only frame it around one use case," Isabel said clearly, clicking to the third slide: **WHO NEEDS OPT-IN GENDER-INCLUSIVE HOUSING?** "Supporting LGBTQ+ and gender-nonconforming students is vital, and it is a cornerstone of our proposal. But what Pilot Unit Alpha taught us at CPI is that strict, binary corridor segregation also fails two other huge populations of students who rarely get talked about at housing conferences."

Across the room, dozens of pens started moving across notebooks.

"First," Isabel said, holding up one finger, "are **students who were raised primarily around the opposite gender**—for example, young men who grew up in households with all sisters or female cousins, or who experienced severe trauma around hyper-masculine environments, and who genuinely feel far safer, calmer, and more at home living with female suitemates than in a traditional all-male dorm wing. And second—and this is where Pilot Unit Alpha changed everything for us—are **medically complex, physically disabled, and neurodivergent students whose trusted peer support, daily-living assistance, AAC communication, and note-taking circles naturally cross gender lines**."

Isabel clicked to the next slide, which showed an anonymized diagram of a two-room suite (3 beds + shared accessible jack-and-jill bath + 3 beds) linked to an upstairs buddy network (9 students total).

"On Move-In Friday, when I checked the resident of Bed A into his room," Isabel continued softly, "he arrived at college from a profoundly neglectful home environment with a dead laptop battery, untreated vision and hearing loss, and eighteen years of being conditioned to believe his disabilities made him a burden. In a traditional all-male suite of strangers who didn't understand sensory overload or assistive communication, he would have been isolated inside a week. Instead, within forty-eight hours, the five women in his connecting suite—along with a male engineering resident on the third floor and two female residents on the fifth floor—formed a voluntary, 24/7 peer-support constellation around him."

**Garrett** stepped to the center mic to walk through the operational mechanics.

"As an Industrial and Systems Engineering major who stepped onto Floor 2 this spring when Henry left for London," Garrett said, gesturing to the data charts on Slide 5, "I looked at Pilot Unit Alpha like a systems engineer. How does a nine-person, mixed-gender support network actually function day-to-day inside a 1960s residence hall?
- **Classroom & Campus Redundancy:** Every single class on the disabled resident's schedule is paired with at least one suitemate or suite ally acting as an official OEA note-taker and campus transit buddy.
- **Dignified Division of Care:** When the resident needs assistance in multi-stall public men's restrooms on campus where his female suitemates cannot enter, the third-floor male ally steps in seamlessly. Inside the suite, every transfer, meal run, and sensory-grounding protocol is shared voluntarily with zero burnout.
- **Emergency & Fire-Drill Evacuation Integration:** Because the building is built into a steep campus hillside where the elevators automatically recall and lock out during any fire alarm, the connected suite's buddy system and our Floor 2 Residence Life staff coordinate a zero-step horizontal evacuation straight out the second-floor Washington Street ground-level exit doors—with emergency noise-reducing earmuffs kept on hand inside the suite for sensory-sensitive residents."

"And for the administrators in the room who are wondering what happens to grades, conduct, and building safety when you let freshmen live in a co-ed support suite," **Kelsey** said with a dry, knowing smile as she clicked to Slide 6—**PILOT UNIT ALPHA: TWO-SEMESTER EMPIRICAL OUTCOMES**—let's look at the numbers:

> **PILOT UNIT ALPHA — CUMULATIVE PERFORMANCE METRICS (2014–2015)**
>
> - **Conduct / Noise / Policy Infractions:** 0 (Building Average: 4.2)
> - **Health, Safety & Fire-Drill Compliance:** 100% (Fastest Clear Time)
> - **First-Semester Retention Rate:** 100% (9 of 9 Retained)
> - **Cumulative Cohort GPA (Fall 2014):** 3.94 / 4.00 *(Highest Suite GPA in Bennett Hall; includes two 4.00 Astrophysics GPAs)*

An audible murmur of amazement rippled through the hundred and forty attendees in Room 204. Two housing directors in the front row leaned over to photograph the slide with their tablets.

"A 3.94 cumulative GPA across nine freshmen," Kelsey emphasized, letting the number hang in the air. "Zero conduct incidents. Zero roommate mediation requests. In eighteen years of residence life administration, I have never seen a healthier, higher-performing floor community."

Isabel stepped back to the mic for the closing proposal slide: **THE CPI OPT-IN GENDER-INCLUSIVE HOUSING (GIH) BLUEPRINT (FALL 2015 PILOT → FALL 2016 UNIVERSITY-WIDE ROLLOUT)**.

"Starting in **Fall 2015**, CPI Housing and Residence Life and our Office of Educational Accessibility are launching an official **Opt-In Gender-Inclusive Housing Pilot** in our newer accessible residence halls, with a full university-wide rollout planned for **Fall 2016**," Isabel said. "The rule is simple: **100% Voluntary & Mutual Opt-In, Zero Random Placement**. Every student in a GIH room or suite must actively check the opt-in box on the housing portal and mutually confirm their suitemates."

She paused for a half-breath, her fingers resting lightly on the edge of the podium as she thought of home in Charlottesville.

"For me, this isn't just an abstract policy paper," Isabel added quietly, her voice steady and heartfelt. "My seventeen-year-old younger sister has complex quadriplegia. She is non-speaking, communicates with an AAC tablet via a sip-and-puff straw, drives a heavy-duty power wheelchair, and is partnered with a trained service miniature horse. This fall, she is coming to CPI as a freshman to study Systems Architecture alongside our seventeen-year-old male cousin, who also uses a power wheelchair and has been her primary safe person and overnight muscle-spasm caregiver their entire lives. Under our old binary housing rules, CPI would have forced my sister and her cousin into separate wings on Move-In Day. Because of what **Pilot Unit Alpha** proved on my floor this year, my sister and my cousin will be able to check a box on their housing portal and live together in an accessible suite from Day One—with dignity, safety, and zero red tape."

For a full second after Isabel finished, the room was completely still—and then all one hundred and forty people in Breakout Room 204 erupted into sustained, thunderous applause.

When Kelsey opened the floor for Q&A, hands shot up across every row:
- When an Associate Dean from Tidewater asked how CPI screens against coercion or unbalanced relationships in a mixed-gender suite, **Kelsey** walked them through the **dual-signature Central Housing + OEA intake protocol** (Form HRL-COED-PERM), private individual check-ins, and the no-fault confidential opt-out guarantee.
- When a Residence Director from Piedmont State asked how student RAs handle overnight guest boundaries and privacy in a connected suite, **Henry** (from London) and **Garrett** explained how clear door-card communication and mutual respect actually made Pilot Unit Alpha the easiest suite on the floor to supervise.

By the time the session officially adjourned at three o'clock, twelve different Virginia universities were lined up at the front table asking Kelsey for thumb-drive copies of CPI's policy template and waiver forms.

Stepping out of the conference center into the crisp February afternoon air twenty minutes later with their poster tubes slung over their shoulders, Garrett let out a huge breath of relief as a boxy, heavy-duty **40-foot Stalwart Advantage**—a classic **Stalwart Shoebox** transit bus—pulled up to the shuttle curb with a smooth air-brake kneel instead of the dreaded 35-foot Gamble Aria.

"Oh, thank heaven," Garrett grinned as the bus operator waved them aboard. "A real Stalwart Shoebox! No more bug-eyed fiberglass torture chamber!"

Isabel laughed as she dropped into a window seat behind the front wheel well—and as the bus rolled smoothly back toward the conference hotel, her thoughts drifted straight back down I-81 to the second floor of Bennett Hall, and to the wooden clothespin waiting in her pocket to be painted in Electric Color neon teal and CPI maroon for the boy in **Room 214**.

### Part 3: HEY CACUHO! Clothespins and the Gamble Aria Nightmare

**Date:** 2015-02-15 at 18:30 America/New_York

![Inside Bennett Hall Room 214 after returning from the CACUHO conference, Resident Advisor Isabel Dawson—her woven conference lanyard covered in dozens of brightly painted wooden clothespins—blushes warmly as she kneels beside Jordan's wheelchair to clip a hand-painted neon-teal clothespin onto his laptop bag while Kelsey Brennan, Garrett Reynolds, Aubrie Jean Kelly, and Madison Scott smile fondly behind them.]({{CDN}}/raggiesoft-books/images/scenes/aubrie/e003/c004/p003/hey-cacuho-clothespins-roanoke.jpg)

At six-thirty on Sunday evening, just as the nine residents of **Suite 214/216** were finishing a Sunday study block across the desks and lower bunks of **Room 214**, footsteps and laughter echoed down the second-floor hallway outside their door, followed by a familiar, cheerful two-beat knock.

Jordan's head snapped up toward the door before anyone else's, his whole face lighting up behind his glasses.

**Mark** pulled the door open—and everyone in the room burst out laughing in delight.

Standing in the doorway were **Isabel Dawson**, **Garrett Reynolds**, and **Kelsey Brennan**, fresh off Interstate 81 South from the **CACUHO** conference at **Shenandoah Valley University** in **Harrisonburg**. Around each of their necks hung a wide woven conference lanyard that was almost completely buried under **dozens of brightly painted, glitter-covered, hand-decorated wooden clothespins** clipped edge-to-edge down the fabric.

"What happened to your lanyards?!" **Hannah** giggled, pointing at the rattling armor of wooden clothespins covering Garrett's chest. "Did you guys get attacked by a craft store?!"

"Conference clothespins!" **Garrett** laughed, tapping a neon-orange wooden pin clipped to his collar that read *KEEP CALM & CALL DUTY*. "It's the classic housing conference tradition—every delegation at **CACUHO** brings hundreds of decorated clothespins to trade and secretly clip onto people's badges when they aren't looking!"

"Wait until you hear how the Gender-Neutral Housing session went," **Kelsey** beamed, leaning against the doorframe in her maroon-and-burnt-orange Residence Director polo. "Room 204 only had chairs for eighty people, and by 1:55 PM there were over a hundred and forty RAs, Hall Directors, and Housing Officers standing along the walls and sitting in the aisles—and the chatter was so loud you couldn't even hear the microphone check!"

"So how did you quiet them down?" **Madison** asked.

Garrett grinned, puffed out his chest, cupped both hands around his mouth, and demonstrated at half-volume right there in the doorway:

"**HEY CACUHO!**"

Instantly, **Isabel** and **Kelsey** shouted back in unison:

"**Hey, what?!**"

The entire suite cracked up laughing.

"Worked like magic!" Garrett grinned. "The second a hundred and forty housing people yell *'Hey, what?!'* back at you, the whole room goes dead silent! Henry popped up on the projector screen live from his dorm in London right on cue, Isabel walked the crowd through our anonymized **Pilot Unit Alpha** framework without a single identifying detail leaked, and by the end of the Q&A, twelve different Virginia universities asked for copies of our policy template!"

"Although," **Isabel** added, shaking her head with a wry laugh as she looked at Jordan and Mark, "since we know how much you guys appreciate good transit buses here on Blue Ridge Transit... Shenandoah Valley University's campus shuttle fleet up in Harrisonburg nearly gave us whiplash on Saturday morning."

**Mark** perked up immediately. "Uh-oh. What were they running?"

"The first bus that picked our delegation up from the hotel lot was a **35-foot Gamble Aria**," Garrett groaned, making a face as if he had just bitten into a lemon. "What a complete hunk of garbage! It had that weird, bulbous fiberglass front cap like a squished bug, the transmission jerked on every shift, the steering wandered all over the lane, and the poor campus bus operator looked like he wanted to drive it off a cliff. He literally told us at the red light that the 35-foot Gamble Aria is every bus operator's worst nightmare because of how badly it drives!"

"And the wheelchair ramp on the front door rattled so loudly over every expansion joint that the delegates in the front row had to hold onto their coffee mugs with both hands," Isabel agreed, laughing. "We were all so relieved after our afternoon presentation when a boxy, rock-solid **Stalwart Advantage**—a classic **Stalwart Shoebox** just like the ones Blue Ridge Transit runs on campus—pulled up to the curb instead! Even the driver was grinning from ear to ear."

Jordan laughed, his shoulders shaking as he typed on his Pinnacle keyboard:

<aac>Friends don't let friends ride a 35-foot Gamble Aria when there's a Stalwart Shoebox on the route!</aac>

"Amen to that," Garrett chuckled. "Well, Kelsey and I are going to run these presentation tubes down to the first-floor office, relieve the Westgate crew at the desk, and get unpacked back in Room 201."

Before stepping back across the hall to **Room 215**, Isabel lingered in the doorway of Room 214 for a moment. Reaching up to her conference lanyard, she unclipped one special wooden clothespin she had kept tucked right near her collarbone and held it out to Jordan.

Unlike the quick marker-scribbled pins traded in the hallways, this clothespin had been carefully hand-painted in shimmering **Electric Color neon teal and CPI maroon**, with tiny silver stars along the edges and neat white lettering down the wood: **SUITE 214 — CAPTAIN OF THE HILL**.

"I painted this one at the spirit table while I was thinking about our presentation," Isabel said softly, a warm flush coloring her fair cheeks behind her rectangular glasses as she knelt slightly to clip it neatly onto the side pocket of Jordan's laptop bag. "Because without you, Jordan... none of what we shared this weekend would exist. And I have to admit—even at a great conference, it felt strange not being across the hall."

Across the room, **Aubrie Jean** and **Madison** exchanged the quietest, fondest glance, while Jordan felt his heart give a warm, steady thump against his ribs. Looking straight into Isabel's dark brown eyes—knowing now what lived in his own heart, and honoring every inch of the professional Residence Life polo she wore—Jordan smiled and tapped his screen:

<aac>Thank you, Isabel. I'm keeping this right on my bag all semester. And it felt really strange here without you, Garrett, and Kelsey too. We're all really glad you're back across the hall in 215.</aac>

Isabel's smile softened into something luminous. She gave his shoulder a gentle, lingering squeeze, stepped out into the second-floor corridor, wiped the At the CACUHO Conference! note off her hanging whiteboard, and unlocked the door of **Room 215**.

Ten seconds later, as Jordan glanced toward the bottom of their door, the familiar ribbon of warm yellow floor-lamp light was glowing underneath the threshold of Room 215 once again—and for the first time all weekend, the second floor of Bennett Hall felt completely whole.

## The Stalker at the Desk & The Bluewater Bunker

### Part 1: The Investigator at the Front Desk & Convoy to Bluewater

**Date:** 2015-03-02 at 14:45 America/New_York

#### March 2, 2015 • 2:45 PM — The Investigator at the Front Desk

The first Monday of March arrived with crisp mountain sunshine across **Commonwealth Green**, five days before the start of CPI's ten-day **Spring Break**.

At two-forty-five that afternoon, as **Jordan**, **Aubrie Jean**, **Madison**, **Zoë**, **Lauren**, **Hannah**, **Mark**, **Sarah**, and **Jessica** walked and rolled across the lower residential quad from **Kepler Hall** toward the **first-floor inner quad entrance** of **Bennett Hall**, Jordan's phone chimed with an urgent campus email alert from Hall Director **Kelsey Brennan**:

> **From:** Kelsey Brennan, Residence Director (Eleanor Bennett Commonwealth Hall)<br>
> **To:** Jordan Fuller, Mark Anderson, Zoë Brooks<br>
> **Date:** Monday, March 2, 2015 — 14:45 EST<br>
> **Subject:** URGENT — Come to 1st-Floor Office via Inner Quad Doors (Room 104)
>
> *Hey guys — come straight in through the first-floor inner quad doors and step directly into my private office (Room 104). Do **not** walk up the hill toward the second-floor Washington Street SW entrance right now. Our fourth-floor RAs just intercepted a man claiming to be a private investigator from Virginia Beach who tried to tailgate behind a resident at the entrance door, and CPI Campus Police are escorting him up to his rental car on Washington Street SW.*

Around Jordan's wheelchair, the eight members of his family immediately locked into Dr. Gable's Roman *testudo* formation—**Mark** stepping to his right flank, **Lauren** and **Madison** to his left, **Aubrie Jean** resting her hand on his shoulder, and **Zoë** already activating **`[Jordan Comms]`** on her phone to alert **Daniel and Laura Brooks** as Jordan tapped his **Poly Pass** against the exterior reader to unlock the **first-floor inner quad doors** and rolled straight across the lobby into Kelsey's office.

Inside the private Hall Director's office (Room 104) behind the front desk, **Kelsey Brennan** had closed the horizontal Venetian blinds to the main lobby. Standing beside her desk were fourth-floor Female RA **Brianna Foster** (`Room 415`) and fourth-floor Male RA **Aaron Vance** (`Room 401`)—along with second-floor RAs **Isabel Dawson** and **Garrett Reynolds**—all wearing their two-tone Chicago Maroon CPI Residence Life athletic polo shirts tucked into belted khaki pants and visibly bristling with protective adrenaline.

"Everybody's safe, Jordan—he never laid eyes on you, and he never set a single foot inside Bennett Hall," Kelsey said immediately as Jordan wheeled inside.

"What happened, Kelsey?" Mark asked, closing the solid oak office door behind the group.

"Twenty minutes ago, one of our fourth-floor female residents was walking up the pathway toward the Bennett Hall entrance carrying two bags of groceries," **Brianna Foster**, the fourth-floor female RA, explained clearly to Jordan and his found family. "She noticed a stranger in a tan trench coat with a DSLR camera bag slung over his shoulder walking uncomfortably close behind her heels—trying to position himself to tailgate right through the door the moment she unlocked it. Instead of tapping her Poly Pass and letting him force his way inside behind her, she slowed down on the approach and looked deliberately through the lobby window toward the front desk, trying to catch the eye of whoever was on duty to wordlessly communicate that someone behind her was trying to force entry."

"Aaron was on duty at the front desk," **Kelsey** continued, gesturing toward the fourth-floor male RA, "and he immediately recognized her as one of his and Brianna's fourth-floor female residents—and read the warning look in her eyes through the glass right away."

"Before I even stepped out from behind the counter, I discreetly hit the silent under-desk panic button—which instantly summoned Kelsey from Room 104 and sent a priority dispatch alert to **CPI Campus Police**," **Aaron** said, folding his arms across his chest. "Brianna and I went straight to the entrance door, got our fourth-floor resident and her groceries safely inside, and I stepped into the threshold to block the door and asked the guy outside on the walkway if I could be of any assistance."

Jordan felt a cold jolt in the pit of his stomach, even as his hands on his wheel rims stayed steady. Beside him, Aubrie Jean squeezed his shoulder firmly.

"He tried to bluff his way past the door," **Brianna** said fiercely. "Standing outside the entrance, he flashed a Tidewater private investigator's license, claimed he had been retained by **Aubrie Sinclair** down in Virginia Beach, and demanded to know whether *'Aubrey Jordan Fuller'* lived in Bennett Hall and what time he left the building for classes. Aaron and Kelsey didn't budge an inch—they cited CPI's **FERPA Directory Hold Policy** and our **No-Tailgating Residence Hall Security Policy**, and told him flatly that Housing & Residence Life will **neither confirm nor deny** that there is a student named Aubrey Jordan Fuller enrolled at the university or residing in this building."

"Because Aaron hit the silent panic button the second he saw our resident being tailed, **CPI Campus Police** were at the door outside of Bennett Hall in ninety seconds," **Kelsey** added, holding up a yellow campus police incident copy. "Officer Jennings intercepted him right there outside the door before he ever crossed the threshold, served him with a permanent criminal trespass bar from all Commonwealth Polytechnic Institute property, and escorted him back up to his tan rental sedan on **Washington Street SW**. However, before Officer Jennings walked him away from the door, the man muttered that he's booked at a motel down on Route 460 for the rest of the week and plans to stake out the town intersections and bus stops off-campus before Spring Break starts on Friday."

Listening to Kelsey, Brianna, and Aaron's report, the pieces clicked together in Jordan's mind with crystal clarity.

Opening his **Pinnacle Vanguard Pro** laptop on his lap tray, Jordan typed steadily:

<aac>My mother's tax return bounced. When she tried to e-file her 2014 taxes at the end of February and claim my Social Security number as a dependent, the IRS computer rejected her return because of Operation File First. And when she called the insurance company and found out I wasn't on her policy anymore, she realized she had lost control—so she hired a private investigator to stalk me and find out where I'm going for Spring Break.</aac>

"And if she paid a PI to drive seven hours from Virginia Beach to Blacksburg, she's hoping he can track you down off-campus or follow us home to Christiansburg," **Zoë** said, looking up from the encrypted **`[Jordan Comms]`** thread on her phone with a calm, focused nod. "I just activated **Jordan Comms** and briefed Dad and Mom on the priority channel. They're convening a War Council at our house on Geneva Street in Christiansburg at five o'clock, and as soon as Campus Police confirm Washington Street SW is clear, Dad and Caleb are pulling right up to the second-floor Washington Street SW entrance to pick us up."

Looking up at **Kelsey**, **Brianna**, **Aaron**, **Isabel**, and **Garrett**, Jordan tapped his AAC screen with deep gratitude:

<aac>Thank you, all of you—and please thank your fourth-floor resident for us too. Because she caught Aaron's eye through the window and you stopped him at the door, he never even made it into the lobby.</aac>

"Not in our building," Aaron said firmly. "Not ever."

And beside the door, Brianna, Garrett, and Isabel gave Jordan a fierce, unified nod—their hands resting near the embroidered **CPI HOUSING & RESIDENCE LIFE** crests on the left chest of their maroon polo shirts, guarding his sanctuary with everything they had.

***

#### March 2, 2015 • 5:15 PM — The War Council and The Hotel at Poly

By five-fifteen that Monday evening—after **Daniel** and **Caleb** had picked up the nine students outside the second-floor **Washington Street SW** entrance of Bennett Hall in Blacksburg and driven them fifteen minutes down Route 460 to the Brooks family residence at **414 Geneva Street** in **Christiansburg**—the dining room had been transformed into a tactical command center.

Seated at the head of the oak table were **Daniel** and **Laura Brooks**, surrounded by all nine members of Suite 214/216 along with **Caleb** and nineteen-year-old **Owen Brooks**.

"First," Daniel said calmly, looking directly at **Jordan** with steady, unshakeable reassurance, "take a deep breath, son. Because of the FERPA Directory Hold that you and Ms. Higgins put in place back in the fall, and because that sharp-eyed fourth-floor resident caught Aaron Vance's eye through the lobby window so Aaron, Brianna, and Kelsey could intercept the man outside the door in less than ninety seconds, Aubrie Sinclair's private investigator never even set foot inside Bennett Hall—and walked away from campus today with zero photographs, zero room numbers, and a permanent criminal trespass bar from CPI Campus Police."

Jordan let out a slow breath, his shoulders easing slightly as **Aubrie Jean** and **Madison** held his hands on either side of his wheelchair.

"What we know right now," **Laura** continued gently, "is that your mother is furious because her 2014 tax return was rejected by the IRS after you filed your own taxes in January, and because she can no longer track you through her health insurance or cell-phone bill. She hired this Tidewater private investigator to figure out where you're living, who you're with, and where you go when CPI lets out for breaks—probably hoping she can either confront you off-campus or find an angle to harass us."

"Wait—what about that investigator lurking around Blacksburg and Route 460 *this* week?" **Aubrie Jean** asked protectively, her hand tightening around Jordan's. "We still have four days of classes before Spring Break starts on Friday afternoon, and we don't want that creep tailing the Blue Ridge Transit buses or staking out the edges of campus waiting for Jordan!"

"And he won't get the chance," **Daniel** said, his calm London accent turning steel-hard. "Because until Spring Break starts on Friday afternoon, Jordan is not going to be at Bennett Hall—and he isn't going to be commuting up and down Route 460 where a private investigator can follow our license plates. Neither is Aubrie Jean or Madison."

Daniel slid three white electronic hotel keycards across the oak table.

"Twenty minutes ago," Daniel said, "we booked an accessible, ground-floor executive suite at **The Hotel at Poly**—the university conference hotel right across the street from the upper quad. And so that no private investigator running a credit-card header or hotel registry search for *Fuller*, *Kelly*, *Scott*, or *Daniel Brooks* can ever trace the room, the reservation is booked and checked in strictly under **nineteen-year-old Owen Brooks's** name."

From the kitchen doorway, **Owen** grinned and held up the hotel check-in folio, while **Caleb** stood beside him with two empty suitcases.

"Caleb and I are driving back up to Bennett Hall tonight with Mark and Lauren to pack five days' worth of clothes, toiletries, and textbooks for Jordan, Aubrie Jean, and Madison," Owen said proudly. "We'll bring them straight through the side courtyard entrance of The Hotel at Poly so the three of you don't even have to step foot near the public lobby."

Jordan looked from Owen and Caleb to Daniel, and then typed on his tablet:

<aac>Wait—what about our classes this week? PHYS 102, ASTR 204, HIST 115, GEOL 101, and MATH 112?</aac>

"Already handled, Jordan," Laura smiled, gesturing toward her phone. "With your permission, we called **Ms. Patricia Higgins** at the **Office of Educational Accessibility (Callahan Hall)**, who immediately notified **Dr. Alistair**, **Dr. Marcus Gable**, **Mr. Evans**, and **Dr. Petrova** that a stalker hired by your estranged mother was trespassed from Bennett Hall today."

Just then, Jordan's laptop chimed with two incoming campus emails—one from **Dr. Alistair** and one from **Dr. Marcus Gable**:

> **From:** Dr. Alistair (Department of Physics & Astronomy, CPI)<br>
> **To:** Jordan Fuller, Aubrie Jean Kelly<br>
> **Subject:** Pre-Spring Break Remote Lab & Lecture Clearance
>
> *Mr. Fuller and Ms. Kelly — Ms. Higgins at OEA informed me that you require a secure off-site study location prior to Friday's Spring Break departure. Consider yourselves 100% excused from in-person attendance for the remainder of the week. Ms. Brooks is authorized to stream the lectures to your terminal, and my door in Kepler Hall is always on your side.*

> **From:** Dr. Marcus Gable (Department of History, CPI)<br>
> **To:** Jordan Fuller, Aubrie Jean Kelly, Madison Scott<br>
> **Subject:** HIST 115 — Holding the Testudo
>
> *Keep your shields locked and stay safe this week. Zoë and Mark will record Tuesday and Thursday's lectures on the Roman Republic for you. See you all after Spring Break.*

***

#### March 2, 2015 • 6:30 PM — Checked In at The Hotel at Poly

An hour later, inside the quiet, plushly carpeted ground-floor accessible suite of **The Hotel at Poly**—with the curtains drawn, room-service dinner trays set out on the table by **Owen** and **Caleb**, and **Aubrie Jean** and **Madison** curled warmly on either side of him on the king-sized hotel bed—Jordan looked around their temporary fortress.

His mother had sent a stalker across the state to hunt him down. Instead, his professors, his RAs, his brothers, and his Constellation had moved like a single unbreakable shield wall before the investigator could even get past the front desk.

***

#### March 7, 2015 • 9:15 AM — Sanctuary Compromised (The Rubber Duck Convoy to Bluewater)

At nine-fifteen on Saturday morning, March seventh—the official start of Commonwealth Polytechnic Institute's ten-day **Spring Break**—**Jordan**, **Aubrie Jean**, and **Madison** were packing their overnight bags inside the ground-floor suite of **The Hotel at Poly** while **Mark**, **Lauren**, **Zoë**, **Hannah**, **Sarah**, and **Jessica** loaded the vehicles in the sheltered side courtyard.

Suddenly, **Mark’s** phone buzzed with a text from sixteen-year-old **Owen Brooks**, who was running a perimeter check down in Christiansburg with **Daniel** and **Caleb**:

> **From:** Owen Brooks<br>
> **To:** Mark Anderson, Zoë Brooks<br>
> **Time:** 9:18 AM
>
> *Heads up — Dad, Caleb, and I just spotted that tan rental sedan with Tidewater plates parked across North Franklin Street near Strickland Farms, watching the turnoff toward Geneva Street. The PI knows CPI just let out for Spring Break and he's waiting to see if you guys bring Jordan back to the Christiansburg house today.*

Inside the hotel suite, **Madison** didn't hesitate for a single second. Back in January, on the night her mother had called in tears to tell her that fourteen-year-old **Bob**—Madison's beloved **"squirt"**—had been assaulted and stuffed into his locker at Bluewater High, permanently damaging his leg, Madison had promised her little brother and her fifteen-year-old cousin **Emily** that she would come home for Spring Break in March. Now, she held up her phone, where she had just finished a call with her parents.

"He can sit in that parking lot all week staring at an empty driveway," Madison said firmly, her bright blue eyes flashing with protective resolve. "I just got off the phone with my Mom and Dad—**David and Diane Scott**—down in **Bluewater**. I already promised **Bob** and **Emily** back in January that I was coming home for Spring Break, and Mom says the **Bluewater Bunker** is open and waiting for all of us—including Daniel, Laura, Caleb, and Owen."

Jordan looked up at Madison from his wheelchair and tapped his **Pinnacle Vanguard Pro** screen:

<aac>Are your parents sure they don't mind all of us descending on their house for Spring Break on ten minutes' notice? Especially with everything Bob has been recovering from since January?</aac>

"Mind?!" Madison smiled warmly, blinking back a sudden shimmer of emotion as she leaned down to kiss the top of Jordan's head. "Jordan, ever since that phone call in January, I've been counting the days until I could get home to hug my squirt and Em in person. Since Bob has been in a wheelchair since the assault, Mom and Dad already built a ramp up the front porch steps. And Mom says having you there—someone who already knows how to live and thrive on wheels—is the best medicine my little brother could possibly ask for."

"And because the Scott residence is ninety minutes southwest in rural **Bluewater** under David and Diane Scott," **Zoë** added with a crisp, approving nod as she closed her laptop, "there is zero public-record link between Aubrie Sinclair's investigator and Madison's family. Dad, Mum, Caleb, and Owen are already pulling out via the back streets of Christiansburg to rendezvous with us at the Interstate 81 ramp. If we depart directly from the west courtyard exit of The Hotel at Poly, we vanish completely off his grid."

Within ten minutes, the **Rubber Duck Convoy** rolled quietly out into the bright March morning and linked up on the highway.

Following **Mark’s** lead, the four vehicles—Daniel and Laura's van, Caleb and Owen's car, Mark's SUV with Hannah, Sarah, and Jessica, and Lauren's car with Zoë riding shotgun and **Jordan** buckled securely in the back seat between **Aubrie Jean** and **Madison**—moved as a single unit down Interstate 81 South and Interstate 77 into Carroll County, maintaining a tight, defensive formation that never let a single unknown vehicle slip between them.

As the convoy climbed into the deep, pine-covered ridges of Southwest Virginia toward Bluewater—leaving the Virginia Beach investigator sitting empty-handed in a Christiansburg parking lot—Jordan leaned his head back against Aubrie Jean’s shoulder, held Madison’s hand across his lap, and got ready to keep the promise he had made to her in January: to show her little squirt that life on wheels wasn't the end of the road.

### Part 2: Making It Work in Bluewater & The Heart-Hum

**Date:** 2015-03-07 at 11:15 America/New_York

#### March 7, 2015 • 11:15 AM — Making It Work in Bluewater

Ninety minutes later, the four-car convoy turned onto a quiet, tree-lined residential street in **Bluewater, Virginia**, and pulled into the driveway of **David and Diane Scott's** home: a warm, lived-in two-story house with white clapboard siding, dark green shutters, and a newly built wooden ramp rising gently beside the front porch steps.

Before the engines had even shut off, the front door swung open.

**Diane and David Scott** stepped out onto the porch with open arms. Just behind them in the wide doorway stood **fifteen-year-old Emily Jenkins** and **fourteen-year-old Bob Scott**.

Even from the driveway, the change since Christmas took everyone’s breath away. **Emily**—who had stood five-foot-three in December—was in the middle of a massive adolescent growth spurt and had shot up to a staggering **five-foot-ten**, standing like a quiet, immovable tower in the doorway. And right beside her, looking up with wide dark eyes, four-foot-eight **Bob** sat in a **wheelchair**.

For **Madison**, seeing her little brother—her beloved **"squirt"**—in a wheelchair for the first time in person was a gut punch. Knowing about the January locker assault from a speakerphone call in Bennett Hall was one thing; seeing her baby brother sitting in that frame was another.

Her breath caught in her throat. The next second, Madison was out of Lauren’s car and sprinting up the wooden porch ramp, dropping to her knees in front of Bob’s chair to wrap both her little brother and her cousin in a fierce, tearful embrace.

"Hey, squirt," Madison whispered thickly into Bob’s hair, holding him with everything she had.

Bob let out a warm, comforted grunt in the **Heart-Hum**, leaning his cheek into his big sister’s shoulder, while five-foot-ten Emily wrapped her long arms around both of them and answered with a soft, welcoming trill of chirps.

Once Mark and Caleb had unfolded Jordan’s manual chair and Jordan rolled smoothly up the front ramp into the house, Madison’s heart ached all over again as she witnessed the reality of Bob’s daily struggle.

Inside the living room, Bob wanted to move from his wheelchair onto his usual spot on the long sofa against the wall. With a stubborn, frustrated grunt, he waved off his father’s offered hands and let out a sequence of low, effortful notes in the **Heart-Hum**—a phrase **Madison** and **Diane** understood effortlessly: *Let me just get to the sofa.*

Gripping a metal walker positioned beside his wheelchair, fourteen-year-old Bob hauled himself upright. His thin arms trembled violently with the strain as he dragged his injured leg through a few slow, agonizingly stiff shuffling steps across the two-foot gap before collapsing onto the sofa cushions, pale and breathless. Instantly, **Emily** was in motion—Her expression a mask of fierce concentration as she wheeled his chair out of the way, stacked a mountain of pillows beneath his legs, and placed their shared **mPad** within reach of his hand, keeping the promise she had made over the speakerphone in January.

Standing by the hallway arch, Madison had to bite her lower lip to keep from crying. Her squirt’s entire world had shrunk to the two feet between that wheelchair and that sofa, and Emily had made herself its tireless guardian.

The rest of the afternoon became a masterclass in **making it work**.

While the front porch now had a ramp for Bob’s chair, the Scotts’ older two-story home wasn't built for Jordan’s complete non-weight-bearing needs. Only one bedroom—Madison’s old childhood room—was on the ground floor, while the rest of the bedrooms were upstairs, and the only downstairs restroom was a small half-bath off the hallway whose narrow twenty-four-inch doorway was four inches too tight for Jordan’s wheelchair wheels.

Nobody treated the layout as a problem for even five seconds.

While **Daniel**, **Laura**, **Caleb**, and **Owen** carried their bags up to the second-floor guest rooms, the nine CPI students transformed Madison’s first-floor bedroom into a wall-to-wall sleepover fortress—pushing the twin bed into the corner and covering every square inch of floor space with plush air mattresses, sleeping bags, and Diane’s hand-stitched quilts.

And when Jordan needed to use the narrow downstairs half-bath an hour later, the family executed what Mark cheerfully dubbed **"Operation Potty Break"** with the precision of a pit crew: **Caleb**, **Owen**, and **Mark** rolled Jordan right up to the bathroom threshold, carefully lifted him from his seat frame on a quiet three-count, and pivoted him through the narrow doorway straight into the waiting arms of **Lauren** and **Aubrie Jean** inside—turning an architectural barrier into a seamless act of love and teamwork.

That evening after dinner, **Daniel Brooks** sat down at the dining room table with **David and Diane** to brief them on the Tidewater private investigator who had tried to tailgate into Bennett Hall on Monday and staked out Christiansburg that morning. Because the investigator was hunting for predictable patterns, David and Diane immediately decided that Bob and Emily would stay home from **Bluewater High School** for the week, turning the house into a true **Bluewater Bunker**.

Out in the living room, a quiet, profound bond began to form between **Jordan**, **Bob**, and **Emily**.

Because none of the three spoke aloud with their vocal cords, the living room became a sanctuary of effortless non-verbal understanding—a rhythmic symphony of Bob and Emily’s **Heart-Hum** (which Madison translated with gentle fluency whenever a nuance was new to Jordan) and rapid-fire messages typed across Jordan’s **Pinnacle Vanguard Pro** and Bob and Emily’s shared **mPad**, while five-foot-ten Emily moved back and forth to the kitchen like a devoted sentinel, bringing mugs of hot cocoa and plates of cookies for the two boys in wheelchairs.

***

#### March 11, 2015 • 2:30 PM — Lessons from a Fellow Traveler and the Heart-Hum

On Wednesday afternoon of Spring Break, while **Jordan** was parked near the living-room armchair reviewing astrophysics notes on his **Pinnacle Vanguard Pro** with **Madison** and **Aubrie Jean** sitting nearby, fourteen-year-old **Bob** decided it was time to move from the sofa back into his wheelchair.

Jordan paused his typing and watched closely as Madison’s little brother reached for the metal walker beside the cushions.

Even from six feet away, Jordan could see why every transfer was leaving the fourteen-year-old boy exhausted. Nobody at the hospital after the January assault had taught Bob how a wheelchair user actually moves across a corner gap; instead, they had handed him a walker and told him to stand up. Bob was trying to haul his entire body weight straight up into the air with his trembling arms while awkwardly maneuvering his injured leg around the four legs of the walker. Halfway up, his foot caught on the rug and his balance wobbled dangerously—sending five-foot-ten **Emily** lunging to his side with a flurry of worried, high-pitched chirps in the **Heart-Hum** to steady his waist until he finally dropped heavily into his wheelchair seat.

Bob slumped back against the canvas backrest, pale, winded, and letting out a low, defeated grunt of pure frustration.

Remembering the promise he had typed to Madison in **Room 214** on the night of the January phone call—*I will teach him every trick I know*—**Jordan** unlocked his brakes and wheeled quietly across the carpet until he was right in front of Bob and Emily.

Switching on **`EchoType`** so his `"Sydney"` voice could speak directly to the two cousins, Jordan tapped his keys:

<aac>Hey, Bob. Can I show you a trick? Something I learned a long time ago.</aac>

Bob looked up from his lap, his dark eyes widening with curiosity, and gave a single, affirmative grunt. Beside him, Emily rested a protective hand on Bob’s shoulder and watched Jordan intently.

Jordan wheeled his manual chair over to the empty edge of the sofa and turned back toward Bob.

<aac>You are working way too hard,</aac> Jordan’s laptop said gently. <aac>You are trying to lift all of your body weight straight up into the air at once, and the walker is actually getting in your way. Watch the angle of my wheels.</aac>

Unlocking his brakes, Jordan rolled forward an inch and back half an inch to swing his small front caster wheels forward for maximum stability, and then parked his wheelchair at a tight **forty-five-degree angle** against the edge of the sofa cushion—so the front right corner of his seat frame snuggled less than two inches from the couch.

<aac>This is called the Forty-Five-Degree Transfer,</aac> Jordan explained. <aac>First, angle your chair at forty-five degrees to the sofa and lock both brakes tight. Look at the gap between my seat and the cushion now—it is barely two inches wide.</aac>

Bob leaned forward in his chair, his eyes locking onto the tiny corner gap.

<aac>Second, leave the walker aside,</aac> Jordan continued. <aac>Place one hand firmly on your wheelchair frame and your other hand on the sofa cushion. Tuck your elbows in, lean your head and chest forward over your knees, and use your momentum to pivot your hips across the corner like a hinge. Watch.</aac>

In one smooth, practiced motion—born of eighteen years of living in a manual chair with zero weight-bearing in his legs—Jordan placed one hand on his armrest and one on the sofa, leaned his head and shoulders forward, and pivoted his hips cleanly from his wheelchair onto the sofa cushion. Pausing a beat, he reversed his hands, leaned forward again, and pivoted smoothly right back into his wheelchair seat without a single wasted ounce of effort.

<aac>See? It is all about angles and leverage,</aac> Jordan said warmly. <aac>You do not lift straight up—you pivot across the corner. It saves your arms, it protects your bad leg, and it is much safer. You do not even need the walker for a transfer like that.</aac>

For three full seconds, Bob and Emily stared at Jordan in stunned silence.

To Jordan, it was basic everyday geometry. To a fourteen-year-old boy who had only been in a wheelchair for seven weeks—and to the fifteen-year-old cousin who had been pouring her whole heart into keeping him safe—it was a revelation.

Bob looked from Jordan to his own wheelchair, then over at the sofa. He let out a low, rising sound of pure awe in the **Heart-Hum**, lifting his hands to mimic Jordan’s pivoting motion in the air.

Beside him, **Emily’s** eyes were shining. Picking up their shared **mPad** from the end table, she typed furiously on the glass screen and turned it toward Jordan:

<aac>Thank you. They don't teach that at the hospital.</aac>

<aac>Want to try it right now, Bob?</aac> Jordan asked, rolling back a foot to give him room. <aac>Emily and I will spot you right here.</aac>

Bob nodded eagerly. Moving the metal walker out of the way, he rolled his wheelchair up to the sofa at the exact **forty-five-degree angle** Jordan had demonstrated, locked both brakes with a sharp *clack*, placed one hand on his armrest and one on the cushion, leaned his head forward over his knees, and pivoted his hips across the two-inch corner.

In less than two seconds, Bob was sitting securely on the sofa cushion—without his arms trembling, without his injured leg dragging, and without breaking a sweat.

Bob froze on the cushion, blinked down at his legs, and let out an exuberant, triumphant chirp that made **Aubrie Jean** burst into applause from the armchair.

For the first time in his nineteen years, Jordan wasn't the fragile boy being sheltered, rescued, or cared for by others. He was the **teacher**—the veteran mentor passing down the hard-won craft of his world to its newest traveler.

Then Bob and Emily looked at Jordan—and turned to face each other.

Right there in the middle of the quiet living room, the two cousins held a rapid, silent conference in the **Heart-Hum**: a questioning, melodic chirp from Emily; a deep, confirming hum from Bob; and a soft, simultaneous click of complete agreement from both of them.

Turning back to Jordan in unison, Bob and Emily looked straight into his eyes and produced a brand-new sound together:

**A sharp, soft click—like a key turning cleanly in a lock—followed immediately by a warm, resonant, appreciative hum.**

Across the room, **Madison** gasped aloud, both hands flying to her mouth as tears welled up in her bright blue eyes.

Jordan blinked in surprise, looking from the two beaming cousins over to Madison, and tapped a quick question on his keyboard:

<aac>Madi, what did they just say?</aac>

Rising from the floor, Madison walked over, dropped to her knees beside Jordan’s wheelchair, and wiped a tear from her freckled cheek. Because she had grown up speaking and understanding her brother and cousin’s non-verbal language her entire life, she knew the sacred weight of what had just happened.

"Jordan... do you understand what they just did?" Madison whispered, her voice thick with emotion. "They... they just gave you a name. In the **Heart-Hum**."

She looked over at her beloved squirt on the sofa and her towering fifteen-year-old cousin standing beside him, her heart overflowing with pride, before looking back into Jordan’s green eyes.

"They don't just give those out, Jordan," Madison said softly. "You have to earn a name in the Heart-Hum, and it has to be a decision they both make together. That click and hum they just made for you—it means ***The Key***. *The one who unlocks the way.*"

Madison reached out and squeezed Jordan’s hand through her tears.

"It means you're one of us now, Jordan," she whispered. "It means you're family. To both of them."

## The S.S. Freedom & Closing the Old Lady

### Part 1: Three Hundred and Fifty Pounds of Freedom & Stripping Room 214

**Date:** 2015-03-16 at 13:30 America/New_York

![Beaming with triumphant confidence, nineteen-year-old Jordan Fuller drives his brand-new 350-pound matte-black Vanguard Titan-X350 all-terrain power wheelchair (S.S. Freedom, with six suspension wheels, glowing white LED fender path-lights, and his laptop mounted on a swing-away arm) effortlessly up the steep twelve-degree paved hillside walkway alongside the gray Ironstone facade of Eleanor Bennett Hall while Aubrie Jean Kelly, Madison Grace Miller, and Zoë Wren Brooks walk beside him and Resident Advisors Isabel Dawson and Garrett Reynolds cheer from the top of the ridge.]({{CDN}}/raggiesoft-books/images/scenes/aubrie/e003/c010/s001/ss-freedom-hill-climb.jpg)

#### March 16, 2015 • 1:30 PM — Three Hundred and Fifty Pounds of Freedom

On Monday afternoon, March sixteenth—as the nine students returned from a peaceful, laughter-filled Spring Break in Bluewater to learn from **Daniel Brooks** that Aubrie Sinclair's private investigator had checked out of his Route 460 motel and gone back to Tidewater empty-handed—the hydraulic lift-gate on the back of the **Blue Ridge Complex Rehab & Mobility** sprinter van hummed down onto the concrete apron of the Brooks driveway at **414 Geneva Street**.

**Marcus Vance** backed the flagship machine out into the March sunlight, while his assistant wheeled out Jordan's matching fourteen-pound **`Vanguard AeroLite-Ti`** custom brushed-titanium folding manual chair for tight indoor spaces and car trunks.

Even knowing the specifications he had personally picked out and signed for in January—and knowing that **Daniel Brooks** had paid for both custom machines in cash out-of-pocket so Jordan would never have to spend another day in the clunky, ill-fitting manual hospital wheelchair his mother had sent him to CPI with—seeing his custom **Vanguard Titan-X350** in person took Jordan's breath away.

Three hundred and fifty pounds of matte-black, aircraft-grade aluminum and steel sat planted on six independent suspension wheels. The high-backed contoured biomechanical seat was upholstered in breathable charcoal ballistic mesh over the custom fluid-cell memory cushion. Mounted on the swing-away right armrest sat the sleek proportional R-Net color LCD joystick module, alongside the ruggedized articulating bracket for his **Pinnacle Vanguard Pro** workstation, integrated amber-and-white LED path-lights tucked into the front matte-black fenders, and a heavy-duty backpack rack welded seamlessly behind the headrest.

"Here she is, Mr. Fuller," Marcus said proudly, locking the electromagnetic parking brakes with a solid *click* and flipping up the left armrest flush against the backrest. "Custom-built and calibrated to your exact seating geometry, right alongside your fourteen-pound *AeroLite-Ti* titanium manual chair. Want to transfer out of that old hospital chair for the very last time?"

Jordan grinned. Rolling the old manual chair forward an inch and back half an inch to trail the front casters, he parked at a crisp **forty-five-degree angle**—the exact **Forty-Five-Degree Transfer** he had just taught Madison's fourteen-year-old brother **Bob** down in Bluewater on Wednesday—tucked his elbows in, leaned his head and chest forward over his knees, and pivoted smoothly across the two-inch corner onto the contoured seat of the *Titan-X350*.

Marcus smiled with a nod of veteran respect. "Cleanest forty-five-degree pivot transfer in Montgomery County, Mr. Fuller."

<aac>Angles and leverage beat brute force every time,</aac> Jordan's AAC speaker replied proudly as **Madison** beamed beside him, thinking of her little squirt practicing that exact pivot down in Bluewater. Then Jordan looked back at the empty, squeaking old hospital wheelchair from Virginia Beach and tapped a second line:

<aac>Mr. Vance, can you haul that old hospital chair away in your van for scrap recycling? I never want to see my mother's chair again.</aac>

"Nothing would give me greater pleasure, Mr. Fuller," Marcus grinned, folding up the worn institutional relic, tossing it into the back of the sprinter van for scrap, and slamming the rear doors shut to a round of cheers from the entire driveway.

The difference inside the new chair was instantaneous. Instead of feeling perched on a lightweight manual sling frame that tipped backward on steep curb cuts and demanded upper-body force for every foot of forward motion, Jordan felt anchored inside a cockpit built like a vault.

Marcus folded the left armrest down and tapped the power button on the right-hand module. The high-contrast color LCD screen booted up with five speed profiles (1: Indoor Dorm, 2: Lecture Hall, 3: Sidewalk Cruise, 4: Hill Climb Torque, 5: Full Campus), battery telemetry (100% — 22.0 MI RANGE), and power tilt-in-space controls.

Jordan rested his right fingertips lightly over the soft-touch ball of the joystick and nudged it two millimeters forward.

With a whisper-quiet, futuristic turbine hum from the dual four-pole center-drive motors, the three-hundred-and-fifty-pound chair glided forward across the driveway as smoothly as if it were riding on magnetic rails. Jordan eased the stick left, then pulled it slightly back, spinning a complete, effortless 360-degree turn inside the footprint of a single sidewalk square before tapping the rocker switch to ignite the bright white LED fender lamps.

Around the driveway, **Caleb**, **Owen**, **Lucas**, and **Jacob** burst into applause, while **Daniel** stood with his arm around **Laura**, beaming with pride.

Looking up at Daniel, Mark, and the women of his Constellation with a fierce glint in his green eyes, Jordan tapped his AAC screen:

<aac>There is only one real test for this chair. Take me up to Bennett Hall. I want to climb the exterior hill from the first-floor inner quad up to Washington Street.</aac>

***

#### March 16, 2015 • 2:15 PM — Conquering the Bennett Hall Hillside

Thirty minutes later back on campus in **Blacksburg**, Daniel parked the accessible ramp-equipped transit van—which he had leased for the spring and summer so Jordan could roll straight inside without transferring—along **Washington Street SW** outside the second-floor entrance of **Bennett Hall**.

After rolling down the exterior hillside walkway to the **first-floor inner quad doors** at the bottom of the slope, Jordan spun his chair around at the base of the hill.

It was the exact twelve-degree paved exterior incline between the first-floor inner quad level and the second-floor **Washington Street SW** entrance where, all through Fall Semester and the first two months of Spring, Jordan had either had to take the interior elevator ("Riding the Hill") or rely on Mark, Lauren, or Aubrie Jean bracing the rear push-handles of his manual chair to keep him from rolling backward.

He looked up the long, steep grade rising alongside the Ironstone and brick facade of Bennett Hall toward **Washington Street SW**. Up at the top of the slope outside the second-floor Washington Street SW doors, **Isabel Dawson** and **Garrett Reynolds** happened to be stepping out for their afternoon building walk—and both of them froze on the upper walkway, staring down the hill in amazement as they saw Jordan sitting in the matte-black power chair at the bottom of the ridge.

"Want us to walk behind you or beside you, Jordan?" **Mark** asked, his hands empty at his sides.

<aac>Beside me,</aac> Jordan's AAC speaker rang out clearly across the pavement. <aac>Nobody ever pushes from behind again.</aac>

Jordan tapped the mode button on his right-hand joystick up to **PROFILE 4: HILL CLIMB TORQUE** and pushed the joystick forward with two fingers.

The dual high-torque motors engaged with a deep, authoritative purr.

Without a single wobble, without a single dip in speed, and without Jordan having to strain a muscle in his shoulders, the three-hundred-and-fifty-pound matte-black *Titan-X350* surged straight up the twelve-degree exterior hillside walkway from the inner quad to **Washington Street SW** at a brisk four miles per hour.

**Aubrie Jean**, **Madison**, **Zoë**, **Lauren**, **Hannah**, **Mark**, **Sarah**, and **Jessica** actually had to lengthen their strides just to keep pace beside his wheels as he climbed the hill effortlessly in the bright afternoon sun.

When Jordan crested the top of the ridge onto the level **Washington Street SW** sidewalk outside the second-floor entrance of Bennett Hall, he spun the chair around to face the campus quad stretching out below them.

Outside the second-floor Washington Street SW doors, **Garrett** grinned and applauded, while **Isabel** pressed both hands over her mouth, her dark eyes shining with pure, unvarnished joy at seeing him back on the hill, whole and unstoppable.

"Three hundred and fifty pounds of freedom," Aubrie Jean whispered, leaning down to kiss his cheek as the wind ruffled his hair at the crest of the ridge.

***

#### March 17, 2015 • 9:00 AM — Maiden Voyage of the S.S. Freedom and the Kuiper Belt

On Tuesday morning, March seventeenth—the first morning of classes after Spring Break—**Jordan Fuller** rolled out through the upper-terrace doors of **Bennett Hall** into the bright spring sunshine.

Before they had gone to sleep the night before, **Mark** and **Hannah** had presented Jordan with a matching pair of laser-engraved matte-silver nameplates that Mark had machined in the **Joule Hall** engineering student shop—one mounted neatly on the rear backrest bracket of Jordan's three-hundred-and-fifty-pound *Vanguard Titan-X350* power wheelchair, and its twin mounted on the brushed-titanium crossbar of his fourteen-pound *Vanguard AeroLite-Ti* tight-space manual wheelchair (christened in honor of both the astronomer Galileo Galilei from `ASTR 204` and *Star Trek*'s famous auxiliary shuttlecraft):

**S.S. FREEDOM — CAPT. J. FULLER**
**SHUTTLECRAFT GALILEO — AUX. CRAFT TO S.S. FREEDOM**

As the nine of them set out across the wide paved paths of **Commonwealth Green** toward their morning lecture in **Archer Hall**, Jordan realized that something fundamental in the way he experienced the campus had changed overnight.

All through Fall Semester and the first half of Spring, rolling across campus in a manual chair had meant constantly calculating every curb lip, every uneven slab of concrete, and every uphill grade—always relying on Mark, Lauren, or Aubrie Jean to take the handles whenever the slope steepened.

Today, the air over **Commonwealth Green** smelled like damp earth, budding maple trees, and freshly cut grass—and Jordan was driving his own ship.

He nudged the joystick of the *S.S. Freedom* up to Profile 3: Sidewalk Cruise, feeling the warm spring breeze against his face as he rolled right down the center of the path—his left hand free to hold **Aubrie Jean's** hand as they moved side-by-side!—while **Madison**, **Zoë**, **Lauren**, **Hannah**, **Mark**, **Sarah**, and **Jessica** walked alongside him without anyone having to stand behind his back.

When they arrived at **Archer Hall** at 9:30 AM for **HIST 115: History of Ancient Rome**, **Dr. Marcus Gable** paused by the lectern as Jordan glided effortlessly up the ramped aisle into the top-tier accessible bay.

"Welcome back from the frontier, Mr. Fuller, Ms. Kelly, Ms. Scott," Dr. Gable said warmly, his sharp eyes taking in the matte-black power wheelchair with an approving nod. "Ms. Higgins told me the three of you executed a textbook strategic withdrawal before the break—and it appears the cavalry has upgraded its armor."

Jordan grinned and tapped his **Pinnacle Vanguard Pro** keyboard:

<aac>Thank you for letting us study remotely before the break, Dr. Gable. And yes, sir—the testudo is motorized now.</aac>

The entire back row chuckled, and Dr. Gable flashed a rare, proud smile before launching into the morning's lecture on Julius Caesar's bridging of the Rhine.

***

#### March 17, 2015 • 2:00 PM — Pluto, Charon, and the Kuiper Belt

That afternoon in **Kepler Hall**, after **Dr. Alistair** had similarly welcomed Jordan and Aubrie Jean back to **PHYS 102** and handed back their latest exam (99/100 for Jordan, 98/100 for Aubrie Jean), the two of them rolled upstairs into the darkened planetarium dome for **ASTR 204: Observational Astrophysics**.

Today's lecture topic was the outer frontier of the solar system: the **Kuiper Belt** and the scattered disk of icy planetesimals orbiting out beyond Neptune in the deep, cold twilight forty astronomical units from the Sun.

As the star projector cast the faint, glittering ring of trans-Neptunian worlds—**Pluto and Charon** locked in their mutual gravitational embrace, along with Haumea, Makemake, and Eris—across the curved dome overhead, Aubrie Jean leaned her shoulder gently against Jordan's left armrest and laced her fingers with his.

"Look at Pluto and Charon up there," Aubrie Jean whispered softly while Dr. Alistair explained how the binary pair orbited a shared center of gravity outside either body—tidally locked so that they forever faced each other across the dark. "Out at the edge of the cold where nobody thought a warm core could survive, and they never let go of each other."

Jordan looked up at the twin points of light wheeling slowly across the planetarium dome, then looked at Aubrie Jean beside him.

With a grin, Jordan typed quietly on his laptop screen for her:

<aac>And in sixty-seven days, we're taking our own orbit around this planet.</aac>

***

#### March 18, 2015 • 12:30 PM — The Food Court Affirmation and the Night of the Pact

At twelve-thirty on Wednesday afternoon, all nine members of **Suite 214/216** met up inside the bustling, multi-level hillside dining hall of **Kincaid Commons**.

At the start of Fall Semester, a crowded campus dining hall at the noon rush—five hundred students talking at once, stainless-steel trays clattering, espresso machines hissing, and lines snaking around the Ironstone pillars—would have spiked Jordan's sensory meter past eighty within three minutes and required Mark and Lauren to form a physical wedge around his manual chair while someone else ordered his food for him.

Today, as the nine of them claimed a long corner table by the tall arched windows overlooking the quad, **Mark** started to ask out of habit, "Want me to grab your grilled chicken wrap from the counter while you park, Jordan?"

Jordan smiled and shook his head.

He tapped his armrest tablet with a bright grin:

<aac>I've got it today, Mark. Meet you guys back at the table in five.</aac>

Guiding the *S.S. Freedom* with effortless precision through the bustling lunch crowd—using the twenty-one-inch mid-wheel turning radius to pivot cleanly around backpack-wearing students in the queue—Jordan rolled up to the counter by himself. When the student cashier looked down and smiled, Jordan triggered his order preset on his phone, flashed his **Poly Pass** dining card at the accessible reader, hooked the warm takeout bag onto his armrest carry-loop, and navigated smoothly back to the corner table without a single spike in his pulse or a single tremor in his hands.

When he pulled into his spot at the head of the table, all eight of his suitemates looked at him with quiet, beaming pride.

Grinning as he unwrapped his sandwich, Jordan tapped a quick key:

<aac>What?</aac>

"Nothing," **Hannah** said softly, leaning over to kiss his cheek. "Just watching a guy who owns his whole life order lunch."

***

#### March 18, 2015 • 9:30 PM — Night of the Constellation Pact

That evening back in **Bennett Hall**, after homework was finished and **Mark** and **Hannah** had retired into **Room 216** for the night, the connecting bathroom door clicked shut and the **six women of the Constellation Pact**—**Aubrie Jean**, **Madison**, **Zoë**, **Lauren**, **Sarah**, and **Jessica**—gathered with **Jordan** inside **Room 214**.

All week in Bluewater, sleeping side-by-side on the air mattresses in Madison's ground-floor childhood bedroom had been cozy and wonderful, yet out of respect for David, Diane, Bob, and Emily under the same roof, they had kept their nights strictly PG-13 under their pajamas and quilts.

Tonight, back inside their private second-floor sanctuary with the deadbolt turned and the warm amber fairy lights glowing along the cinderblock wall above **Bed A** and the two-high bunk (**Beds B and C**), the seven of them shed every layer of fabric and hesitation.

Using his practiced **Forty-Five-Degree Transfer**—the same smooth corner pivot he had passed down to Madison's little brother **Bob** in Bluewater—Jordan parked the *S.S. Freedom* at a clean forty-five-degree angle beside his nineteen-inch standalone Twin XL **Bed A**, leaned forward over his knees, and pivoted smoothly across the corner gap straight into the warm, bare arms of his Constellation.

Even within the narrow footprint of a 1960s dormitory room, there was no rush, no hierarchy, and not a shadow of jealousy anywhere in the space—only six women who loved him fiercely and loved one another as sisters, rotating effortlessly between Jordan's **Bed A** and the bunks across the narrow aisle as they took turns holding him, kissing him, and sharing a slow, breathtaking night of mutual passion and skin-to-skin tenderness where every touch affirmed how far he had come from the boy who used to flinch at his own reflection.

When they finally drifted off to sleep after midnight—with **Sarah** and **Jessica** curled bare and warm against Jordan's left and right sides on **Bed A** for their long-promised overnight turn, **Aubrie Jean** and **Madison** reaching across the narrow aisle from the lower bunk (**Bed B**) to hold his hands, and **Zoë** and **Lauren** nestled up on the top bunk (**Bed C**)—Jordan rested his palm lightly over the center of his chest, remembering the sacred **Heart-Hum** name (*The Key*) that **Bob** and **Emily** had given him in Bluewater, and drifted into a deep, peaceful sleep.

***

#### May 15, 2015 • 11:00 AM — Stripping Room 214

By eleven o'clock on Friday morning, May fifteenth—the final day of Spring Semester move-out at **Commonwealth Polytechnic Institute**, and the final day **Eleanor Bennett Commonwealth Hall ("The Old Lady")** would ever house undergraduate students before being permanently closed for demolition—**Suite 214/216** had been returned to the bare, echoing white cinderblock and polished linoleum it had been when Jordan first rolled across its threshold nine months earlier.

Final exams were officially in the books.

Yesterday afternoon, when the Registrar in **Preston Hall** posted spring grades, Jordan had stared at his transcript screen in quiet wonder: five As across **PHYS 102**, **ASTR 204**, **GEOL 101**, **MATH 112**, and **HIST 115**—locking in a cumulative **4.00 freshman-year GPA** right alongside **Aubrie Jean’s** matching 4.00.

Now, with only **eight days** remaining until all eighteen members of the family departed on **Saturday, May twenty-third** for **Jordan's World Trek**, the nine residents of Suite 214/216 were finishing the last step of freshman year: stripping Room 214 and Room 216 for move-out.

With **Mark**, **Lauren**, and **Daniel** rolling the last of the storage totes and rolled-up foam mattress toppers out to the central elevator—ready to be transferred to the Christiansburg house where their new off-campus quarters and the nine-foot-by-nine-foot Alaskan King bed frame were waiting for sophomore year—Jordan sat at the controls of his matte-black *S.S. Freedom* near the open doorway between Room 214 and the suite bathroom, wearing the heather-grey **CPI FORGERS** crew-neck t-shirt he had bought for himself at **The Foundry** (the CPI campus bookstore).

He packed the last of his desk books—including Arthur MacAllister's *Civitas*, his **ASTR 204** Kuiper Belt star charts, and the **Electric Color teal-and-maroon CAPTAIN OF THE HILL wooden clothespin** Isabel had brought him from the **CACUHO** conference—into his backpack.

He looked around the empty room where the string lights had hung above the headboard all winter and spring.

"Hard to believe freshman year is actually over," **Aubrie Jean** said softly, stepping up beside his chair and resting her hand on his shoulder as they looked at the bare university-issue Twin XL bed frames—Jordan's standalone nineteen-inch **Bed A** and the two-high bunk frame (**Beds B and C**) along the opposite wall—stripped clean for the final housing inspection. "Nine months ago, we walked into the Old Lady just praying we could keep you safe through Labor Day."

"And instead," **Madison** said, joining them with the swept dustpan in her hand and a warm smile on her lips, "we built a whole life inside these walls."

Out in the second-floor hallway, a polite knock sounded against the open oak door.

**Kelsey Brennan**, **Isabel Dawson**, and **Garrett Reynolds** stood at the threshold wearing their official **CPI Housing & Residence Life** staff uniforms—Kelsey in her full-time Professional Staff two-tone Chicago Maroon polo with Burnt Orange side panels, and Isabel and Garrett in their Student Staff Chicago Maroon polos with crisp white side panels and Burnt Orange shoulder trim, all tucked neatly into belted khaki pants—holding the official yellow **Room Condition Report (RCR)** clipboards and clearance envelopes.

"Ready for the last checkout inspection in the history of the Old Lady?" Kelsey asked warmly, her eyes misty as she looked around the spotless, swept floors of Room 216 and Room 214. "Let me sign off Mark, Hannah, Sarah, and Jessica's rooms first, and then we'll take the final cart down to Daniel's trailer."

### Part 2: A Long Hug in the Hallway & Ready for the World

**Date:** 2015-05-15 at 11:20 America/New_York

![In the second-floor hallway outside stripped Room 214 on Spring 2015 Move-Out Day, Isabel Dawson kneels on the clean floor in her maroon-and-white CPI Residence Life uniform beside clean-shaven Jordan's matte-black S.S. Freedom power wheelchair, crying softly as she wraps both arms tightly around Jordan's neck in one last long, deep goodbye hug because she will miss him so much over the summer.]({{CDN}}/raggiesoft-books/images/scenes/aubrie/e003/c011/s002/isabel-goodbye-hug.jpg)

#### 11:20 AM — A Very Long Hug in the Second-Floor Hallway

Within five minutes, eight of the nine yellow **Room Condition Reports (RCRs)** were signed, stamped, and filed into their completed checkout folders, deactivating their Bennett Hall door-access permissions on the central **Poly Pass** server while leaving their university ID cards active for the rest of their college careers.

**Daniel**, **Mark**, **Hannah**, **Lauren**, **Madison**, **Zoë**, **Sarah**, and **Jessica** rolled the last four loaded utility carts out through the **second-floor Washington Street SW entrance** to load the trailer waiting at the curb. **Aubrie Jean** paused at the doorway, gave Jordan's shoulder a gentle, affectionate squeeze, and walked down the hall toward the Washington Street SW doors with the others so Jordan could finish the final Room 214 checkout himself.

At the doorway of Suite 214, **Garrett Reynolds** reached down and shook Jordan's hand with a firm, warm grip.

"It has been an absolute honor being your RA this year, Jordan," Garrett said sincerely. "Watching you climb the Bennett Hall hill from the inner quad up to Washington Street in that matte-black tank and watching how the nine of you stood together all year—that's the kind of thing I'm going to remember long after I graduate. Have the trip of a lifetime across the world this summer, man."

Jordan tapped his armrest tablet warmly:

<aac>Thank you for everything, Garrett. For keeping our wing locked down tight after that investigator showed up outside Bennett Hall, for fighting for our suite at CACUHO, and for keeping the second floor steady.</aac>

Garrett glanced once at **Isabel Dawson**, who was standing beside the open door of **Room 215** holding the very last yellow RCR clipboard—Jordan's—and then glanced at **Kelsey Brennan**.

"Hey, Kelsey," Garrett said smoothly, picking up the heavy file box of completed first-floor and second-floor RCR checkout folders from the hallway table, "let's run these RCR archive boxes down to the main office while Isabel finishes the final signature on 214."

"Good idea," Kelsey said, flashing Jordan a warm smile before heading toward the stairwell with Garrett. "Have an incredible summer abroad, Jordan! We'll see you in August!"

The heavy stairwell door clicked shut at the end of the corridor.

Suddenly, the sun-drenched second-floor hallway of **Bennett Hall** was completely quiet. Dust motes floated in the afternoon light pouring through the tall casement window at the end of the hall.

Isabel stood alone in front of Jordan's chair with the two-part carbonless checkout form and a black pen in her hands.

"One final line at the bottom of the Room Condition Report, Mr. Fuller," Isabel said softly, trying to use her official Resident Advisor voice one last time, though her dark eyes were already bright with emotion behind her glasses as she held out the clipboard. "Zero damages, room left in immaculate condition, Room 214-A cleared and Poly Pass residential access scheduled for five o'clock deactivation."

Jordan took the pen and signed *Jordan Fuller* on the resident checkout line.

Isabel tore off the yellow resident receipt copy, handed it to Jordan, and tucked the white Housing original into the clipboard folder.

Looking up at the Resident Advisor who had welcomed him into **Bennett Hall** nine months ago, knelt beside his desk during the September fire drill, welcomed his found family to Charlottesville over Thanksgiving, and stood guard over their floor all year, Jordan smiled warmly and tapped a lighthearted message onto his armrest tablet screen:

<aac>As of right now, my lease for the academic year is closed. Which means you aren't my Resident Advisor anymore.</aac>

Isabel froze.

Her breath caught audibly in her throat, and a deep, rosy blush rose up her neck into her cheeks. She looked down at the yellow RCR clipboard in her hand, and then looked back at Jordan—her lips parting slightly as her right hand came up to touch the collar of her shirt, as if she were suddenly flustered by a rush of emotion she wasn't ready to put into words.

![At the doorway of stripped Room 214 (with Jordan's single low Bed A and bare oak desk behind him, and the black electronic Poly Pass RFID card reader mounted directly below the ROOM 214 sign), clean-shaven Jordan Fuller sits in his matte-black S.S. Freedom power wheelchair wearing a heather-grey CPI Forgers bookstore t-shirt while RA Isabel Dawson stands in her maroon-and-white CPI Residence Life Student Staff uniform holding his yellow RCR clipboard—blushing rosy pink with one hand touching her collar and smiling through bright, emotional tears.]({{CDN}}/raggiesoft-books/images/scenes/aubrie/e003/c011/s002/isabel-move-out-secret.jpg#fullwidth)

Then Isabel glanced down at the white embroidered **CPI HOUSING & RESIDENCE LIFE — RESIDENT ADVISOR** lettering on the left chest of the two-tone maroon-and-white Student Staff athletic polo shirt she still had tucked into her belted khaki pants, looked at the black electronic **Poly Pass** card reader glowing green directly underneath the **ROOM 214** sign on the cinderblock wall where she was still officially on duty until five o'clock, and looked back at Jordan, who was flying across the oceans in eight days to see the world.

She let out a shaky breath, a bright tear slipping down her flushed cheek as a radiant, tender smile broke through at the exact same time.

"No," Isabel whispered, her voice thick with emotion. "As of eleven-twenty-five on May fifteenth... I'm not your RA anymore."

Jordan tapped the button on his right armrest to flip up the left arm of his chair and opened his arms wide.

Isabel didn't hesitate for a heartbeat.

She stepped right into the open space beside his frame, dropped to her knees on the clean hallway floor so they were at exact eye level, and wrapped both of her arms tightly around Jordan's neck—pulling him into **a very long, deep, breathless goodbye hug**.

Jordan wrapped his strong arms around her waist and shoulders, holding her close against his chest, feeling her shoulders tremble slightly as she cried softly against him—overwhelmed by the end of their year in the Old Lady and by how much she was going to miss him while he was away all summer.

Isabel buried her face against the crook of his neck, her dark hair brushing his smooth, clean-shaven jaw as warm tears dampened the collar of his shirt while she held onto him for nearly a full minute in the quiet hallway.
