#### July 17, 2015 • 9:00 PM — The Three-Continent Video Call

At nine o'clock on Friday evening in **Singapore**—which was two o'clock in the afternoon for **Henry Walsh** at the **London School of Economics and Commerce (`LSEC`)** in **London**, and nine o'clock on Friday morning for **Isabel Dawson** at her family's home in **Charlottesville, Virginia**—**Zoë** propped her **mPad Pro** on the center coffee table of their Marina Bay suite and connected it to the room's wide wall monitor for a three-continent **mFace** video conference.

Within three seconds, the split-screen chime sounded.

On the left half of the screen appeared **Henry Walsh** in his sunlit student flat near Houghton Street in London, a mug of builder's tea in his hand and a huge grin on his face.

On the right half of the screen appeared **Isabel Dawson** sitting at the sunny breakfast table of her parents' home in Charlottesville, wearing blue jeans and a soft maroon **Commonwealth Polytechnic Institute** T-shirt, her dark brown hair cascading over her shoulders.

"Good morning from Virginia, Good Afternoon from London, and Good Evening to Singapore!" **Henry** called out cheerfully as all eighteen members of the World Trek waved at the camera. "Look at that view behind your balcony window! Did the Chief Navigator conquer the equator?"

<aac>Six for six on transit smart cards, Henry!</aac> Jordan's `"Sydney"` voice rang out proudly as he held his gleaming **`MerlionLink Card`** up to the webcam so both Henry and Isabel could see it. <aac>Singapore Changi Airport had a two-story butterfly garden inside the terminal, a butterfly landed right on my AAC screen, and every single SMRT subway station in the entire country is one hundred percent step-free with zero platform gap!</aac>

On the right side of the split screen, **Isabel's** entire face lit up—and the very instant her eyes locked onto Jordan smiling in his wheelchair, a deep, radiant crimson blush bloomed across her cheeks, spreading all the way from the collar of her CPI T-shirt to the tips of her ears.

"Oh, Jordan, look at you!" Isabel beamed, her hands coming up to her glowing cheeks as she leaned closer to her laptop camera in Charlottesville, completely captivated by how healthy, sun-kissed, and relaxed he looked. "You look so happy! You don't have any tension in your shoulders at all! Have you been sleeping well? Did the ferry across the Seto Inland Sea go okay?"

<aac>It was the best night of my life, Isabel,</aac> Jordan typed warmly, smiling straight into the lens at her. <aac>The ship sang a lullaby called Hoshizora no Uta over the speakers as we sailed out of Osaka, and Zoë translated the lyrics for me. It told us to leave our heavy shadows on the shore because we were safe upon the sea. And next semester, all nine of us are registering together for Elementary Japanese I at CPI!</aac>

Isabel's dark eyes turned glassy with sudden, overwhelming emotion. Her blush deepened by another three shades of scarlet, her heart beating so fast she completely forgot there were nineteen other people on the call.

"Jordan, I am so proud of you I could burst," Isabel said breathlessly, her voice trembling with raw, unfiltered adoration as her fingers pressed over her collarbone. "I've missed your voice and your smile every single day since May, and seeing you glow like that makes me realize how madly in l—"

Isabel froze mid-syllable.

Her eyes went wide in sheer panic as her brain caught up with her tongue half a second before the word *love* left her lips.

"—in *luck*!" Isabel blurted out, her voice pitching an octave higher as her face turned the exact color of her maroon CPI T-shirt. "How madly in *luck* I am to have been your RA in Bennett Hall and to be your neighbor at **Allegheny Commons** this fall! Just—so, *so* lucky!"

For two full seconds, a hilarious, electric silence hung across three continents.

In London, **Henry Walsh** had to clamp his hand over his mouth and pretend to take a very long sip of his tea to hide his grin—because from his side of the split screen, Isabel's radiant, head-over-heels blush was visible from space.

In Singapore, **Aubrie**, **Madison**, **Lauren**, **Sarah**, **Jessica**, **Hannah**, **Mark**, **Daniel**, **Laura**, and every single one of the **Brooks** siblings saw it too, exchanging warm, knowing, delighted glances across the suite without saying a word to embarrass her.

Beside Jordan's right armrest, **Zoë's** internal diagnostic logger fired at light speed:

```
ZOË.Systems.Logs.KernelLog: Thread 7 (Campus_Allies: Isabel_Dawson) — Verbal.Slip.Intercepted("madly in l-[ove]" -> "madly in luck"). Cutaneous.Vasodilation: MAXIMUM_CRIMSON_BLUSH (Continuous duration: 142 seconds). 07-17-2015 21:04:18
ZOË.Systems.Logs.EmotionalStateLog: Thread 3 (Jordan) — Visual.Recognition: CONFIRMED. Jordan's optical sensors have locked onto Thread 7's blush. Facial expression: Warm_Affectionate_Smile. Probability(Mutual_Awareness) == 100.00%. 07-17-2015 21:04:22
```

Because even **Jordan** saw it.

Sitting in his power chair in the middle of the room, Jordan looked at Isabel's bright red cheeks on the monitor, his eyes crinkling warmly behind his glasses as a gentle, unmistakable smile curved his lips. He knew Isabel wasn't ready to say the word out loud over a group video call across twelve time zones—and he respected her boundary completely—but the warmth in his chest told him he had heard every word she *almost* said.

<aac>I feel pretty lucky too, Isabel,</aac> Jordan's `"Sydney"` voice replied softly, rescuing her with effortless grace. <aac>When do you move into Apartment 101 at Allegheny Commons?</aac>

Isabel let out a shaky, grateful breath, fanning her still-blushing cheeks with one hand while smiling back at him with her whole heart in her eyes.

"RA training starts the first week of August, so I'll be all moved into **Apartment 101** well before you get back from Australia," Isabel said, leaning toward her camera as she looked directly at Jordan. "Tell me the exact flight number and arrival time for your return into **Roanoke-Blacksburg Regional Airport (`ROA`)** in August, Jordan. I don't care what time of day or night your plane touches down—I promise I'm going to be standing right there at the arrivals gate at **ROA** waiting for you the second you roll off that jet bridge."

"Make that *two* of us at the **ROA** arrivals gate!" **Henry** chimed in warmly from the London half of the screen, lowering his teacup with a broad smile. "My summer term at **LSEC** wraps up in two weeks, and I fly back into Virginia at the end of July to move into **Apartment 115** right down the hall from Isabel. So Isabel and I will drive up to **Roanoke-Blacksburg Regional Airport** together and be waiting side by side at the gate when all eighteen of you land!"

"It's a date!" **Aubrie** smiled, squeezing Jordan's shoulder as **Mark** and **Hannah** gave Henry and Isabel a double thumbs-up. "Next stop tomorrow morning: a seven-hour flight down to **Sydney** and **Liverpool, New South Wales**, and then two weeks out at the **Gallagher Roadhouse** in the Northern Territory Outback before we fly home to Virginia!"

<aac>See you both at ROA in August,</aac> Jordan typed, giving Isabel and Henry a warm wave before the call signed off—and even as the screen faded out, Isabel was still blushing and smiling from ear to ear.

#### July 18, 2015 • 2:00 PM — Sentosa Monorail, Palawan Boardwalk, and the Southern Cross Boarding Gate

Because their overnight **Southern Cross Airways** flight from **Singapore Changi (`SIN`)** to **Sydney (`SYD`)** didn't depart until eight-fifteen on Saturday evening, **Daniel** and **Zoë** had arranged a late checkout from their Marina Bay suites so the family could spend Saturday afternoon at the very southern edge of the Asian continent.

Tapping their **`MerlionLink`** cards on the **North East Line** down to **HarbourFront Station**, the eighteen travelers rode the wide glass elevator up to the third-floor monorail terminal and boarded the brightly painted, barrier-free **Sentosa Island Monorail**.

Gliding high above the turquoise shipping channel on a single concrete beam with zero platform gap at every station, the monorail carried them out across the causeway to the lush, palm-fringed resort island of **Sentosa**.

At **Beach Station**, Jordan rolled off onto the shaded, step-free **Palawan Accessible Boardwalk**, where a wide timber-and-stone promenade wound beneath swaying coconut palms along the white sand of **Palawan Beach** overlooking the warm, emerald-green waters of the **Singapore Strait**.

Pausing at the coastal lookout pavilion at **`1° 14' North Latitude`**—just eighty-five miles north of the equator, marking the southernmost coastal edge of continental Asia—Jordan sat in his power chair watching rows of giant red-and-blue container ships steaming between the Indian Ocean and the South China Sea while **Sarah** and **Jessica** pointed straight south across the horizon.

"Right out past those ships and across the Java Sea is home, J," **Jessica** grinned, shading her eyes in the eighty-four-degree equatorial sunshine. "By nine o'clock tomorrow morning, we'll be sixty-two degrees and wearing our winter jackets in **Sydney**!"

Beside Jordan's right armrest, **Zoë** logged the coordinate milestone on her `mPad`:

Outside the panoramic floor-to-ceiling glass sat a gleaming white widebody **Southern Cross Airways** jet, its towering red tail fin emblazoned with the iconic white silhouette of a bounding kangaroo and the five stars of the **Southern Cross**.

Welcome aboard Southern Cross to Sydney!" the lead purser beamed in a rich New South Wales accent that sounded like a live twin of Jordan's **`"Sydney"`** `EchoType` profile, kneeling briefly beside his power chair to review the padded cargo-hold tie-down checklist with Daniel and Jessica. "We've got your First Class flat-bed pod right up front next to your family, and our Sydney ramp engineers at Kingsford Smith are already briefed to have your rig waiting right at the aerobridge door at `06:10` sharp tomorrow morning."

<aac>Thank you very much,</aac> Jordan's `"Sydney"` voice replied—causing the purser's eyes to crinkle with instant delight as he heard his own hometown accent speaking back from an American teenager's laptop. <aac>I have been using a Sydney voice all year in Virginia. I am very excited to finally bring it home to Sydney.</aac>

"Mate, Sydney's going to roll out the red carpet for you!" the purser laughed warmly.

Ten minutes later—after **Jessica** effortlessly scooped Jordan out of his power chair at the aerobridge door, waved off the terminal aisle chair with a cheerful grin, and carried him straight into his First Class lie-flat suite beside **Aubrie** and **Zoë**—the widebody jet roared down the Changi runway and climbed southward into the equatorial twilight. Jordan watched the altitude display cross thirty-five thousand feet, and then watched the cabin map line cross **`0° 00' Latitude`** into the **Southern Hemisphere** while he drifted off to sleep.

## Leg 8: Southern Cross Winter, The Red Centre, & Home to Roanoke (Australia)

### Part 1: Sydney Harbour, The Three Sisters, & The Jamison Skyway

**Date:** 2015-07-19 at 09:30 Australia/Sydney

![On the sunny suburban rail platform at Liverpool Station, New South Wales, Australia beneath towering eucalyptus gum trees and silver double-decker Waratah trains, Jordan Fuller sits in his matte-black S.S. Freedom power wheelchair wearing his maroon CPI fleece with his black laptop angled toward his face in front of the orange-and-white LIVERPOOL STATION sign while Australian suitemate Sarah Braithwaite grins and gives a triumphant thumbs-up alongside Aubrie Jean Kelly, Madison Scott, Zoë Wren Brooks, tall Jessica Gallagher, Lauren, and Hannah.]({{CDN}}/raggiesoft-books/images/scenes/aubrie/e004/c008/p001/right-liverpool-station-nsw.jpg)

#### July 19, 2015 • 9:30 AM — Southern Cross Airways and Smart Card Number Seven

When the widebody **Southern Cross Airways** jet touched down on Runway 16R extending into Botany Bay at **Sydney Kingsford Smith International Airport (`SYD`)** after a seven-and-a-half-hour overnight flight south from Singapore, **Jordan Fuller** had officially crossed into the Southern Hemisphere for the first time in his life.

Six weeks earlier, back in the study on Geneva Street in Christiansburg, the words *"two weeks in Australia in July and August"* had briefly triggered a spike of anxiety in Jordan's chest. Having spent eighteen years locked inside a second-floor bedroom in the Northern Hemisphere, Jordan had heard *"August"* and immediately pictured a lethal, one-hundred-and-twenty-degree Australian summer—blistering heatwaves, scorching pavement, and overheated wheelchair motors.

It had taken **Jessica Gallagher** five minutes with a desk globe and a weather chart of New South Wales and the Northern Territory to gently dismantle that Northern Hemisphere illusion.

*"Mate, we're south of the equator,"* Jessica had grinned back in May, tapping the bottom half of the globe with her knuckle. *"When Virginia is sweating through July and August, Australia is in the dead of winter. Sydney sits around a crisp sixty-two degrees in the afternoon, and out at my family's roadhouse in the Petermann desert, you'll be scraping white winter frost off your tires at dawn."*

As the airport ground crew delivered Jordan's matte-black power chair to the forward aircraft door at **Sydney Terminal 1** and Jordan rolled up the jet bridge through Australian Customs and Quarantine, he felt the truth of Jessica's words the instant the automatic glass doors slid open to the outdoor arrivals concourse.

Gone was the warm, eighty-six-degree equatorial air of Singapore. In its place was a brisk, crystal-clear, sixty-one-degree **Southern Hemisphere winter morning** carrying the clean salt tang of the Tasman Sea—so crisp and invigorating that Jordan happily zipped his maroon **Commonwealth Polytechnic Institute** fleece jacket up to his chin while **Sarah Braithwaite** and **Jessica Gallagher** took deep, nostalgic breaths of home.

"Smell that eucalyptus and harbour salt!" **Sarah** beamed, her Sydney accent richer and brighter than ever as she bounced on her toes beside **Lauren**. "Welcome to New South Wales, family! Ready to claim the final trophy in the sleeve, J?"

<aac>Seven of seven,</aac> Jordan's `"Sydney"` voice—which now matched the accent of every customs officer and station attendant around them—announced proudly. <aac>Lead the way to the station elevator, Sarah.</aac>

Following the blue wheelchair pictograms across the terminal concourse, the eighteen travelers rode the wide glass lift down to the underground platform of **International Airport Station**, served by the **Transit NSW / Sydney Rail** network.

Right beside the wide accessible faregate stood the customer service counter and smart-card vending kiosk. With the entire family gathered around him in a grinning semicircle, Jordan rolled up to the lowered counter window and purchased his seventh and final international transit card of the summer: the glossy teal-and-navy **`HarbourCard`**, emblazoned with a stylized geometric wave of Sydney Harbour.

Jordan pulled the clear collector's binder sleeve from his side bag and slid the **`HarbourCard`** into the seventh pocket, completing the global grid he had started building six weeks earlier across four continents:

1. **`NordicPass`** — *Reykjavik Capital Transit (`RCT`), Reykjavik, Iceland*
2. **`Pearl Card`** — *London Transport Authority (`LTA`), London, England, UK*
3. **`MerseyPass`** — *Mersey Transit, Liverpool, Merseyside, England, UK*
4. **`Midori Card`** — *Nippon Rail East (`NR East`) & Tokyo Rapid Subway, Tokyo, Japan*
5. **`KansaiPass`** — *Nippon Rail West (`NR West`) & Osaka Rapid Subway, Osaka, Japan*
6. **`MerlionLink Card`** — *Singapore Mass Rapid Transit (`SMRT`), Singapore*
7. **`HarbourCard`** — *Transit NSW / Sydney Rail, Sydney & Liverpool, New South Wales, Australia*

Beside Jordan's armrest, **Zoë** smiled warmly and tilted her **mPad** screen slightly toward him—openly sharing her cognitive telemetry now that the secret was out:

<aac>Array complete with zero missing indices,</aac> Jordan typed back to Zoë with a grin before tapping his new **`HarbourCard`** against the circular reader on the wide accessible gate.

With a cheerful *ding*, the glass barriers swung open. On the platform below, a silver double-decker **T8 Airport & South Line** train glided to a stop, and a uniformed **Sydney Rail** station attendant stepped out with a lightweight folding boarding ramp to bridge the threshold into the vestibule's dedicated wheelchair space.

Twenty minutes later, the train emerged from the underground city tunnel onto the elevated viaduct of **Circular Quay Station**, and Jordan rolled out onto the wide, level granite foreshore promenade of **Sydney Cove**.

Directly to his right, gleaming like giant porcelain seashells against the deep cobalt blue of the harbour and a cloudless winter sky, stood the soaring white sails of the **Bennelong Point Performing Arts Centre**—affectionately known across Australia as ***The White Sails of Sydney Cove***. Directly to his left rose the monumental grey steel arch of **The Sydney Harbour Arch Bridge**, while green-and-gold **Circular Quay** ferries churned across the sparkling water between the harbour headlands.

Jordan parked his chair along the accessible harbourside railing between **Aubrie**, **Sarah**, and **Jessica**, letting the cool sixty-four-degree July winter breeze wash over his face as his `"Sydney"` voice spoke softly over the sound of the waves.

<aac>Ten thousand miles from Virginia,</aac> Jordan typed, looking out across the harbour toward the gleaming white sails of Bennelong Point. <aac>And the air feels just like late October in Blacksburg.</aac>

***

#### July 19, 2015 • 2:30 PM — Under the White Sails and the Royal Botanic Foreshore

After checking into their accessible harbourside serviced apartments near **Circular Quay** and eating a hearty winter lunch overlooking the ferry wharves, **Sarah Braithwaite** officially assumed command as Sydney Chief Tour Guide.

"Alright, everyone, zip up your fleeces and follow me!" Sarah beamed, linking her arm through **Lauren's** while walking right beside Jordan's left armrest as they rolled east along the wide, level granite promenade of **East Circular Quay**. "You've seen **The White Sails** from across the cove—now you're going to touch them up close!"

Rising at the tip of the headland where **Sydney Cove** met **Farm Cove** stood the world-famous silhouette of the **Bennelong Point Performing Arts Centre**.

From a distance, its interlocking vaulted shells had looked like smooth white porcelain sails billowed by the harbour wind. Up close, as Jordan rode the dedicated subterranean glass lift up from the lower concourse to the upper podium deck—completely bypassing the monumental ceremonial granite stairs—he realized that the surface of every single shell was actually an intricate, shimmering chevron mosaic composed of over **one million Swedish ceramic tiles** in alternating glossy white and matte cream tones.

"Touch the tilework right there on the rib, J," **Zoë** said, running her fingers admiringly along the curved precast concrete and ceramic edge beside Jordan's wheelchair. "In 1957, the original competition sketches were freehand curves that no structural engineer knew how to calculate—until they realized every single shell could be sliced as a precise geometric triangle from a single sphere of identical radius, allowing the ribs to be mass-cast and computer-modeled cleanly."

<aac>They solved an impossible curve by slicing it out of a single sphere,</aac> Jordan typed into `NeoEdit`, reaching out with his right hand to feel the cool, glazed geometric chevrons warming in the crisp sixty-three-degree July winter sun. <aac>And look how the matte and glossy tiles catch the winter sunlight without blinding you.</aac>

From the western boardwalk of **Bennelong Point**, a wide, step-free stone gate led directly into the thirty-hectare waterfront sanctuary of the **Royal Botanic Foreshore**.

For the next two hours, Jordan drove his power chair along the curving, level seawall promenade that hugged the sparkling blue curve of **Farm Cove** all the way out to **Mrs. Macquarie's Point**.

Above them towered ancient Moreton Bay fig trees with massive buttressed roots and silvery eucalyptus gums, and perched in the branches—completely unbothered by the passersby—were dozens of wild, snow-white **sulphur-crested cockatoos** with bright yellow head crests that fanned up like punk-rock mohawks whenever they squawked to one another.

"Wait—those are wild cockatoos just hanging out in the park trees like pigeons?!" **Madison** gasped, pulling out her camera as **Hannah** and **Mark** stared up at three cockatoos preening on a low sandstone wall.

"Wait till you see how cheeky they are if you leave a hot chip unattended on a picnic table," **Jessica** chuckled, standing tall beside **Sarah**. "They're smarter than half the blokes in Tom Lawson's fraternity."

Out at the sandstone headland of **Mrs. Macquarie's Point**—where ahistoric bench had been hand-carved out of the living coastal rock in `1810`—the entire group paused as the early Southern Hemisphere winter sunset began at four-forty-five in the afternoon.

Looking west across the cobalt water of **Farm Cove**, the view was pure postcard magic: the gleaming white shells of the **Bennelong Point Performing Arts Centre** stood in the foreground, framed directly beneath the monumental grey steel arch of **The Sydney Harbour Arch Bridge** while the sky behind the city skyline blazed with bands of deep winter rose, amber, and violet.

#### July 21, 2015 • 11:30 AM — Right Liverpool, Everyone! (Liverpool, New South Wales)

On Tuesday morning, it was time to close the loop on a ten-thousand-five-hundred-mile joke.

At **Circular Quay Station**, Jordan tapped his **`HarbourCard`** at the wide accessible gate and led the eighteen travelers aboard a step-free, double-decker **T2 Inner West & South Line** commuter train heading southwest across the sprawling suburbs of **Greater Western Sydney**.

For fifty minutes, **Sarah Braithwaite** sat right beside **Lauren** and **Jordan** in the accessible vestibule carriage, pointing out every landmark through the wide glass windows as the urban towers of central Sydney gave way to brick bungalows, towering eucalyptus gums, rugby ovals, and the winding bends of the **Georges River**.

At eleven-twenty-eight, the automated chime sounded overhead: *"Next stop: Liverpool. Doors will open on the left."*

When the station attendant deployed the boarding ramp onto the level concrete platform and the group rolled out past the faregates into the sunny forecourt of **Liverpool Station, New South Wales**, **Mark**, **Madison**, and **Lauren** immediately Recreated their formation from six weeks earlier in Merseyside—lining everyone up directly in front of the large white-and-orange **`LIVERPOOL STATION`** sign beneath a canopy of Australian gum trees.

Only this time, **Sarah Braithwaite** didn't give a thumbs-down.

Standing right beside Jordan's matte-black power chair in the crisp sixty-five-degree winter sunshine, Sarah threw one arm around Lauren's waist, pointed at the **`LIVERPOOL`** sign with a radiant grin, and gave a triumphant thumbs-up to the camera.

"**Right Liverpool, everyone!**" Sarah cheered at the top of her lungs as all eighteen of them burst into laughter and applause. "Zero Irish Sea fog, one hundred percent Greater Western Sydney, and not a single narcissist ex-boyfriend within ten thousand miles!"

Jordan's fingers flew across his **Pinnacle Vanguard Pro** keyboard as Lauren snapped the companion photograph to their Merseyside picture:

<aac>Iteration 2 of 2: Liverpool, New South Wales, Australia (33.9200° S, 150.9255° E),</aac> Jordan's `"Sydney"` voice announced to a chorus of cheers. <aac>Query resolved. Correct hemisphere confirmed. You owe the family meat pies and flat whites, Sarah.</aac>

"And a Braithwaite always pays her debts!" Sarah laughed, kissing Jordan's cheek before leading the procession two blocks down the level footpath of **Macquarie Street** to her favorite childhood bakery, where she treated the entire eighteen-person family to flaky, piping-hot Australian meat pies, sausage rolls, and velvety flat white coffees.

From the bakery, they walked ten minutes down a quiet, tree-lined residential street near the Georges River to the single-story brick **Braithwaite family homestead**—where Sarah's aunts, uncles, cousins, and childhood neighbors had spent the morning setting up a massive backyard winter barbecue on the wide, step-free concrete patio under the gum trees.

The afternoon was pure, unhurried warmth. While Sarah's Uncle Mick manned the sizzling flat-top barbie—grilling marinated lamb chops, beef sausages, caramelized onions, and burgers topped with sliced beetroot and grilled pineapple—Jordan rolled smoothly across the level patio, chatting effortlessly with Sarah's cousins as his `"Sydney"` voice blended right into the backyard banter.

Toward the end of the afternoon, as they sat around the patio table drinking cold ginger beer in the slanting golden winter sunlight, Sarah's Uncle Mick clapped **Jessica Gallagher** on her six-foot-three shoulder.

"So, Jessica," Uncle Mick grinned, nodding toward Sarah. "You're taking our Liverpool city girl out to your folks' roadhouse in **Petermann** next week? You do know the furthest west Sarah's ever been in her life is the Blue Mountains cable car, right?"

At the end of the table, **Sarah's** cheeks turned pink as she hid behind her ginger beer bottle.

"Wait a second," **Mark** grinned, leaning forward across the table. "Hold everything. Sarah, you're Australian—have you seriously never been to the Outback?"

"I grew up in **Greater Sydney**!" Sarah protested, laughing as **Lauren** and **Madison** teased her mercilessly. "Liverpool has train lines, shopping malls, and espresso bars! The **Northern Territory** is two thousand kilometers of red dirt, road trains, and freezing desert nights! I'm a hundred percent a suburban city girl—I need Jessica and her twin sister Bec to teach me how not to freeze in a swag just as much as the rest of you!"

"Too right you do, Braithwaite," **Jessica** chuckled warmly, flexing her sun-bronzed arm as she looked around the table at Jordan, Sarah, Mark, and the rest of the Pact. "Out in **Petermann**, we're three hours of corrugated red dirt past the **Uluṟu** airstrip—the very last fuel bowser and mechanics' bay before three hundred kilometers of empty desert scrub. And since Bec and Dad just finished welding a custom steel treadplate ramp onto the homestead verandah for Jordan's chair, class starts the second we touch down in the Red Centre."

***

#### July 24, 2015 • 10:30 AM — Across Sydney Heads on the Manly Ferry and the Mosman Wildlife Sanctuary

On Friday morning of their first week in New South Wales, **Sarah** and **Jessica** declared that it was time for Jordan to put his teal-and-navy **`HarbourCard`** to use on the water.

At **Circular Quay Wharf 3**, Jordan tapped his **`HarbourCard`** at the wide accessible gate and rolled across the heavyhydraulic brow ramp onto the lower main deck of the *Collaroy*—one of Sydney's iconic, double-ended green-and-gold **Freshwater-class Manly Ferries**.

As the deep brass horn echoed off the skyscrapers of Circular Quay and the ferry churned northeast out into the main harbour channel, Jordan parked his 350-pound power chair beside the wide viewing windows of the forward promenade deck, surrounded by the entire eighteen-person family.

Halfway through the thirty-minute voyage, the sheltered bays fell behind them and the ferry crossed straight across the one-mile-wide oceanic entrance between **North Head** and **South Head**—the towering sandstone cliffs known as **Sydney Heads**, where the deep turquoise swells of the **Tasman Sea** and the **South Pacific Ocean** rolled directly into the harbour.

As the 1,100-ton vessel rose and dipped gently over the long ocean rollers, Jordan felt his stomach give a thrilling, weightless swoop—laughing silently as **Mark**, **Caleb**, and **Lucas** tried to walk in a straight line across the deck without grabbing the brass handrails while **Jessica** and **Sarah** stood planted like seasoned sailors.

<aac>Look at those sandstone cliffs at the harbour mouth,</aac> Jordan typed into `NeoEdit` as the ferry glided into the calm waters of **Manly Cove**. <aac>Every ship that ever sailed to Sydney had to pass right between those two rocks.</aac>

Rolling off the step-free wharf at **Manly**, they followed the wide, flat, palm-lined pedestrian plaza of **The Corso** straight across the narrow peninsula from the harbour side to the roaring surf of **Manly Beach** on the open ocean, where towering Norfolk Island pines lined the accessible beachfront promenade and wetsuit-clad winter surfers rode the crisp emerald rollers.

After lunching on grilled barramundi and hot chips along the Corso, the group caught the cross-harbour ferry back toward the city, disembarking at the northern headland wharf of **Mosman Headland Wildlife Sanctuary**.

Because the sanctuary had been carved into a natural bushland amphitheater rising steeply up from the harbour shore, the ferry wharf connected directly to the lower terminal of a step-free **Aerial Sky Safari Gondola** and accessible electric bus link that carried Jordan's power chair effortlessly to the very top of the ridge—so that his entire route through the sanctuary was a gentle, scenic downhill roll with panoramic views of **The Sydney Harbour Arch Bridge** and **The White Sails of Sydney Cove** glittering across the water behind every enclosure.

Ten minutes down the upper eucalyptus trail, a ranger swung open the wide double gates of the **Walk-Through Kangaroo & Wallaby Bush Track**.

There were no bars or glass barriers inside the paddock—just a wide, compacted red-gravel wheelchair path winding through native banksia and gum trees where dozens of **eastern grey kangaroos** and smaller, russet-furred **swamp wallabies** lounged in the warm afternoon winter sun.

Jordan slowed his power chair to two miles per hour and came to a gentle stop near a sunny patch of grass.

Almost immediately, a three-foot-tall swamp wallaby with velvety brown ears and dark, curious eyes hopped unhurriedly over to the side of Jordan's wheelchair, resting its tiny front paws lightly against the rubber edge of his right armrest to sniff the cup of ranger-supplied grass pellets resting in Jordan's palm.

Jordan held his right hand steady and open. The wallaby's soft, warm nose tickled the center of his palm as it nibbled the pellets one by one—while ten feet away, a six-foot-tall male eastern grey kangaroo stretched out on its side in the sun like a sleepy dog, casually scratching its ribs with one paw.

"Hold right there, J—don't move a muscle!" **Aubrie** whispered in pure delight as **Laura** and **Lauren** snapped a dozen photographs of the wallaby eating right out of Jordan's hand with the distant arch of **The Sydney Harbour Arch Bridge** framed between the gum trees behind him.

Further down the boardwalk at the **Eucalyptus Koala Sanctuary**, where an elevated timber ramp brought Jordan's chair level with the upper branches of the red gum trees, a fuzzy, silver-gray **koala** with round tufted ears woke briefly from its twenty-hour daily nap, blinked sleepily at Jordan from three feet away, Munched two eucalyptus leaves in slow motion, and promptly curled back into a ball around the tree fork.

<aac>Sleeps twenty hours a day in a quiet tree, avoids loud crowds, and only eats one specific food that never changes,</aac> Jordan's `"Sydney"` voice observed dryly as **Zoë** and **Aubrie** burst out laughing beside his chair. <aac>I think the koala might be the fourth autistic member of our group.</aac>

#### July 28, 2015 • 11:00 AM — The Three Sisters Lookout and the Glass-Floored Jamison Valley Skyway

Ever since Sarah's Uncle Mick had teased her at the Liverpool backyard barbecue about how *"the furthest west Sarah's ever been in her life is the Blue Mountains cable car,"* **Mark**, **Madison**, and **Lauren** had refused to let the subject drop.

So on Tuesday morning of their second week in New South Wales—four days before their flight into the **Northern Territory**—**Sarah Braithwaite** announced that before **Jessica** took them into the real Outback, she was taking the entire family up to *"Sarah's Frontier"*: the **Blue Mountains** world heritage wilderness sixty-five miles west of Sydney.

At **Sydney Central Station**, Jordan tapped his **`HarbourCard`** and led the eighteen travelers aboard a step-free **Transit NSW Blue Mountains Line** intercity train. For two hours, the train climbed steadily westward out of the coastal plain, winding along dramatic sandstone ridges and deep eucalyptus gorges until they rolled off at `3,336 feet` above sea level at **Katoomba Station**, where a wheelchair-accessible local bus carried them down to the cliff rim at **Echo Point**.

Because of the elevation high in the Great Dividing Range, the July winter air at Katoomba was a brisk, crystal-clear forty-six degrees Fahrenheit (`8°C`), smelling intensely of cool mountain pine and peppermint eucalyptus oil.

Rolling out onto the wide, step-free stone viewing terrace of **Echo Point**, Jordan stopped his power chair at the glass-and-steel cliff railing and looked out over one of the grandest panoramas on the Australian continent.

Dropping nearly a thousand feet straight down below his front wheels was the vast, primeval expanse of the **Jamison Valley**—an endless carpet of dark green eucalyptus rainforest stretching for twenty miles toward the flat-topped tableland of **Mount Solitary**. Rising directly beside the lookout like three colossal, weather-sculpted sandstone towers stood the **Three Sisters** (*`Meehni`*, *`Wimlah`*, and *`Gunnedoo`* in Indigenous **Gundungurra** and **Darug** tradition), glowing warm ochre and gold against the deep blue haze hanging in the valley air.

"Wait—the air in the canyon really *is* blue!" **Hannah** marveled, leaning over the railing beside **Mark** and **Aubrie**.

"Rayleigh scattering through microscopic droplets of volatile **terpenoid eucalyptus oil** released by millions of gum trees across the valley," **Zoë** said aloud at the exact same second **Jordan** typed on his **Pinnacle Vanguard Pro**:

<aac>Rayleigh scattering through microscopic droplets of volatile terpenoid eucalyptus oil released by millions of gum trees across the valley.</aac>

Both of them grinned at their near-simultaneous harmony and high-fived across his right armrest.

Ten minutes along the level clifftop boardwalk from Echo Point stood the exact landmark Uncle Mick had joked about: the **Jamison Valley Skyway**.

"Alright, city girl, lead the way onto your frontier cable car!" **Jessica** teased warmly, resting an elbow on Sarah's shoulder as the attendant opened the wide automatic glass doors of the **Skyway** cabin.

Engineered with a 100% flush, zero-step entry platform, the massive aerial cabin glided out from the cliff terminal on heavy steel cables—suspending all eighteen of them **two hundred and seventy meters (`885 feet`) in mid-air** directly above the rainforest canopy between the two sandstone cliffs of the gorge.

And right down the center of the cabin floor ran a strip of solid, electrochromic panels that turned from frosted white to **completely transparent glass** the moment the cable car cleared the cliff edge.

"Whoa—don't look down if you're scared of heights!" **Caleb** laughed, taking a hasty step back onto the solid steel side deck as the tree fern crowns appeared nearly nine hundred feet straight below his boots.

**Jordan**, **Aubrie**, and **Jessica** didn't step back an inch.

Jordan drove his 350-pound power chair right onto the center of the structural glass floor panel, looking straight down past his footrests at the tiny silver ribbon of the valley creek nine hundred feet below and across at the thundering multi-tiered veil of **Katoomba Falls** plunging down the sheer cliff wall.

<aac>Eight hundred and eighty-five feet of air right under my wheels,</aac> Jordan's `"Sydney"` voice announced gleefully as **Sarah** and **Lauren** stood on the glass beside him for a family photo. <aac>Okay, Sarah, I have to admit—even for a city girl's frontier, this is a ten out of ten.</aac>

"Thank you, J!" Sarah laughed triumphantly, throwing her arms around Jordan's shoulders. "Which means I am officially ready to survive **Petermann** on Saturday!"

### Part 2: Uluṟu & The Track to Gallagher's Roadhouse

**Date:** 2015-08-01 at 11:30 Australia/Darwin

On the first morning of August, thirty minutes before their **Southern Cross Airways** jet began its descent into **Red Centre Desert Airport (`AYQ`)** in the heart of Australia's **Northern Territory**, **Jordan Fuller** looked out his oval cabin window at the vast, rust-red expanse of the Central Desert.

Rising solitary and immense from the flat crimson plain below was the ancient sandstone monolith of **Uluṟu**, glowing like a deep ember beneath the cloudless winter sun.

Across the aisle, **Jessica Gallagher** leaned over and spoke quietly to Jordan, Daniel, and the rest of the family.

"Out there is **Uluṟu**," Jessica said, her voice carrying deep respect. "A lot of tourists fly into this airstrip thinking it's just a big rock to climb for a holiday snapshot. Back in 2015, the chain up the steep sandstone face hasn't been permanently closed yet, so you'll still see ignorant people scrambling up the forty-six-degree cliff. But to the **Aṉangu** people—the traditional custodians who have lived on this land for tens of thousands of years—that monolith is sacred law, or *Tjukurpa*. The Aṉangu elders ask every visitor at the base to respect their law and not climb."

Jordan didn't hesitate for a single second.

Opening the master itinerary file inside **`NeoEdit`** on his **Pinnacle Vanguard Pro**, Jordan typed a formal executive directive and transmitted it to every phone and tablet in their eighteen-person party—a timestamped document that **Ms. Helen Gable** would enter seventeen days later in Courtroom 3B as **Respondent's Exhibit E**:

> **EXECUTIVE ITINERARY DIRECTIVE — LEG 7 (NORTHERN TERRITORY)**<br>
> **Issued By:** Jordan Fuller (Chief Navigator)<br>
> **Timestamp:** `2015-08-01 11:12 ACST`<br>
> **Directive:** Out of respect for the **Aṉangu** traditional custodians and Indigenous law, all eighteen members of our expedition will strictly honor the request of the Aṉangu elders. No member of our party will set foot on the Uluṟu climb path. We will pay our respects exclusively along the level, accessible base cultural trail and proceed directly to **Gallagher's Roadhouse** in **Petermann**.

"Unanimously approved, Chief Navigator," **Daniel** said warmly, resting a hand on Jordan's shoulder as the aircraft tires touched down on the desert runway at **Red Centre Desert Airport (`AYQ`)**—where **Jessica** happily carried Jordan off the plane into the bright Outback sunshine and settled him into his power chair on the tarmac.

Waiting outside the single-story bush terminal stood a rugged convoy of three heavy-duty, long-wheelbase four-wheel-drive overland rigs outfitted with steel bullbars, rooftop dual spare tires, high-mount desert air snorkels, and—on the lead vehicle—a custom hydraulic wheelchair platform lift welded onto the rear chassis.

Leaning against the lead bullbar alongside Jessica's parents, **Callum and Fiona Gallagher**, stood a young woman who made **Mark**, **Madison**, and **Sarah** do an immediate double-take.

She was six feet three inches tall, broad-shouldered, and heavily muscled, wearing grease-stained work boots, khaki canvas cargo trousers, and a sleeveless flannel work shirt—and her sun-bronzed face and braided blonde hair were a carbon-copy mirror image of **Jessica**.

"Everyone," Jessica grinned as she strode across the red gravel and swept her identical twin sister into a bone-crushing bear hug, "meet my twin sister, **Rebecca—'Bec'—Gallagher**, chief diesel mechanic of Petermann!"

"G'day, legends!" **Bec** boomed, her Northern Territory drawl identical to Jessica's as she shook Daniel's hand and walked right up to Jordan's power chair with a huge, grease-smudged grin. "Jessica told me you've got a three-hundred-and-fifty-pound high-torque beast of a rig here, Jordan! Wait till you see the steel treadplate ramp Dad and I welded onto the homestead verandah—you could drive a road train up it!"

<aac>Seeing two six-foot-three Gallaghers at the same time is breaking my optical sensors,</aac> Jordan's `"Sydney"` voice joked, making both twins roar with laughter. <aac>Thank you for building the ramp, Bec.</aac>

After pausing respectfully along the level, red-sand base cultural trail of **Uluṟu** to admire the ancient rock art caves and read the **Aṉangu** cultural plaques, the convoy turned west onto the **Great Central Road (*Tjukaruru Road*)**.

Ten minutes past the boundary, the asphalt ended completely.

Callum and Bec pulled the three 4WD rigs onto the shoulder and used portable deflators to drop the air pressure in every 10-ply off-road tire down to twenty-six pounds per square inch (`psi`) to absorb the brutal, washboard-like iron-oxide corrugations of the unsealed red-dirt track. Twenty minutes later, the last bar of cellular service vanished from every screen in the convoy.

For three solid hours, they drove deeper and deeper into the vast **Petermann** bush—passing towering red sand dunes, silver-green desert oaks, and thorny spinifex grass—until the corrugated-iron roof, towering rainwater tanks, solar array, and high-flow diesel bowsers of **Gallagher's Roadhouse** rose out of the crimson plain like an oasis at the edge of the earth.

True to Bec's word, welded seamlessly onto the wide, shaded timber-and-steel verandah of the Gallagher family homestead sat a massive, zero-lip steel diamond-plate ramp. Jordan gripped his joystick and drove his 350-pound power chair straight up onto the verandah to the sound of eighteen voices cheering across the silent desert.

### Part 3: Frost on the Tires & The Royal Flying Doctor Service

**Date:** 2015-08-05 at 06:15 Australia/Darwin

![At 6:15 AM freezing winter dawn outside Gallagher's Roadhouse in the Petermann Outback of the Northern Territory, Australia (Respondent's Exhibit D), a crystalline layer of white winter frost coats the rust-red iron-oxide desert dirt, spinifex grass, and the thick rubber tire treads and casters of clean-shaven Jordan Fuller's matte-black S.S. Freedom power wheelchair at the foot of the custom-welded steel diamond-plate verandah ramp, while identical six-foot-three blonde Australian twin sisters Jessica and Bec Gallagher stand proudly behind him in warm Outback work jackets as their breath rises in the 27.8-degree Fahrenheit dawn air.]({{CDN}}/raggiesoft-books/images/scenes/aubrie/e004/c010/s002/outback-frost-tires.jpg)

#### August 5, 2015 • 6:15 AM — Twenty-Eight Degrees at Dawn (Frost on the Tires)

Out at **Gallagher's Roadhouse**—the final outpost of fuel, artesian bore water, and mechanical repair before three hundred kilometers of uninhabited desert scrub stretching toward the Western Australian border—life ran on strict seasonal physics.

During the afternoon, the **August winter** weather was brisk and glorious: sixty-eight degrees Fahrenheit (`20°C`) under a dome of blindingly clear blue sky with bone-dry ten percent relative humidity. And it was out on the packed red-dirt yard and bush tracks around the compound that **Daniel** and **Jordan** discovered an unexpected mechanical triumph.

Back in Virginia the previous autumn, Daniel had ordered Jordan's matte-black, three-hundred-and-fifty-pound power wheelchair with over-specced high-torque brushless motors, heavy-duty coil-over active suspension, and deep-lugged pneumatic tires purely so Jordan could climb the steep Appalachian grades of **Bennett Hill** and the **Academic Quadrangle** at **CPI** in Blacksburg. Neither of them had ever imagined that engineering a wheelchair for the mountains of Southwest Virginia would inadvertently turn it into a legitimate **Northern Territory bush rig**—capable of rolling across Petermann red gravel and spinifex tracks without a single wheel slip.

Every afternoon at three-thirty, before the sun began to sink, Jordan rolled into the multi-bay **Mechanical & Welding Workshop**—Jessica and Bec's domain—where the twins taught him the daily discipline of **Bulldust Purge**.

"Out here in the Red Centre, the dirt isn't sand—it's iron-oxide bulldust ground finer than talcum powder," **Bec** explained, handing Jordan the insulated nozzle of the workshop's industrial air compressor while wearing her safety goggles. "If you leave fine red dust sitting inside your actuator seals and motor housings overnight, the pre-dawn winter frost and condensation will turn it into red cement by morning. Give those housings a clean thirty-psi blowout from the inside out."

Wearing his own safety glasses and work gloves, Jordan methodically directed the compressed-air jet across his dual motor housings, suspension pivots, and wheel bearings, blasting clouds of rust-red dust out onto the concrete workshop apron until the metal shone clean.

At four-thirty every afternoon, **Callum and Fiona Gallagher** initiated **Sundown Thermal Protocol**.

Because the Central Desert air held almost zero moisture and zero cloud cover to trap the day's warmth, the moment the sun dropped below the western horizon, the heat radiated straight out into space. Within four hours, the temperature plummeted nearly **fifty degrees Fahrenheit**.

After dinner around the blazing mulga-wood fire pit—where the family ate Fiona's homemade meat pies and drank hot billy tea—Callum cut the main yard floodlights so the diesel generators could throttle down into night-quiet mode.

Looking up from his power chair in the freezing, crystal-clear desert darkness, **Jordan**—the rising sophomore Astrophysics major—was left completely breathless.

With zero light pollution for hundreds of kilometers and zero summer heat haze in the sub-freezing winter air, the **Bortle Class 1** night sky blazed overhead with a brilliance Jordan had only ever seen in space-telescope photographs. Arching from horizon to horizon hung the blazing core of the **Milky Way**, the cuatro-star diamond of the **Southern Cross (`Crux`)**, the ink-black silhouette of the **Coalsack Dark Nebula**, and two entire neighboring dwarf galaxies visible to the naked eye: the **Large and Small Magellanic Clouds**.

```

```

The next morning at six-fifteen—just as the first pink and gold light of dawn touched the desert horizon—Jordan dressed in his merino wool base layers, his insulated windproof jacket, and his thermal gloves, unplugged his chair's insulated battery charger from the homestead generator circuit, and rolled down the steel treadplate ramp onto the forecourt alongside **Daniel**, **Jessica**, and **Lauren**.

The calibrated digital weather station mounted to the roadhouse verandah post read **`27.8°F (-2.3°C)`** on **`August 5, 2015`**.

Stretching across the entire compound, a thick, sparkling blanket of **white winter frost** coated the iron-oxide red dirt, the spinifex clumps, the steel fuel bowsers, and the deep rubber treads of Jordan's wheelchair tires.

"Look at that—white ice on red desert sand in the middle of August," **Daniel** murmured, pulling out his camera as **Lauren** held up the roadhouse's digital thermometer display next to Jordan's frost-rimmed front casters. "Smile, Jordan. Let's take a few timestamped shots for the family album."

Neither Jordan nor Daniel knew it at six-fifteen that frosty Wednesday morning, but the geolocated photographs they snapped of white winter frost coating Jordan's wheelchair tires at twenty-eight degrees Fahrenheit were about to become **Respondent's Exhibit D**—the exact piece of physical evidence that would obliterate **Aubrie Sinclair** and **Mr. Davies** on the record in a Virginia courtroom thirteen days later.

***

#### August 5, 2015 • 9:30 PM — Bortle Class One: The Galactic Center Overhead

By nine-thirty that Wednesday night—fifteen hours after Daniel and Lauren had photographed the twenty-eight-degree morning frost coating Jordan's wheelchair tires at dawn—the temperature outside **Gallagher's Roadhouse** was already plunging back toward the freezing mark.

Out by the mulga-wood fire pit, **Fiona Gallagher** had handed out steaming enamel mugs of hot **Milo** malted chocolate and wrapped thick Australian merino wool blankets around the shoulders of the eighteen travelers. Then, at nine-thirty sharp, **Callum** and **Bec Gallagher** walked over to the generator shed and flipped the exterior compound floodlights off, dropping the diesel generators into whisper-quiet night mode.

Instantly, the darkness of the **Central Australian Desert**—three hundred kilometers from the nearest town streetlight—descended around the homestead, and the sky overhead exploded into light.

Wait-free and completely stable on the wide timber verandah, **Callum**, **Jessica**, and **Bec** had bolted a custom, heavy-duty steel mounting pier at exact wheelchair eye height to hold the roadhouse's twelve-inch aperture **Dobsonian reflector telescope**, coupled with a digital CCD camera adapter that piped the live eyepiece feed directly onto **Jordan's** and **Aubrie's** screens so the entire twenty-two-person circle could see every deep-sky object together.

For **Jordan Fuller** and **Aubrie Jean Kelly**—two rising sophomore **Astrophysics** majors who had spent their entire lives at **`37° North Latitude`** in Virginia—looking up at the winter sky from **`25° South Latitude`** in a **Bortle Class 1** dark-sky sanctuary was like opening their eyes to the universe for the very first time.

In Virginia, the northern hemisphere pointed outward toward the sparser outer spiral arms of the Milky Way, and the bright **Galactic Center** in the constellation **Sagittarius** never rose more than thirty degrees above the murky southern horizon haze.

Here in the **Northern Territory** in August, the **Galactic Center of the Milky Way** passed **directly overhead at the zenith**.

"Look straight up, J," **Aubrie** whispered, her breath rising in a tiny white cloud in the thirty-four-degree desert air as her gloved hand squeezed Jordan's shoulder, her hazel eyes reflecting the starlight. "You don't even need the telescope to see the dust lanes. It's bright enough to cast a shadow on the red dirt."

She wasn't exaggerating. Stretching from the northeastern horizon straight across the crown of the sky to the southwest hung a blazing, three-dimensional river of silver-gold starlight, cleft down the middle by the dramatic dark dust rifts of the **Great Rift** and the ink-black silhouette of the **Coalsack Dark Nebula** tucked right beside the four jewel-like stars of the **Southern Cross (`Crux`)**.

Jordan slewed the telescope barrel smoothly on its Teflon azimuth bearings, locking onto three targets he had dreamed of seeing since he was ten years old reading astronomy books alone in his bedroom in Virginia Beach:

First, **`NGC 4755`—The Jewel Box Open Cluster (`Kappa Crucis`)**, a glittering cluster of supergiant stars fifteen million years old where a brilliant ruby-red supergiant blazed in the center of dozens of sapphire-blue and emerald-white stars like a handful of gemstones scattered on black velvet.

Second, **`Omega Centauri` (`NGC 5139`)**, a colossal globular cluster sixteen thousand light-years away containing **ten million stars** packed into a single gravitationally bound sphere so dense that its core filled the entire wide-field eyepiece with a solid dome of diamond dust.

And third—visible right to the naked eye above the southern horizon—two entire neighboring dwarf galaxies orbiting the Milky Way: the **Large Magellanic Cloud (`163,000 light-years`)** and the **Small Magellanic Cloud (`200,000 light-years`)**, with the pink-and-silver spiderweb filaments of the **Tarantula Nebula** glowing inside the larger cloud.

Beside Jordan's wheelchair, **Zoë's** runtime console recorded the moment:

<aac>Look at the light from the Large Magellanic Cloud on the screen,</aac> Jordan's `"Sydney"` voice spoke softly into the hushed desert night as **Callum**, **Fiona**, **Bec**, **Jessica**, **Sarah**, **Lauren**, **Madison**, **Zoë**, **Hannah**, **Mark**, **Daniel**, **Laura**, and the **Brooks** siblings leaned in around the monitor. <aac>Those photons left those stars one hundred and sixty-three thousand years ago, traveled across intergalactic space for a sextillion miles, and tonight—because I have my glasses and I am standing here with all of you—they landed right in my eyes.</aac>

Aubrie leaned down, kissed Jordan's cold cheek warmly, and rested her forehead against his temple under the blazing arch of the Southern Cross.

#### August 9, 2015 • 3:30 AM — The Satellite Phone at Three-Thirty in the Morning

At three-thirty on Sunday morning in the **Northern Territory**—while the outside desert temperature sat at twenty-six degrees below freezing and the entire roadhouse compound slept in dead silence—the fixed **satellite telephone** inside the Gallagher homestead office began to ring.

Because three-thirty in the morning in Central Australia (`UTC+09:30`) was **two o'clock on Saturday afternoon** in **Christiansburg, Virginia** (`UTC-04:00`), only an urgent call from the East Coast of the United States would ever come through the homestead's fixed satellite dish at that hour.

**Daniel Brooks** was awake and in the office within four rings.

Ten minutes later, a soft knock sounded on the door of the accessible homestead donga suite shared by **Jordan**, **Mark**, **Aubrie**, and **Zoë**.

When Jordan transferred into his power chair with Mark's quiet help and rolled out into the warm homestead kitchen, he found **Daniel**, **Laura**, and **Jessica** gathered around the heavy timber table with steaming mugs of tea while the satellite data terminal hummed on the desk behind them.

"Everything is completely under control, Jordan," **Daniel** said immediately, his voice calm, steady, and transparent as he pulled out a chair beside Jordan's right armrest. "Five minutes ago, our next-door neighbor on Geneva Street in Christiansburg called our emergency satellite number. At two o'clock this afternoon Virginia time, a private process server knocked on our front door in Christiansburg attempting to serve legal papers."

Jordan's hands remained completely still over his keyboard. His heart rate ticked up slightly, but the old terror that used to paralyze him at the mention of his mother was gone.

<aac>My mother,</aac> Jordan typed cleanly. <aac>What did she file?</aac>

"She hired a Virginia Beach attorney named **Mr. Davies** and filed an emergency petition in the **Montgomery County Circuit Court** seeking full adult **Guardianship and Conservatorship** over your person and your estate," Daniel explained, laying a faxed summary sheet from his legal team on the table. "She is claiming to the court that you are an incapacitated adult with the cognitive comprehension of a young child, and that Laura and I 'abducted' and 'endangered' you by taking you out of the country. Worse yet, Mr. Davies actually tried to get **Judge Harrison** to schedule an immediate hearing *this week while we are still in Australia*—hoping to win a default guardianship order *in absentia* while we were ten thousand miles away."

Around the kitchen table, **Aubrie**, **Zoë**, and **Mark** stiffened with protective fury—and then all four of them looked at Jordan.

Instead of crashing into a `System.IO.FileNotFoundException()`, Jordan looked down at the calendar on his **Pinnacle Vanguard Pro** screen and ran the math.

<aac>Wait—we bought these airline tickets back in the winter, five months before she filed anything,</aac> Jordan's `"Sydney"` voice stated with crystal clarity. <aac>Our starting flight out of Roanoke to Dulles was on May 23, and our pre-booked return flights from Red Centre Desert Airport (`AYQ`) to Sydney (`SYD`) to Los Angeles (`LAX`) to Charlotte (`CLT`) to Roanoke (`ROA`) depart on August 16 and land at Roanoke-Blacksburg Regional Airport at 6:30 PM on Monday, August 17. Did Ms. Gable show the judge when our tickets were purchased?</aac>

A slow, fiercely proud smile spread across **Daniel's** face.

"That is the exact first move **Ms. Helen Gable** and your court-appointed **Guardian ad Litem**, **Ms. Evelyn Caldwell**, made in chambers this afternoon," Daniel replied. "The moment Mr. Davies demanded an immediate August hearing date claiming we had 'fled the jurisdiction,' Ms. Gable and Ms. Caldwell handed Judge Harrison the certified airline ticket receipts and Passenger Name Records for all eighteen of us—showing both our outbound **May 23 `ROA ➔ IAD`** departure and our confirmed **August 16–17 `AYQ ➔ SYD ➔ LAX ➔ CLT ➔ ROA`** return itinerary, along with the bank clearing timestamps proving that every single ticket was purchased and ticketed back in **January and February 2015**, half a year before your mother ever set foot in a lawyer's office. Judge Harrison took one look at the January ticketing dates, shut down Mr. Davies's attempt to hold a hearing while you were in Australia on the spot, denied her request for an *ex parte* seizure order, and docketed the full evidentiary hearing on the merits for **Tuesday, August 18 at 9:30 AM** in **Courtroom 3B** in Christiansburg—fifteen hours after our pre-booked flight touches down at `ROA`."

<aac>So we do not need to cut our trip short by a single hour,</aac> Jordan typed, his green eyes bright behind his glasses.

"Not by a single minute," Daniel confirmed warmly. "Ms. Gable and Ms. Caldwell both agreed: if we scrambled to buy emergency change tickets and fled home early, your mother's lawyer would claim we were panicking. By finishing the exact two-week Outback educational itinerary we booked back in the winter and rolling into Courtroom 3B on Tuesday morning right on schedule, we prove that your life runs on calm, deliberate order."

Beside Jordan, **Zoë's** eyes gleamed behind her glasses as her cognitive logger compiled the entire courtroom defense matrix in real time:
