Inside the quiet back booth of the **`Rocket Burger`**, after Sarah held Jordan over fries and milkshakes until his breathing steadied, **Zoë** presented the new zero-`I-64` route: `State Route 285` to `U.S. 250` up to the **Afton Overlook**, and `U.S. Route 60 West` through Buena Vista to Lexington on the way home. Refusing to let his mother's ghost steal their Fall Break, Jordan moved into the middle row of Daniel's minivan between **Aubrie Jean** and **Zoë**, and twenty minutes later, rolled *S.S. Freedom* out onto the stone terrace of the **Afton Overlook**—gazing out over the vast golden sea of the Shenandoah Valley wrapped safely in the arms of his entire family.

***

#### October 17, 2015 • 5:15 PM — The 100.1°F Fever & The Aethelian Tome Box Set

By the time the three-car caravan returned down `U.S. 60` and pulled back into the driveway at **414 Geneva Street** late Saturday afternoon, Jordan was deeply, bone-wearily depleted.

Down in the walk-out basement sanctuary, he transferred onto the queen bed between **Aubrie Jean** and **Madison**, resting his head between them as Aubrie Jean gently steered his mind toward the calm, predictable mathematics of **`PHYS 2305`**—talking quietly about electron-degenerate matter and the helium flash inside red giant stars until his tremors finally stopped. Lying between the two young women who had held his universe together since his very first morning in Room 214, Jordan looked at them with profound clarity: *they were his autistic safe people.*

Then, at `5:30 PM`, when Laura called downstairs that dinner was ready and Jordan pushed himself up on the edge of the mattress, the room spun violently around him.

"Whoa," Madison said, catching his elbow immediately and pressing the back of her hand against his flushed forehead. "J, you're burning up."

**Hannah** and **Isabel** hurried over with the digital thermometer from the medical kit. Sixty seconds later, the thermometer beeped: **`100.1°F`**.

Coming downstairs with Daniel, **Laura** took one look at the reading and nodded with calm maternal understanding. "This isn't from the highway, sweetheart," Laura told him gently. "Because your mother refused to vaccinate you for eighteen years, your immune system is still working through your catch-up immunization schedule and building its armor. You caught an autumn viral bug—and when the panic about that `CP87A` tax letter hit right on top of the fever, your body just hit the wall."

Dinner was immediately converted into a sick-ward perimeter: chicken noodle soup, saltine crackers, and cold dry ginger ale brought down on a tray while Daniel reminded Jordan that their indexed **IRS Audit Binder** was already sitting on the shelf upstairs waiting to crush his mother's tax fraud with hard facts.

With Sunday's outdoor plans officially scrubbed by Jordan's fever, **Mark** walked over to the basement media shelves, paused, and pulled down a massive, foil-embossed Blu-ray box set with a look of sheer reverence.

"No. Way," Mark breathed, holding the box set up to the light. "***The Silver Gauntlet of Aethel: 25th Anniversary Definitive Aethelian Tome Edition***."

"Oh, I *love* that movie!" Hannah gasped. "That `'A Sister's Love'` synth theme song is pure 1980s cheesy fantasy bliss!"

"This isn't the hundred-minute 1987 theatrical cut, ladies," Mark announced solemnly. "This is the 2012 four-disc Blu-ray restoration. This is the legendary **Leviathan Cut**—*twelve hours and twenty-one minutes* long."

***

#### October 18, 2015 • 9:00 AM — The Leviathan Cut (12 Hours and 21 Minutes)

On Sunday morning, October 18, with Jordan's fever hovering at `99.8°F` and the entire household camped out in pajamas across the basement sectional and beds with trays of Laura's oatmeal, lunchtime sandwiches, and an evening feast of baked ziti, Mark pressed `Play` on Disc 1 (*Book I: The Sundering of Sunstead* and *Book II: The Shadow's Heart*).

Cocooned between Aubrie Jean, Madison, and Isabel, Jordan was completely mesmerized—not only by how the twelve-hour *Leviathan Cut* restored **Lord Malakor's** entire origin story, the twins **Kaelan and Kaela's** cramped childhood sharing a single shepherd's hut bed (which made the Room 214 trio exchange a deeply knowing look), and Kaela's secret psychological rebellion inside the Shadowspire, but by **Klaus Richter's** soaring 1980s synthesizer score and **Jareth Blade's** rock-opera anthems. By Sunday night, as his fever broke and all six women of the Pact piled around him on the sectional sofa in a warm puppy pile, Jordan turned to **Zoë**, took her hand, and thanked her from the bottom of his soul for opening her childhood home to him—inviting Zoë to share his bed that night in quiet, loving gratitude for the family that had saved his life.

## Friday, 9:32 AM: The Broken Foundation & The Failed Angioplasty

### Part 1: Friday, 9:32 AM (The Attack) & The Wrong Bus on Commonwealth Mall

**Date:** 2015-11-13 at 09:32 America/New_York

![Inside the back accessible row of the Walton Hall lecture auditorium at CPI, nineteen-year-old Jordan Fuller slumps in acute cardiac distress in his matte-black S.S. Freedom power wheelchair clutching his sternum beside a dropped water bottle, while Mark drops to one knee to steady his shoulder, Aubrie Jean Kelly holds his hand in terror, Madison Scott wipes his brow, Zoë Wren Brooks urgently calls 911 dispatch, and Lauren and Hannah clear the lecture hall aisle behind them.]({{CDN}}/raggiesoft-books/images/scenes/aubrie/e006/c003/p001/walton-hall-stemi-emergency.jpg)

#### 9:32 AM — Friday, 9:32 AM (The Attack)

Friday morning, November 13, 2015—two months into a happy, thriving autumn of classes, quiet evenings with **Isabel** and the Pact in the walk-out basement on Geneva Street, and steady progress toward Thanksgiving break—began like any bright, ordinary morning of their new life.

There was laughter in the sunlit upstairs kitchen at `414 Geneva Street` as **Laura** and **Daniel** handed out warm travel mugs before leaving for work. There was the smooth, familiar ten-second roll up the low-floor ramp of the **`6:00 AM` Blue Ridge Transit Route 1** bus, the fifteen-minute wait on **Commonwealth Mall**, and a warm breakfast together at **Kincaid Commons**, where Isabel stopped by their booth in her clinical nursing scrubs to kiss Jordan good morning before heading to her `8:00 AM` rehabilitation practicum lab in Callahan Hall.

By `8:50 AM`, the nine commuters had filed into the massive, three-hundred-seat tiered auditorium of **Walton Hall** for **`SOC 101` (`Introductory Sociology`)** and assembled their usual back-row **Sociology Fortress**: **Mark** and **Hannah** anchoring the outer aisle flank, **Lauren**, **Sarah**, **Jessica**, and **Zoë** holding the middle seats, and **Jordan** parked in the wide accessible wheelchair cutout at the end of the row with **Aubrie Jean** in a movable companion chair on his right and **Madison** in the fixed auditorium seat on his left.

At `9:00 AM` sharp, the professor stepped up to the lectern and began a Friday morning lecture on social stratification. Jordan reached under the table and laced his right fingers warmly through Aubrie Jean's hand, feeling completely safe, completely loved, and completely free.

His mind was finally safe.

*His body, however, was still carrying a nineteen-year-old time bomb.*

For nearly two decades under **Aubrie Sinclair's** roof, Jordan's cardiovascular and endocrine systems had been subjected to relentless, unremitting biological warfare: eighteen years of chronic fight-or-flight cortisol floods, terrifying psychological abuse, forced immobility, weaponized nutritional and metabolic neglect, and untreated vascular inflammation. Even though his soul had found sanctuary in Christiansburg, the structural damage etched into his coronary arteries over nineteen years of terror had been silently waiting to give way.

At `9:25 AM`—twenty-five minutes into the lecture—Jordan felt a strange, unfamiliar sensation in the center of his chest.

At first, he thought it was just indigestion from breakfast or a brief wave of sensory fatigue.

*No. This isn't anxiety.*

Within ninety seconds, the sensation deepened into a heavy, suffocating, vise-like pressure right behind his breastbone—as if someone were stacking concrete blocks one after another onto his ribs. A sudden wave of violent nausea rolled through his stomach. Cold, clammy sweat broke out across his forehead and the back of his neck, soaking the collar of his shirt, and a dull, searing ache began radiating upward from his chest into the left side of his jaw.

Then, at `9:30 AM`, his entire left arm went dead numb from his shoulder to his fingertips.

The plastic water bottle he had been holding in his left hand slipped through his slack fingers and hit the concrete floor with a loud, hollow *thud*.

Shaking, gasping for air that refused to fill his lungs, Jordan let go of Aubrie Jean's hand and pressed his right palm flat against the center of his sternum, rubbing hard at his chest as if he could physically push the crushing weight away, before his trembling hand moved up to grip his aching jaw.

Beside him, Aubrie Jean felt Jordan pull his hand away and saw him clutch his chest. Every drop of color drained from her face.

"J? Jordan, what's wrong?!" Aubrie Jean whispered, her eyes wide with alarm as she gripped his right forearm.

On his other side, Madison leaned in immediately, her own face going pale as she saw the beads of ice-cold sweat rolling down Jordan's temples. "Is it a panic attack? J, look at me, breathe with me—"

Jordan tried to shake his head, his chest heaving in shallow, ragged gasps as a high-pitched ringing filled his ears and the tiered auditorium began to tilt and spin. With his left arm hanging uselessly against the armrest, he dragged his trembling right thumb across the screen of his mounted **MagnaByte `mPad`** AAC tablet and hit two emergency tiles:

<aac>Chest. Hurts.</aac>

Four seats down the row, Mark had been taking notes on his laptop when the clatter of the dropped water bottle and the frantic, unnatural motion of Jordan's right hand caught the corner of his eye.

Mark looked over. He saw Jordan press his palm hard against the center of his sternum, saw the drenching, clammy gray pallor of his skin, and then saw Jordan's hand slide up to clutch the angle of his left jaw.

Mark's blood turned to ice water.

*He had seen that exact posture once before in his life—the afternoon his fifty-eight-year-old uncle collapsed in the driveway.*

*No,* Mark's mind screamed, rejecting the thought. *He's nineteen years old. You don't have a heart attack at nineteen. Wait—the cold sweat, the crushing chest pressure, the jaw pain, his left arm hanging limp—*

Mark didn't wait another second. Shoving his laptop aside, he scrambled past Hannah, Sarah, and Zoë and dropped to one knee in the aisle directly in front of *S.S. Freedom*.

"Jordan?! Jordan, look at me!" Mark said, his voice low and razor-sharp as he touched Jordan's ice-cold, sweat-drenched cheek.

Jordan's emerald-green eyes were glassy and unfocused, his lips turning a faint, terrifying blue-gray as he slumped sideways against the padded bolster of his wheelchair, his right hand still clawed over his sternum.

Mark's disbelief vanished, replaced by sheer, agonizing certainty.

*It is. It's a heart attack.*

**"Zoë, call 911! NOW!"** Mark's shout cut straight through the professor's lecture, freezing all three hundred students in the auditorium.

Aubrie Jean let out a choked cry of pure terror, dropping to her knees beside Jordan's wheel and holding his head as Madison began sobbing and wiping his brow with her sleeve. Mark didn't even wait for Zoë's phone to connect—he vaulted into the main aisle and sprinted full-speed down the steep auditorium steps toward the stage, waving both arms over his head.

**"Professor!"** Mark yelled, his voice cracking with panic. **"Jordan's having a heart attack! We need 911! We need help right now!"**

Down at the podium, the sociology professor took one look at the sheer terror on Mark's face and the commotion in the back wheelchair bay and didn't hesitate for a heartbeat. Snatching up the red hardwired campus emergency handset on the lectern wall, he punched the dispatch button.

"Yes, this is Dr. Vance in `SOC 101`, **Walton Hall Main Auditorium**!" the professor barked into the receiver. "I have a student collapsing in a wheelchair in the back row—possible acute heart attack! Send paramedics and rescue immediately!"

Up in the deathly silent back row, while Lauren and Hannah held the crowd of stunned students back to give Jordan air, Zoë's trembling right hand was already talking to CPI 911 Dispatch at her ear while her left thumb executed the emergency broadcast macro across the **`Jordan Comms`** family network:

Symptoms: Crushing_Substernal_Pressure, Left_Arm_Paresthesia, Mandibular_Radiation, Diaphoresis, Pallor(Ashen_Gray). Differential_Diagnosis(Thread 4 / Mark): Acute Myocardial Infarction (STEMI). 11-13-2015 09:32:14


Mark raced back up the auditorium steps three at a time, his own heart hammering against his ribs as he knelt beside Aubrie Jean and gripped Jordan's trembling right hand.

*He's nineteen years old,* Mark thought, his mind screaming as Jordan's eyelids fluttered and a ragged, agonizing whimper escaped his throat. *He just got free. Please, God, don't let her kill him now.*

"Stay with us, J! Look at me, brother, stay right here with us!" Mark pleaded, holding Jordan's hand as Aubrie Jean pressed her tear-streaked cheek against Jordan's shoulder.

At the front of the hall, the professor set down the phone and called out over the silent room:

"Paramedics are two minutes out! Clear the center aisle and prop the exterior double doors wide open!"

***

#### 9:38 AM — Massive STEMI: The Extrication

The heavy double doors at the bottom of the **Walton Hall** auditorium burst open, and two paramedics from **Medic 3** rushed inside—the lead medic carrying a 12-lead cardiac monitor/defibrillator and a red first-in trauma bag, followed closely by two EMTs wheeling a collapsible stair chair and a rolling ambulance gurney.

"We got a call for a nineteen-year-old male with acute chest pain?!" the lead paramedic called out, scanning the steep tiers of seats.

"Up here! Back accessible row!" **Mark** yelled, waving both arms from the top aisle.

Seeing the steep concrete steps of the tiered lecture hall, the crew parked the heavy rolling gurney at the bottom doorway and sprinted up the stairs with the cardiac monitor, oxygen cylinder, and collapsible stair chair as students in the middle rows scrambled into the aisles to clear a path.

Within seconds, the paramedics knelt beside *S.S. Freedom*.

"Sir, my name's **Mike**. We're right here with you, okay?" the lead paramedic said, his voice a calm, steady anchor in the middle of the storm as he checked Jordan's radial pulse. "Can you tell me your name?"

Jordan couldn't speak, and his left arm was dead weight against the armrest, so **Aubrie Jean** answered through her tears while holding his right hand: "His name is Jordan! He's nineteen, and he's non-verbal autistic—he uses his tablet, or he can nod and shake his head!"

"Got it—thank you, ma'am. Jordan, we're going to take great care of you," Mike said immediately, turning to his partner. "Let's get him on high-flow oxygen and run a 12-lead right now."

As his partner slipped a nasal cannula over Jordan's ears and turned the oxygen regulator up, he glanced down at Jordan's pale, sweat-drenched face and obvious bariatric frame. "Nineteen?" the partner murmured, his surprise visible for only a fraction of a second before his clinical training locked in.

"Jordan, nod or shake your head for me—are you allergic to aspirin?" Mike asked clearly.

Pale and terrified, with a crushing white-hot band tightening across his sternum, Jordan managed a weak shake of his head: *No.*

"He has no drug allergies!" Mark confirmed from behind them.

"Good job, buddy," Mike said, popping four `81 mg` chewable baby aspirins into his gloved palm and lifting them to Jordan's lips. "I need you to chew all four of these up for me right now and swallow them. Don't swallow them whole—chew them up."

Jordan obeyed, grimacing at the chalky orange-bitter taste as Mike's partner unbuttoned the top of Jordan's shirt and rapidly placed the ten adhesive 12-lead EKG electrodes across his chest and limbs.

"We need a little room to work, folks—just take two steps back for me," Mike said firmly but gently as Aubrie Jean clung to Jordan's hand.

```zoe-log

```

The cardiac monitor whirred, beeped rapidly, and fed out a long pink-grid strip of thermal paper.

Mike tore the strip from the printer and held it up.

His eyes went wide. Silently, he angled the paper toward his partner, who took one look at the massive tombstone ST-segment elevations across the anterior leads and swore under his breath.

*"He's nineteen,"* the partner whispered in sheer disbelief.

"Monitor doesn't lie," Mike said, every trace of calm routine vanishing into steel-sharp urgency. "He's having a massive STEMI. We have to move. *Now.*"

Mike turned to the stunned circle of Jordan's family.

"Listen to me closely: he is having a major heart attack," Mike told them, his voice brisk and commanding. "We are transporting him emergency traffic to **New River Valley Medical Center** in Christiansburg. We're transferring him into the stair chair right now—we need this aisle completely clear."

Mark and **Hannah** stepped forward instinctively to help lift him, but the four EMS personnel moved as a single, practiced machine: unfolding the tracked stair chair, lifting Jordan smoothly out of *S.S. Freedom*, strapping him securely across the chest and shins, and tilting the chair back onto its stair-gliding tracks.

"We're coming with you!" Aubrie Jean sobbed, stumbling forward as they wheeled him into the aisle.

"We can't take passengers in the rig on a critical cardiac alert, ma'am—we need the whole cabin to work on him," Mike called back over his shoulder as the team glided rapidly down the auditorium steps toward the waiting gurney. "Meet us at New River Valley ER! We're running hot!"

***

#### 9:44 AM — The Ambulance Ride (Running Hot)

Outside the main entrance of Walton Hall, the transfer from the stair chair onto the rolling ambulance gurney was a blinding, terrifying blur of crisp November sunlight and flashing red-and-white strobe lights.

Jordan felt strong hands lifting him onto the narrow mattress and heavy nylon straps clicking tight across his chest, hips, and knees. Through the dizzying haze of pain, as they lifted the gurney into the back of **Medic 3**, he caught one last, agonizing glimpse of Aubrie Jean's tear-streaked face, Mark's pale shock—and **Lauren** and **Sarah** clutching their backpacks in horror on the brick steps.

Then the heavy double rear doors of the ambulance slammed shut.

*THUD.*

The metallic boom echoed through Jordan's skull like a vault door sealing him away from everyone who kept him safe.

For ten agonizing seconds, the ambulance didn't move. The siren wasn't even on yet.

*Why aren't we moving?!* Jordan panicked, his vision blurring as the crushing anvil on his chest made every shallow breath feel like inhaling broken glass.

Paramedic Mike was leaning right over him, switching the nasal cannula to a high-flow oxygen mask while his partner tore open an IV start kit with lightning speed. "Hang in there, Jordan, we're just getting your line established before we roll," Mike said, and a second later Jordan felt the sharp prick of an eighteen-gauge IV catheter sliding into his right forearm while the cardiac monitor beside his head beeped in a frantic, erratic staccato.

Mike keyed the shoulder microphone of his radio.

*"Dispatch, this is Medic 3,"* Mike's voice cut through the cabin, clinical and urgent. *"We are 10-23 departing CPI Walton Hall. We have a nineteen-year-old male, five-foot-seven, approximately three hundred forty pounds, presenting with a critical anterior STEMI. We are ten minutes out from New River Valley ER running Code 3—requesting immediate **Cardiac Alert and Cath Lab activation**. Vitals are—"*

The radio crackled back with a burst of static and hospital confirmation tones.

*Nineteen-year-old male. Critical STEMI. Cath Lab activation.*

Suddenly, the ambulance lurched forward into motion, and the dual-tone electronic siren ripped through the air—a deafening *WHUMP-WHUMP-WHUMP* that vibrated straight through the aluminum floor and into Jordan's bones as `Medic 3` tore out of campus toward Route 460.

And as the rig banked hard around the **Commonwealth Green** curve, a brand-new jolt of terror hit Jordan in the gut.

*My chair.*

His eyes darted wildly around the cramped ambulance bay.

*Where's my chair?!*

With a sickening lurch, Jordan realized that the paramedics had lifted him out of *S.S. Freedom* inside the auditorium and left his power wheelchair behind in Walton Hall. He was being hurtled down the highway away from his family, away from his AAC voice, and away from his own legs.

"Jordan, stay with me, buddy—keep your eyes open for me," Mike's voice sounded distant and tinny through a rising roar of tinnitus in Jordan's ears. A second later, Mike looked at the monitor and spoke sharply to his partner: *"His blood pressure is dropping—systolic's down to eighty-six. Let's push a normal saline bolus wide open and prep the nitro hold."*

Jordan felt an icy-cold rush of fluid travel up the vein in his right arm. As he squeezed his eyes shut against the searing white fire behind his breastbone, a single, heartbreaking thought echoed through the dark:

*I'm nineteen years old. I just got free. I just found my family. Please... I don't want to die.*

***

#### 9:41 AM — The Wrong Bus on Commonwealth Mall

Back outside **Walton Hall**, the wail of `Medic 3`'s siren faded rapidly toward the south exit of campus, leaving the eight of them—**Mark**, **Hannah**, **Aubrie Jean**, **Madison**, **Zoë**, **Lauren**, **Sarah**, and **Jessica**—standing frozen on the sidewalk while **Isabel** messaged frantically from her senior nursing clinical practicum across campus at Callahan Hall that she was getting emergency permission from her clinical instructor to meet them at the hospital as soon as she could.

"How do we get to the hospital?!" Aubrie Jean cried out, her whole body shaking as **Madison** held her around the waist to keep her upright. "We don't have a car on campus!"

"The `9:45 AM` *Maroon Express* is the next bus out of **Commonwealth Mall** toward Christiansburg," **Zoë** said, her voice trembling slightly as her processor fought through sheer adrenaline to build a transport vector. "We can—"

"No—a bus is too slow for all of us, and we need Daniel, Laura, and Megan at the hospital right now," **Mark** said, grabbing his and **Hannah's** backpacks. "Hannah and I are sprinting to the North End cab stand—we'll take a taxi straight to Geneva Street, grab my SUV, call Daniel, Laura, and Megan on the way, and meet you at the ER!"

"Go! Run!" **Lauren** urged.

Mark and Hannah took off at a dead sprint across the lawn. At the exact same moment, Lauren and Jessica looked back through the open glass doors of Walton Hall—where *S.S. Freedom* was still sitting empty in the back row with Jordan's **mPad** AAC tablet and backpack attached.

"We cannot leave his wheelchair behind," Lauren said fiercely, wiping a tear from her cheek. "That chair is his legs—if he wakes up in the ER and finds out his chair is stranded on campus, he's going to panic!"

"Let's get it!" Jessica barked.

In forty-five seconds flat, Lauren and Jessica dashed back inside the silent auditorium, gathered up Jordan's backpack, unlocked *S.S. Freedom*'s drive controller, and switched the speed dial to Stage 3 (`Full Outdoor Speed — 6.0 mph`). With Lauren jogging beside the right armrest and steering the joystick one-handed while Jessica guarded the left flank, the six women—**Zoë**, **Aubrie Jean**, **Madison**, **Lauren**, **Sarah**, and **Jessica**—sprinted as a single pack across the green toward the curbside bus lineup along **Commonwealth Mall** beneath **The Keystone Bridge**.

Aubrie Jean was sobbing openly as she ran, her sneakers stumbling on the brick path until Madison and Sarah caught both of her elbows and half-carried her forward.

Leading the pack by three strides, Zoë burst onto the sidewalk of **Commonwealth Mall** at `9:41:28 AM`, her eyes immediately locking onto the familiar white-and-maroon highway coach idling at the head of the curbside lineup.

### Part 2: The Emergency Room (Cardiac Trauma Bay 3) & Room 312 (Strict NPO)

**Date:** 2015-11-13 at 10:15 America/New_York

#### 10:15 AM — The Emergency Room (Cardiac Trauma Bay 3)

The ambulance gurney burst through the `AMBULANCE ONLY` automatic sliding doors of **New River Valley Medical Center** in Christiansburg, the fluorescent ceiling panels streaking past **Jordan's** vision in a blinding, sterile blur as he was wheeled straight into **Cardiac Trauma Bay 3**.

"Nineteen-year-old male, acute anterior STEMI," Paramedic **Mike** recited crisply to the attending emergency physician as four trauma nurses and orderlies slid Jordan on a draw-sheet from the ambulance cot onto the hospital trauma bed. "Onset approximately `9:25 AM` at CPI. Vitals borderline hypotensive, 12-lead in the field was conclusive, `324 mg` aspirin chewed, normal saline bolus running."

"Get him on our monitor and run a stat troponin and coagulation panel!" the attending physician ordered.

Jordan flinched as trauma shears sliced cleanly up the front of his t-shirt and sweatshirt, the cold airconditioning of the trauma bay hitting his bare chest seconds before clammy-cold hospital EKG electrodes were pressed against his skin. Another nurse drew three vials of blood from his left antecubital vein while a sublingual nitroglycerin tablet dissolved under his tongue.

He was stabilized—the crushing white-hot anvil on his chest dulling slightly into a heavy, throbbing ache—but he was completely alone, without his wheelchair and without his AAC tablet to speak.

Outside in the Emergency Department waiting room, less than four minutes later, the automatic vestibule doors hissed open as the six young women from the **`1 CBURG TRANS CTR` (`BRT Route 1`)** local bus tumbled inside with *S.S. Freedom*—arriving at the exact same moment **Daniel** and **Laura Brooks**, **Mark**, **Hannah**, and Zoë's twenty-seven-year-old eldest sister **Megan** (who had immediately paused her remote logistics job at Geneva Street to drive Mark and Hannah's overflow gear down in her four-door sedan) sprinted in from the parking lot.

"What's happening?! Where is he?!" **Aubrie Jean** cried out, her voice breaking.

Before Daniel could even reach the triage desk, the inner security doors swung open and the ER attending stepped out in blue scrubs.

"Family for Jordan Fuller?"

Daniel and Laura stepped forward immediately. "We are," Daniel said, his voice deep and steady as he held up his wallet card. "We're his parents and legal emergency contacts, and we hold his registered Virginia healthcare power of attorney."

"He's stabilized for the moment, and the interventional cardiologist is on his way down," the physician told them. "He's conscious, alert, and in sinus tachycardia, but he's terrified—and without his communication device, he's been gesturing nonstop for his family. I can let two of you back into Bay 3 right now, and you can bring his wheelchair and communication tablet with you."

"Go," Daniel said immediately, nodding to Aubrie Jean and **Zoë**.

Buzzed through the heavy security doors, Aubrie Jean and Zoë hurried down the polished linoleum corridor—with Zoë steering *S.S. Freedom* at indoor speed and Jordan's backpack (with his **mPad** AAC tablet mounted back on the swing-arm) until a trauma nurse pointed them to **Bay 3**.

Aubrie Jean pulled back the privacy curtain.

Jordan was lying propped at thirty degrees on the narrow trauma bed, still wearing his jeans and sneakers, his bare chest covered in a web of ten colored EKG leads and his nose framed by a clear oxygen cannula. Yet the second his eyes locked onto Aubrie Jean, Zoë, and *S.S. Freedom* rolling safely into the corner of the bay, a visible shudder of relief rippled through his shoulders. *They hadn't left his legs behind.*

Seeing him lying there so pale, sweaty, and vulnerable shattered the last of Aubrie Jean's composure. She rushed to the left rail of the bed, took his hand in both of hers, and burst into tears.

"Jordan! Oh, my God, J," Aubrie Jean sobbed, pressing her forehead against his knuckles. "We—we thought we were losing you..."

Then a second, ice-cold terror crept into her voice, making her whole frame tremble.

"Your mom," Aubrie Jean whispered frantically, looking up with wide, haunted eyes. "What if *she* finds out you're in the hospital? What if she comes here and tries to take you back to Virginia Beach while you can't fight back?!"

Even with his chest aching, Jordan's very first instinct was to comfort *her*. He squeezed Aubrie Jean's fingers as firmly as he could with his left hand and reached his right hand out toward Zoë.

Zoë stepped up to the right rail and took Jordan's hand instantly. Her fingers were trembling slightly from the sprint across campus, but her grip was warm and rock-steady.

Just then, the trauma nurse stepped back in with a fresh lab tray. "Just need to draw one more purple-top tube, Mr. Fuller—the cardiologist wants a repeat troponin enzyme level."

While the nurse capped the vial, Jordan tapped weakly on his rail-mounted **mPad** with his right thumb:

<aac>What happens now?</aac>

"Now we wait for the cardiologist and imaging," the nurse said kindly, patting his shoulder before stepping out.

Jordan let his head sink back against the flat, crinkly hospital pillow. He was nineteen years old. He had arrived in an ambulance with sirens screaming. His chest still throbbed with a dull, heavy ache. And now he was stuck in the universal hospital limbo: *waiting*. Ironically, the sheer mundane annoyance of waiting cut right through a fraction of his terror.

***

#### 10:45 AM — The Nuclear Medicine Lab & The Agonizing Wait

Twenty minutes later, an imaging technician pushed a transport stretcher into Bay 3, glancing at his clipboard.

"Jordan Fuller? We're going to take you down the hall to **Nuclear Medicine and Non-Invasive Cardiology** for a stat **echocardiogram**."

Jordan, Aubrie Jean, and Madison all looked up in surprise.

"An *echocardiogram*?" Madison asked, a fresh knot of anxiety tightening in her voice. "What is that?"

"It's a specialized ultrasound of his heart," the technician explained gently.

Jordan's brow furrowed, and despite his exhaustion, he tapped on his **mPad**:

<aac>An ultrasound? I thought that was how you looked at babies?</aac>

The technician gave a small, clinical smile. "Exact same sound-wave technology, different target. We aren't looking for a baby today—we're looking at your heart muscle and valves in real time to see where the wall motion is impaired and how badly the muscle was affected by the attack."

The word *damaged* hit Aubrie Jean like a physical blow; her knuckles went white around Jordan's hand.

"Can we walk with him?" Aubrie Jean asked, her voice trembling.

"You can walk alongside the stretcher down to the department, and then you'll wait right outside in the corridor for about thirty minutes while we run the scan," the tech nodded.

With Aubrie Jean walking on the left side of the stretcher and Madison on the right—their hands resting continuously on his forearms while Madison brought *S.S. Freedom* and his backpack along—they rolled down the quiet, subterranean hospital corridors to the Nuclear Medicine suite.

"We'll be right outside this door, J," Madison promised as the tech prepared to wheel him through the heavy automatic double doors. "We aren't moving an inch."

"We love you," Aubrie Jean whispered, leaning down to kiss his forehead.

The double doors hissed shut behind him, leaving the two young women alone in the silent hallway. Instantly, Aubrie Jean's knees gave out; she slid down the wall onto the linoleum floor as a fresh wave of tears broke over her, and Madison sat right down beside her, wrapping both arms tightly around her best friend as they stared at the closed doors.

Thirty agonizing minutes later, when the heavy doors finally hissed open and the tech wheeled Jordan back out—his chest wiped clean of cold ultrasound gel, his eyes wide after thirty minutes of grim clinical silence from the sonographer—Aubrie Jean scrambled to her feet and grabbed his hand before the stretcher had even cleared the doorway.

"Jordan! Are you okay?! Did it hurt? What did they say?!" Aubrie Jean gasped.

<aac>I am okay. It did not hurt. They just took pictures and said the doctor will talk to us,</aac> Jordan tapped softly, his hand immediately finding hers as they rolled back to ER Bay 3.

Once he was settled back onto the trauma bed and the curtain was drawn, another long, heavy silence descended over the bay, broken only by the rhythmic *beep... beep... beep* of the cardiac monitor. Seeing that Aubrie Jean hadn't let go of Jordan's left hand for a single second, Madison leaned over the right rail.

"Aubrie, I'm going to go update Daniel and Laura in the waiting room and switch out," Madison whispered gently, turning her gaze to Jordan. "Who do you want to see next, J?"

Jordan didn't even have to think. He was terrified of what the cardiologist was about to walk in and say, and he needed the family's unshakable moral anchor.

<aac>Hannah. I want to see Hannah.</aac>

Two minutes later, **Hannah** slipped through the curtain and quietly took the chair on Jordan's right side. Her steady, protective big-sister presence washed over the bay like a warm blanket as she rested her hand over Jordan's right forearm, sitting vigil beside him and Aubrie Jean while the minutes ticked past `11:30 AM`.

Then the curtain swept open, and the ER physician stepped back inside alongside the attending cardiologist, **Dr. Patel**. Both men wore grave expressions.

"Jordan," Dr. Patel began, speaking directly and respectfully to the nineteen-year-old in the bed. "The results from your echocardiogram and your troponin labs are back. They confirm what the paramedic's 12-lead EKG showed: you have suffered a significant anterior heart attack, and the ultrasound shows a **severe, high-grade blockage in one of your main coronary arteries**."

Beside the bed, Aubrie Jean let out a muffled, strangled sob and pressed Jordan's knuckles against her cheek.

"Because of the severity of the blockage, this isn't something we can simply manage with blood thinners and medication," Dr. Patel continued calmly. "We have to intervene mechanically to restore blood flow. Our first step is a procedure called a **coronary angiogram and balloon angioplasty** up in our Cardiac Catheterization Lab. We'll thread a thin catheter through the artery in your arm or groin up to your heart and inflate a specialized high-pressure balloon to open the blockage. We are admitting you to the inpatient cardiac unit effective immediately, and a transport team is on its way down right now."

*Admitting me. Cardiac unit. Balloon angioplasty.*

Jordan's heart raced, triggering a brief warning chime on the monitor as he looked from Aubrie Jean's tear-streaked face to Hannah's pale expression and tapped frantically on his **mPad**:

<aac>Please do not make me be alone. Can I see my family before they move me?</aac>

Seeing the raw fear in the nineteen-year-old's eyes, Dr. Patel didn't hesitate. "Your whole family is out in the waiting room?"

"Every single one of them," Hannah confirmed, her voice thick with emotion.

"I'll have the charge nurse bring all of them back right now so they can walk up to the inpatient floor with you," Dr. Patel nodded compassionately.

Sixty seconds later, the privacy curtain of Bay 3 was pulled wide open, and the small trauma bay was suddenly, overwhelmingly filled with love: **Daniel** and **Laura Brooks** hurried in first, followed immediately by **Mark**, **Madison**, **Zoë**, **Lauren**, **Sarah**, **Jessica**, **Megan** (who gave Jordan a warm, reassuring wave from beside her parents), and a breathless **Isabel**—who had just sprinted in from the parking lot in her maroon CPI clinical nursing scrubs the second her clinical instructor excused her from Callahan Hall!

#### 11:45 AM — The Transfer to the Third Floor

The inpatient transport team arrived at the doorway of **ER Bay 3** just minutes after **Dr. Patel** stepped out, their crisp, clinical efficiency a stark contrast to the raw terror inside the room.

"Okay, Mr. Fuller, we're moving you up to the third-floor cardiac step-down unit now," the lead transporter said, stepping to the foot of the stretcher and clicking the wheel brakes into neutral.

As the stretcher began to roll forward, **Aubrie Jean**—whose left hand was still locked around **Jordan's** fingers—took a shaky, instinctive step alongside the rail.

"Ma'am, you'll need to follow behind us in the corridor," the transporter said, his voice kind but firm. "We need room to maneuver the bed through the doors and into the service elevator."

"No," Aubrie Jean whispered, her voice a raw, desperate sob. She wasn't asking permission; she was stating an unyielding law of physics. "I'm not letting go."

The transporter glanced at his partner, then down at the pale, terrified nineteen-year-old on the stretcher whose eyes were fixed entirely on Aubrie Jean, and finally at the ten other anxious faces of the **Pact** and the **Brooks family** packed shoulder-to-shoulder behind them. He let out a quiet, human sigh.

"Fine," the transporter relented. "Just stay tight against the left rail and *do not* get in our way."

The rest of the family fell into formation right behind them—**Zoë** piloting *S.S. Freedom* at a slow indoor crawl with Jordan's backpack clipped to the frame, **Isabel** walking beside **Madison** and **Hannah**, and **Daniel**, **Laura**, **Mark**, **Lauren**, **Sarah**, and **Jessica** forming a silent, protective phalanx as the stretcher rolled out of the Emergency Department and up the oversized hospital elevators to the third floor.

For Jordan, the heavy, throbbing pressure behind his breastbone was a constant drumbeat of dread. Yet as the fluorescent ceiling tiles of the third-floor cardiac wing glided overhead, his entire world narrowed to a single point of gravity: the warmth of Aubrie Jean's hand around his fingers. She was his first true **Safe Person**—the girl who had climbed onto his bed in Room 214 on the morning of the clerical error and held him through his very first meltdown—and he clung to her hand like a lifeline.

Beside him, Aubrie Jean was trembling from head to toe, tears spilling silently down her cheeks with every step. Her mind still couldn't reconcile the clinical words she had heard in the ER. *He's nineteen,* she thought, a wave of dizziness washing over her. *Nineteen! Heart attacks are for grandparents. This can't be real.*

When they wheeled him into **Cardiac Step-Down Room 312**, the transport team aligned the stretcher beside the inpatient bed. Aubrie Jean didn't let go for a second; as they slid the draw-sheet across, she scrambled right onto the edge of the mattress beside his hip, burying her face against his right shoulder and muffling her sobs against his hospital gown.

Seeing the state she was in, the two transporters quietly backed out of the room with the empty stretcher, giving the family a moment to breathe. Jordan sank back against the pillows, his chest aching, and used his free hand to gently pat the top of Aubrie Jean's head.

***

#### 12:00 PM — Room 312 (Strict NPO)

All eleven members of his family crowded into **Room 312** right behind the stretcher. Within seconds, the private cardiac room felt small, warm, and thick with the scent of antiseptic and collective fear. Seeing that Aubrie Jean was perched precariously on the edge of the mattress where the nurses needed to work, **Mark** quietly grabbed the padded visitor's armchair from the corner and slid it right up against the left bed rail.

"Here, Aubrie," Mark said gently, guiding her shoulder. She sank into the chair without ever breaking her grip on Jordan's hand.

A moment later, the inpatient cardiac nurse stepped inside with a vital-signs cart, her expression warm but no-nonsense.

"Okay, folks, I need a little breathing room to get Mr. Fuller settled," the nurse said kindly, her eyes landing on Aubrie Jean's white-knuckled grip. "Honey, I need you to let go of his hand for just sixty seconds so we can get his gown straightened out and hook him up to our central telemetry monitors."

With a shaky, pained breath, Aubrie Jean reluctantly unlaced her fingers from his. Even that sixty-second loss of physical contact sent a jolt of cold static through Jordan's chest as the nurse and an orderly swiftly attached fresh five-lead telemetry patches to his torso, connected his IV line to an infusion pump on the pole, and swung his **MagnaByte `mPad`** AAC mount onto the right bed rail.

The second the nurse stepped back, Aubrie Jean's hand locked right back onto Jordan's left hand, while **Isabel**—still in her maroon CPI clinical nursing scrubs—stepped up beside the right rail and rested her warm palm over his forearm, her trained eyes scanning his telemetry waveform (`Sinus Rhythm — 94 BPM`, `SpO2 98%`) with quiet, fierce vigilance.

As the initial flood of adrenaline from the ambulance ride finally began to ebb, Jordan's body registered a mundane, overwhelming sensation: his stomach was completely empty. He hadn't eaten since breakfast at Kincaid Commons before `SOC 101`, and his stomach let out a loud, hollow growl.

With his right thumb, he tapped on his **mPad**:

<aac>I am really hungry. Can I have something to eat?</aac>

The cardiac nurse gave him a sympathetic, motherly look. "I know you are, sweetie. Putting a body through a heart event burns through everything you've got. But after an acute STEMI, we can't just bring you a tray. Let me step out and check your orders with Dr. Patel to see if you're **NPO**—that's medical shorthand for *nil per os*, or nothing by mouth."

She stepped out to the nurses' station and returned sixty seconds later, her expression apologetic.

"I'm so sorry, Jordan," she said softly. "Dr. Patel confirmed it: you are strictly **NPO** right now—no food, no water, not even ice chips—because they're preparing to take you into the Cath Lab this afternoon."

A wave of pure, grumpy frustration washed over Jordan. His chest ached, he was terrified of dying at nineteen, and now he wasn't even allowed to eat or drink a sip of water. He let out a long, defeated sigh through his nose and squeezed Aubrie Jean's hand.

### Part 3: The Fork in the Road & 99% Calcified: The Failed Angioplasty

**Date:** 2015-11-13 at 12:15 America/New_York

#### 12:15 PM — The Fork in the Road

Ten minutes later, the door of **Room 312** opened, and **Dr. Patel** stepped inside carrying a digital tablet. Instantly, the quiet murmurs in the room vanished. **Daniel** and **Laura Brooks** stood side-by-side at the foot of the bed like sentinels while the rest of the Pact pressed close.

"Alright, Jordan, now that you're settled upstairs, let's walk through the exact game plan," Dr. Patel began, looking directly at Jordan, Daniel, and Laura. "The echocardiogram and blood work downstairs confirmed a high-grade occlusion in your **left anterior descending (`LAD`) coronary artery**—the main vessel supplying the front wall of your heart. We have to open that vessel."

He held up two fingers.

"We have two paths forward," Dr. Patel explained clearly. "**Path One**—the path we are preparing for right now—is a **percutaneous transluminal coronary angioplasty (`PTCA`)**, commonly called a **balloon angioplasty**. As soon as our Cardiac Catheterization Lab opens up this afternoon, we'll bring you down, access the artery through your right wrist, thread a microscopic guidewire up to your heart under live X-ray fluoroscopy, and inflate a high-pressure balloon inside the blockage to crush the plaque flat against the artery wall and place a stent. If Path One works, the restoration of blood flow is immediate. You'll stay with us here at New River Valley for two or three days of monitoring, and then you'll go home to Christiansburg."

Jordan squeezed Aubrie Jean's fingers, a sudden, desperate spark of hope rising in his chest. *Two or three days. Then home to Geneva Street.*

"However," Dr. Patel continued, his voice dropping an octave into grave candor, "I need to be completely honest with you and your family. Having a severe LAD blockage at nineteen years old—likely driven by years of extreme chronic cortisol stress, severe vascular inflammation, and metabolic strain—is highly unusual. If we get in there and find that the blockage is too heavily calcified, or hard as stone, the balloon will not be able to expand it. If the angioplasty fails, your only remaining option is **Path Two**: an immediate **Coronary Artery Bypass Graft (`CABG`)**—open-heart bypass surgery."

A cold, suffocating silence fell over Room 312.

"Because New River Valley is a community hospital without an open-heart cardiothoracic surgical program," Dr. Patel finished gently, "a CABG cannot be performed in this building. If the balloon fails, we will stabilize you and transfer you by critical care ambulance to the cardiothoracic surgeons at **Star City General Hospital** in **Roanoke**. And unlike an angioplasty, the recovery from open-heart surgery is not measured in days. It is a long, slow, painful process measured in months."

Dr. Patel gave a respectful nod. "We have you on the Cath Lab schedule for this afternoon. A transport team will come for you as soon as the suite is prepped. Until then, rest as much as you can."

When the door clicked shut behind the cardiologist, the room remained frozen for several seconds. Trying to hold onto the best-case scenario, Jordan turned his head toward Aubrie Jean, his eyes wide and pleading behind his glasses as he tapped on his **mPad**:

<aac>Aubrie... if the balloon works... just for the couple of days... will you stay here with me? I do not want to be alone in this place.</aac>

"I'm not going anywhere, Jordan," Aubrie Jean promised instantly, fresh tears spilling down her cheeks as she kissed the back of his hand. "I'm staying right here with you the entire time."

Daniel Brooks immediately shifted into decisive father mode, resting a steadying hand on Laura's shoulder as twenty-seven-year-old **Megan** stepped forward from the doorway with her car keys already in hand.

"Mom, Dad, you two stay right here with Jordan and the cardiologist," Megan said warmly, her practical older-sister instincts kicking in immediately for the newest member of their Geneva Street household. "I've got my car parked right out front. I'll run back to Geneva Street right now, pack overnight bags with pillows, blankets, chargers, and pajamas for Aubrie, and bring them right back before they take him down to the Cath Lab."

"And I have to run back up to campus for ninety minutes to sign out my clinical rotation packet at Callahan Hall and hand off the Allegheny Commons duty binder to Garrett," **Isabel** added reluctantly, leaning over the right rail to press a warm kiss to Jordan's forehead. "I'll ride back down with Henry, Garrett, and Kelsey before they wheel you into the Cath Lab, J. I promise."

***

#### 12:35 PM — A Brother's Warning, A Family's Vow

As Megan and Isabel hurried out to the elevator—Megan heading to Geneva Street for overnight supplies and Isabel heading briefly back to CPI to clear her clinical schedule—the room felt noticeably quieter. Jordan's gaze drifted from the door to **Mark**, who was standing taut and pale by the window with **Hannah's** arm linked through his.

Remembering the look on Mark's face back in `SOC 101`, Jordan tapped softly on his **mPad**:

<aac>Mark... earlier you thought of my heart attack right away because of your family. Did your uncle have the second path? The CABG?</aac>

Mark's jaw tightened. Slowly, he walked over from the window, pulled a rolling stool up to the right side of Jordan's bed beside Isabel, and sat down eye-to-eye with his brother. He glanced briefly at Aubrie Jean and Hannah before looking back at Jordan. He wasn't going to lie to him.

"Yeah, J. He did," Mark said, his voice low and steady. "My uncle had a quintuple bypass five years ago. And I'm not gonna sugarcoat it for you, man—it's rough. To sew the new graft vessels onto your coronary arteries, they have to temporarily stop your heart, hook your bloodstream up to a heart-lung bypass machine, and saw through your breastbone to open your chest."

At the words *open your chest*, a horrified, strangled sob tore from Aubrie Jean's throat. Hearing the clinical acronym *CABG* from the doctor had been scary enough; picturing a surgical saw dividing Jordan's sternum was almost too much to bear. Beside the bed, **Madison** and **Sarah** wrapped their arms around Aubrie Jean's shaking shoulders, while **Laura** quietly reached over and rested her hand on Jordan's right shoulder, her thumb rubbing a slow, grounding circle against his collarbone.

Jordan stared at Mark, his own chest aching beneath the telemetry leads as his mind pictured what Mark had just described.

Seeing the sheer terror in Jordan's green eyes, Mark immediately reached out and gripped Jordan's right hand firmly.

"Hey—look at me, J," Mark said, his voice locking in with fierce, unwavering conviction. "It is rough, and the recovery is slow—it has high points and really hard low points. *But my uncle made a one-hundred-percent full recovery.* He's alive, he's healthy, and his heart is stronger now than it was for twenty years before the surgery. It *works*. And you aren't fifty-eight—you're nineteen years old, and you're the toughest guy in this room. Whatever happens in that lab this afternoon, you've got this."

Mark gave Jordan's hand a final, brotherly squeeze and stepped back beside Hannah.

The exact second Mark released Jordan's right hand, **Zoë** stepped forward and took it. On his left side, Aubrie Jean still hadn't let go.

Jordan looked up into Zoë's gray eyes behind her glasses. Inside Zoë's head, her processor was analyzing both halves of Jordan's fear: he wasn't just terrified of the surgery itself—after eighteen years of being treated like a broken, unwanted burden by Aubrie Sinclair, he was terrified that a multi-month surgical recovery would make him too much trouble to keep.

"Mark is right, Jordan," Zoë said, her crisp British-Virginian voice cutting through the emotional storm in the room like a steel anchor. "If it is two days, we handle it. If it is open-heart surgery and a two-month recovery, it will be arduous—which is precisely why you will not be doing a single second of it alone."

She squeezed his fingers firmly.

"Listen to me very carefully: you are part of my family now," Zoë told him, her gaze intense and unblinking. "My parents view you as their son. My bedroom at Geneva Street is fifteen feet from yours. Whether you leave this hospital in forty-eight hours or after open-heart surgery in Roanoke, you have a permanent home in Christiansburg. You will *never* go back to Hampton Roads or a nursing facility ever again. That timeline is terminated. We are your family, and we will handle this together."

Leaning down over the right bed rail, Zoë pressed a firm, loving kiss to Jordan's right cheek. On his left side, bolstered by Zoë's iron certainty, Aubrie Jean leaned in through her tears and kissed his left cheek, while **Hannah** smiled warmly through her own damp lashes and squeezed his shoulder.

"And as soon as Isabel finishes signing out her clinicals at Callahan Hall, you'll have our senior nursing student right back at your bedside too," Hannah added softly, brushing a damp curl of hair back from Jordan's forehead. "You're stuck with all of us, J."

Anchored between them, with his hands held tightly on both sides of the bed, Jordan felt the terror in his chest loosen its grip by a fraction of an inch.

***

#### 2:15 PM — Megan's Supply Run & The CPI Reinforcements

Just after two-fifteen in the afternoon, **Megan Brooks** returned from `414 Geneva Street` carrying two quilted duffle bags stuffed with pillows, fleece blankets, extra phone and `mPad` chargers, and clean pajamas for Aubrie Jean—and riding up in the third-floor elevator right beside Megan were **Isabel** (who had just finished clearing her clinical rotation schedule on campus) and three more familiar faces from **Commonwealth Polytechnic Institute**: **Henry Walsh**, **Garrett Reynolds**, and **Kelsey Brennan**.

Stepping quietly into the doorway of **Room 312** so they wouldn't overwhelm the telemetry space, sixty-one-year-old **Henry Walsh** held his battered canvas cap in both hands, his weathered face creased with fatherly concern as he looked toward **Jordan's** bed, while **Garrett** and **Kelsey** stood right beside **Daniel** and **Isabel**.

"We came straight down Business 460 as soon as word reached Residence Life about what happened in Walton Hall," Kelsey whispered, stepping over to hug **Isabel**, **Lauren**, and **Sarah** in turn. "First: **Ms. Higgins** over at **Educational Accessibility** and the Dean of Students' office have already issued formal emergency medical excusal notices to every single professor for all ten of you. Nobody has to worry about a missed class, lab, or attendance grade."

"And second," Garrett added earnestly, resting a hand on Isabel's shoulder, "Kelsey, Henry, and the New River Hall staff have already covered every single one of your RA duty shifts at **Allegheny Commons** and **New River Hall** for the entire week. And **Stephen** and **Elana** called from Charlottesville—they're keeping **Stella** happy and fed at Apartment 101 until you're ready. Your only job right now is being right here with Jordan."

"And I've got my crew-cab Silverado parked right downstairs in the lot," Henry said gruffly, giving Jordan a warm, steady nod from the foot of the bed. "Whenever you need an extra set of wheels or an extra pair of hands to haul gear, I'm on standby, son."

Tears of gratitude welled in Isabel's and Lauren's eyes as Jordan raised his right hand slightly off the mattress in a silent thank-you wave to Henry, Garrett, and Kelsey.

***

#### 2:45 PM — The Red Line

Fifteen minutes later, at `2:45 PM`, the door of **Room 312** swung wide open, and two cardiac catheterization transport nurses entered in lead-lined scrub vests and surgical caps.

"Mr. Fuller? We're ready for you down in the **Cath Lab**."

Jordan's heart slammed against his ribs, the green waveform on the bedside telemetry monitor spiking from `88` to `112 BPM`. *This is it,* he thought. *The fork in the road.* Within the next hour, he would either have a stented, open artery and be going home to Geneva Street in two days—or he would be facing a surgical saw and a heart-lung machine in Roanoke.

As the transport nurses unplugged the bed from the wall and released the floor brake, **Aubrie Jean**—who was still sitting in the armchair beside the left rail—instinctively started to lunge to her feet to grab the bed frame.

Halfway up, she caught herself.

Remembering the paramedic in Walton Hall and the transporter downstairs—*do not get in their way while they're trying to save him*—Aubrie Jean forced her hands into tight, white-knuckled fists at her sides and walked steadily alongside the moving hospital bed as they wheeled Jordan out into the third-floor corridor.

All fourteen of them—**Daniel**, **Laura**, **Mark**, **Hannah**, **Aubrie Jean**, **Madison**, **Zoë**, **Lauren**, **Sarah**, **Jessica**, **Isabel**, **Henry**, **Garrett**, and **Kelsey**—followed in a silent, solemn procession down the elevator to the second-floor procedural wing.

At the end of a long, brightly lit corridor, they reached a pair of heavy, automated stainless-steel double doors marked **`CARDIAC CATHETERIZATION LABORATORY — AUTHORIZED PERSONNEL ONLY — RADIATION AREA`**, with a wide red boundary line painted across the linoleum floor.

The lead transport nurse halted the bed just before the red line and turned gently to the group.

"This is as far as family can come," she said softly. "We'll take very good care of him inside, and Dr. Patel will come straight out to the family room as soon as we're finished."

Lying flat on the rolling bed in his thin hospital gown, Jordan looked up at the circle of faces standing behind the red line. He was about to be pushed through those heavy steel doors into a freezing, sterile room completely alone, without his wheelchair and without a single person who knew his soul. A wave of raw, suffocating terror seized his chest.

Before the nurse could hit the silver wall plate to open the doors, Jordan tapped frantically on his rail-mounted **mPad** before they unclipped it:

<aac>Wait. Please wait. I want a hug. From everyone. One last hug before I go in, please.</aac>

The Cath Lab nurse looked down at the terrified nineteen-year-old, then up at the circle of pale, tear-streaked faces behind the red line. Her professional mask softened immediately.

"Of course," she nodded, unclipping the **mPad** mount and handing the tablet carefully to Zoë so the rails could drop. "Go right ahead, folks—just be gentle around his IV line."

One by one, his family surged forward across the corridor to wrap him in their arms.

**Mark** stepped up first, leaning over the right rail to clasp Jordan's shoulder and pull him into a firm, brotherly embrace. "You've got this, brother," Mark whispered fiercely into his ear. "See you on the other side."

**Hannah** followed immediately behind him, her protective big-sister warmth enveloping Jordan as she smoothed his dark hair back from his forehead and hugged him gently. "We will be waiting right outside these doors when you wake up, J. We love you."

Then came **Lauren**, **Sarah**, **Jessica**, and **Madison**, each leaning down in turn with tearful hugs and soft kisses on his forehead and cheeks, followed by **Henry**, **Garrett**, and **Kelsey** clasping his hand warmly at the foot of the bed.

**Isabel** leaned down next, her dark eyes glistening as she cupped his jaw in her warm palm and pressed a tender kiss to his lips. "That balloon is going to do its job, and I'm going to be right here checking your vitals the second you roll back out," she whispered. "I love you, Jordan."

Then **Zoë** stepped up to the rail. Her face was pale, but her gray eyes were steady and fierce behind her glasses. Instead of a quick embrace, she framed both sides of Jordan's face in her hands so he was looking directly into her eyes.
