#### January 18, 2016 • 9:00 AM — Twelve Weeks Post-Op & Off Sternal Precautions

On **Monday morning, January 18, 2016**—the day before **Commonwealth Polytechnic Institute** opened its doors for the **Spring 2016 semester**—**Jordan** sat on the examination table at the **Star City General Hospital Outpatient Heart & Vascular Center** in Roanoke while **Dr. Tariq Hassan** and **Dr. Patel** reviewed his twelve-week post-operative chest X-ray and echocardiogram.

Standing in a semi-circle around the exam room were **Daniel and Laura Brooks**, **Aubrie Jean**, **Isabel**, and twenty-seven-year-old **Megan**.

Dr. Hassan clipped the digital radiograph onto the illuminated wall viewer, showing the clean, unbroken line of surgical stainless-steel sternal wires holding Jordan's healed breastbone together, and turned around with a broad, warm smile.

"Look at that cortical bone fusion, Jordan," Dr. Hassan said, tapping the center of the image. "Twelve weeks to the day since your bypass graft. Your left internal mammary artery graft to the LAD is flowing at one hundred percent capacity, your ejection fraction is fifty-eight percent, and your sternum is completely, structurally fused."

Dr. Hassan picked up Jordan's red heart-shaped sternal-precaution cough pillow from the chair beside the table and handed it to Megan with a ceremonial grin.

"Which means as of nine-fifteen this morning, Mr. Fuller—soon to be Mr. Kelly—you are officially **one hundred percent cleared from Sternal Precautions**," Dr. Hassan announced. "No more ten-pound lifting limit, no more bolster-pillow barriers in bed, and you are fully cleared to propel your manual chair, transfer independently, and return to a full sophomore course load at CPI tomorrow morning."

In the corner of the exam room, **Zoë's** phone buzzed on speakerphone from Christiansburg as she logged the clinical milestone:

```zoe-log
ZOË.Systems.Logs.KernelLog: Thread 3 (Jordan / Jordan.OS) — Clinical_Clearance_Received(Dr_Tariq_Hassan, Star_City_General_Cardiology). Sternal_Fusion_Status == 100.0%. LIMA_to_LAD_Graft_Patency == 100.0%. 01-18-2016 09:16:04
ZOË.Systems.Logs.SystemSchedulerLog: Thread 1 (Self) — Deactivating Protocol(Daniel_Brooks_Single_Bed_Partner_Sternal_Restriction). Restoring Full_Constellation_Sleep_Topology(8_Partner_Puppy_Pile) effective 2016-01-18T22:00:00. 01-18-2016 09:16:12
```

Jordan looked down at the pale, healed silver scar running down the center of his chest before buttoning his soft flannel shirt. For nearly three months, that scar had felt like a fragile fault line that required his entire family to tiptoe around him. Now, pressing his palm flat over his breastbone, he felt only solid, unyielding bone and the strong, steady rhythm of his repaired heart.

Reaching for his **mPad** mounted on the swing-arm of `*S.S. Freedom*`, Jordan tapped:

<aac>Thank you, Dr. Hassan. And thank you, Daniel—does this mean the one-person-at-a-time bed rule is officially retired?</aac>

Daniel laughed aloud, clapping a warm hand on Jordan's shoulder. "Officially retired, son. Though how all nine of you fit across those pushed-together mattresses down in the basement without somebody rolling onto the carpet is still beyond my engineering degree."

***

#### January 22, 2016 • 8:30 PM — Megan's First Night Off Precautions

Four days later, on **Friday evening, January 22, 2016**, the first week of Spring Semester classes was in the books.

Back on Monday morning after Jordan's cardiology clearance in Roanoke, **Megan**—who had waited patiently for Jordan to be completely off Sternal Precautions before taking the next step in their relationship—had driven with **Aubrie Jean** and **Isabel** to **New River Valley Women's Health** in Christiansburg. Having already started her physician-prescribed oral contraceptive regimen right after Boxing Day and completed her mandatory seven-day effectiveness window alongside a 100% clean, negative STI screening panel, Megan was officially cleared on every clinical front.

At eight-thirty that Friday night, after a celebratory family dinner of Laura's homemade beef shepherd's pie upstairs at **414 Geneva Street**, **Aubrie Jean**, **Madison**, **Zoë**, **Lauren**, **Sarah**, **Jessica**, and **Isabel** gathered up their mugs of tea and textbooks from the basement living room with knowing, affectionate smiles.

"Mark and Hannah are hosting board-game night upstairs with Mum and Dad until ten-thirty," twenty-year-old **Zoë** announced calmly, pausing at the foot of the basement stairs to give her twenty-seven-year-old big sister a tight, grounding hug. "Sternal precautions are zero. Contraceptive and screening verification is one hundred percent. The walk-out basement sanctuary belongs to you and Jordan, Meg."

```zoe-log
ZOË.Systems.Logs.EmotionalStateLog: Thread 1 (Self) — Observing Sister_Node(Megan) and Thread 3 (Jordan). Post_CABG_Sternal_Clearance == VERIFIED. Allocating 120-minute private sanctuary window. Sister_Happiness_Index == MAXIMUM. 01-22-2016 20:32:45
```

One by one, the other seven women of the Pact kissed Jordan's cheek and squeezed Megan's hand before heading up the stairs and clicking the basement door shut behind them.

Standing beside the king bed in the warm amber glow of the salt lamps, **Megan** took off her wire-rimmed glasses, set them carefully on the nightstand beside Jordan's glasses and hearing-aid case, and let her long, wavy coppery-red hair fall loose over her shoulders. At six feet tall, she had spent months effortlessly lifting, steadying, and protecting Jordan through his darkest post-operative fears—yet now, with no surgical restrictions between them, her cheeks were flushed a soft, vulnerable rose.

"For three months," Megan whispered in her gentle British-inflected cadence as she sat down beside Jordan on the edge of the mattress and traced her fingertips lightly over the healed silver line on his chest, "every time I helped you out of the shower or held you in the passenger seat of my car during a panic spike, I was so terrified of putting even an ounce too much weight on your chest."

Jordan smiled warmly, his eyes clear even at close range as he reached up with both hands to cup her freckled cheeks, and tapped one last line on his **mPad** before setting the tablet onto the nightstand:

<aac>My chest is strong, Meg. You helped heal it. You do not have to hold back anymore.</aac>

"Good," Megan breathed, a radiant, tearful smile breaking across her face as she leaned down and kissed him deeply, wrapping her long arms around his shoulders and drawing him down onto the pillows with her. "Because I have been waiting a very, very long time to love all of you, Jordan."

Later that night, at ten-thirty, when the basement door clicked open and **Aubrie Jean**, **Madison**, **Zoë**, **Lauren**, **Sarah**, **Jessica**, and **Isabel** padded quietly back downstairs in their pajamas, there was no more single-partner sternal quarantine. For the first time since September, all eight women of the **Constellation Pact** climbed onto the massive pushed-together mattress island around Jordan—**Megan** curled blissfully against his right side, **Aubrie Jean** against his left, and his entire family tangled together in the warm, unbroken safety of their sanctuary.

## HEY SAACURC! & The Bear and the Bug

### The Friday Arrival & The Bus to Christiansburg

**Date:** 2016-02-12 at 16:15 America/New_York

#### 4:15 PM — Two Different Branches on College Avenue

Friday afternoon, February 12, 2016 was crisp and cold across the 2,100-foot plateau of Blacksburg. A winter storm two days earlier had blanketed the New River Valley in four inches of snow; by Friday afternoon, the brick walkways and asphalt lanes were dry and salted, while patches of mostly melted white snow still clung to the shaded grass along **College Avenue** and **Commonwealth Mall**.

With their Friday afternoon classes finished for the week, **Jordan** guided his **power wheelchair** (*S.S. Freedom*) smoothly along the wide brick sidewalk alongside **Aubrie Jean**, **Madison**, **Zoë**, **Lauren**, **Sarah**, **Jessica Gallagher**, **Mark**, **Hannah**, and **Isabel**, heading past **The Hotel at Poly** and **Kincaid Student Center** (`290 College Ave.`) toward the curbside bus lineup on **Commonwealth Mall** to catch their bus back to the **Christiansburg Transit Center** and `414 Geneva Street`.

As they passed the wide brick circular drive of **The Hotel at Poly**—the university conference hotel directly adjacent to campus—the sidewalk was suddenly buzzing with fifteen-passenger university vans, rolling suitcases, painted fabric banners, and dozens of bundled-up college students wearing lanyards and colorful winter parkas loaded with painted wooden clothespins.

Across the street at the entrance to **Kincaid Student Center**, a massive maroon-and-orange welcome banner billowed between two stone columns:

> **WELCOME TO COMMONWEALTH POLYTECHNIC INSTITUTE!**<br>
> **SAACURC 2016 REGIONAL STUDENT LEADERSHIP CONFERENCE**<br>
> ***South Atlantic Affiliate of College and University Residence Halls***<br>
> **February 12–14, 2016 • Kincaid Student Center (`290 College Ave.`)**

"Whoa, wait a second," **Madison** laughed, glancing from the banner outside Kincaid Student Center back toward the vans unloading at **The Hotel at Poly**. "Didn't we already see those decorated conference clothespins last spring when Isabel, Kelsey, and Garrett went up to **Shenandoah Valley University** in **Harrisonburg** for `CACUHO`? Why isn't Isabel working the check-in desk today?"

"Because `CACUHO` and `SAACURC` are two completely different branches of the housing world, run by two completely separate entities—and they don't intermingle at all," **Isabel** explained with a warm smile, adjusting her maroon scarf against the February breeze. "`CACUHO`—the *Commonwealth Association of College and University Housing Officers* that **Shenandoah Valley University** hosted up in **Harrisonburg** last February—is the professional Housing and Residence Life organization for university housing staff and hired RAs. **`SAACURC`**, on the other hand, is strictly the student-governed **Residence Hall Association (`RHA`)** branch, where **every single RHA position is elected by on-campus residents**."

"Affirmative," **Zoë** added, her eyes scanning the arrival logistics outside **The Hotel at Poly**. "Unlike RA staff who are employed by the university, `RHA` executive officers and hall council representatives are democratically elected by the students living in the dorms. The visiting delegations from across the region arrive tonight—Friday night—to check into **The Hotel at Poly**, unless their campus is close enough for a short daily commute like **Radford University** fifteen minutes away. Then the conference sessions run all day Saturday and Sunday morning inside Kincaid Student Center, wrapping up Sunday afternoon with a closing lunch and awards ceremony—where, per the universal conference conflict-of-interest ground rule, the host school (`CPI`) is never eligible to win any awards—before the delegations drive back to their home campuses."

<aac>"And since we all live off campus at 414 Geneva Street in Christiansburg now,"</aac> Jordan tapped on his `mPad` with an amused grin as he steered *S.S. Freedom* around a cluster of suitcases on the sidewalk, <aac>"none of us are on-campus residents eligible for RHA or SAACURC. We are officially off-campus commuters heading home for Friday night dinner."</aac>

"And thank goodness for that," **Mark** chuckled, wrapping an arm around **Hannah**’s shoulders. "Hearing about those thirty-five-foot Gamble Aria shuttle buses in Harrisonburg last spring was plenty of conference excitement for me!"

***

#### 4:25 PM — Passing Ships at the Commonwealth Mall Curb

As the ten of them rounded the corner from **The Hotel at Poly** onto the wide sidewalk of **Commonwealth Mall** beneath the limestone arch of **The Keystone Bridge** across from **Kincaid Hall**, another visiting delegation was crossing in passing from the hotel's accessible ground-floor wing toward Kincaid Student Center to pick up their Friday evening registration packets.

Even in the sea of collegiate colors along the sidewalk, their winter gear stood out immediately: deep, rich **`Chesapeake Teal`** (`#005F6A`) and bright **`Harbor Gold`** (`#D4AF37`), embroidered with the distinctive emblem of an eighteenth-century Chesapeake naval Admiral and a golden fouled anchor—the delegation from **Virginia Dominion University (`VDU`)** in Norfolk, accompanied by their **VDU RHA Advisor** and four student delegates carrying a rolled `VDU ADMIRALS RHA` banner.

At the center of the VDU group rolled a young man of about twenty-one—the exact same `5'7"` frame as the young woman walking right beside him if he were standing—with short dark brown hair and rectangular glasses, bundled up in a heavy `Chesapeake Teal` and `Harbor Gold` **VDU Admirals** winter parka over an embroidered **`VDU RHA • DIRECTOR OF OPERATIONS`** badge. He was propelling a blue-upholstered manual wheelchair with the careful, deliberate upper-body cadence of someone who was not normally a wheelchair user, but was temporarily using the chair while recovering from a planned surgery. Walking right beside his right wheel in effortless synchronization was a young woman of the exact same `5'7"` height with warm brown hair and a matching `Chesapeake Teal` winter coat and `Harbor Gold` scarf over her **`VDU RHA • SECRETARY`** sweater, dozens of painted wooden clothespins clipped along the strap of her messenger bag.

Just as both groups passed the **Commonwealth Mall** crosswalk—where there were **no dedicated bus bays**, and buses from every transit agency in the New River Valley simply pulled up and lined up one behind the other along the curb—two buses rumbled into view beneath **The Keystone Bridge**.

Pulling up first at the front of the curb line was a thirty-foot low-floor **Radford Transit** bus (`Unit 104`)—operating the hourly ***Radford Connector*** route that exits CPI from **Commonwealth Mall**, turns right onto **Stanger Street**, left onto **Prices Fork Road**, right onto **Peppers Ferry Road**, left onto **U.S. Route 11**, crosses the **New River Bridge** into **Radford**, and turns left onto **West Main Street** to terminate at **McConnell Transit Center** (providing once-hourly local service for **Prices Fork**, **Belview**, **Centerville**, and **Fairlawn**, where rural stop spacing lets it move like an express bus). Its amber LED destination sign cycled between:

```
RADFORD CONNECTOR
```

and:

```
TO MCCONNELL TRANSIT CTR via PRICES FORK & FAIRLAWN
```

And gliding smoothly into line right behind the *Radford Connector* came a sixty-foot articulated **Blue Ridge Transit (`BRT`)** bus, its destination sign reading:

```
1 CBURG TRANS CTR
```

```
via BUSINESS 460 & PEPPER PLAZA
```

As the articulated bus kneeled its front suspension and deployed its wheelchair ramp onto the **Commonwealth Mall** sidewalk with a smooth pneumatic hiss, both Jordan (in his power chair, *S.S. Freedom*) and the visiting VDU student in the blue manual wheelchair happened to glance toward the two transit buses at the exact same second.

Neither of them knew who the other was—just a CPI student in a power chair catching his Friday afternoon bus home to Christiansburg with his family, and a visiting VDU RHA delegate in a temporary post-surgical manual chair arriving with his sister for `SAACURC`—but as their eyes briefly met across the salted brick sidewalk, they exchanged a warm, knowing nod and a friendly wave in passing. Standing right beside Jordan's chair, **Aubrie Jean**—who had grown up in the **Emerald Creek** area of **Chesapeake** right next door to Norfolk—caught a fleeting, half-familiar sense of *déjà vu* as she glanced at the two VDU delegates in their `Chesapeake Teal` parkas, wondering for half a second if she had ever walked past them years ago in the corridors or bookstore of **Emerald Creek Mall** back home in Hampton Roads, before the moment passed into the crisp mountain air.

### Part 2: The Letter From Home & The Box Office Confrontation

**Date:** 2016-02-22 at 10:00 America/New_York

#### February 22, 2016 • 7:00 PM — An Open Letter to Blacksburg & Forger Nation

On Monday, February 22, 2016, at `10:00 AM`, the remaining general-public allocation for **[The Stardust Engine](https://music.raggiesoft.com/artists/the-stardust-engine)**'s *Live at the Crucible* went on sale via **TicketSphere** at a flat `$45.00` per ticket and sold out all sixty-five thousand seats in less than four minutes.

Predictably, the commercial ticket-broker industry lost its collective mind. Because **Holly O'Connell** and **Engine Room Records** had forced **TicketSphere** to lock every digital ticket barcode to the original purchaser's ID token and banned above-face-value resale—routing all returned tickets through an automated face-value-only fan exchange—scalpers and secondary-market executives flooded the regional newspapers and sports-talk radio stations with furious op-eds complaining that the band was "leaving millions of dollars on the table" and "shutting out premium hospitality buyers" by giving thirty thousand `$15.00` field and lower-bowl seats to CPI undergraduates.

That evening, a new dispatch appeared at the top of **[`thestardustengine.com`](https://stardust.raggiesoft.com)**, **[`engineroom-records.com`](https://engineroom.raggiesoft.com)**, and the front page of *The Collegiate Times*.

At `414 Geneva Street`, **Jordan** sat in his `Vanguard Pro` wheelchair with **Aubrie Jean** curled against his side and **Madison**, **Zoë**, **Lauren**, **Sarah**, **Jessica**, **Isabel**, **Megan**, **Mark**, and **Hannah** gathered around the living room as Mark read the open letter aloud:

> **AN OPEN LETTER TO BLACKSBURG & FORGER NATION**<br>
> **From:** [The Stardust Engine](https://music.raggiesoft.com/artists/the-stardust-engine) (CPI Class of `'89`)<br>
> **Date:** February 22, 2016<br>
> **Subject:** Coming Home to The Crucible<br>
> <br>
> Thirty years ago, in the fall of 1986, the five of us were broke Commonwealth Polytechnic Institute sophomores cramming amplifiers into the back of a rusted station wagon and riding Blue Ridge Transit buses through the mountain sleet to get to our 8:00 AM classes.<br>
> <br>
> Back then, fifteen dollars was our entire grocery budget for a week. We wrote our first songs—including [**"The Stardust Engine"**](https://music.raggiesoft.com/artists/the-stardust-engine/1987-electric-color?track=1-13-the-stardust-engine) and [**"Electric Color"**](https://music.raggiesoft.com/artists/the-stardust-engine/1987-electric-color?track=1-01-electric-color)—in an unheated garage at the corner of Progress and Turner Streets because we loved the cosmos, the rockets that take you there, and the town that gave us a home when we had nothing else.<br>
> <br>
> We have spent the last twenty-one years building **Engine Room Records** so that no suit in a glass skyscraper could ever again tell us who is allowed to hear our music, or price the kids who need it most out of the room. A college concert at our alma mater is not a luxury asset portfolio for ticket brokers. It belongs to the students walking across Commonwealth Green today.<br>
> <br>
> Furthermore, for everyone who secured digital tickets during the Student Presale or Public Onsale: we know a barcode on a smartphone screen isn't something you can keep in a scrapbook or frame on your dorm wall. Beginning Wednesday, February 24, every ticket holder may bring their `Poly Pass` or confirmation token to **The Crucible Gate 1 Box Office** to pick up complimentary, custom-embossed **30th Anniversary Ceremonial Ticket Stubs** printed on heavyweight archival stock at no charge.<br>
> <br>
> See you under the lights on May 21. Go Forgers.<br>
> <br>
> — **Cassidy, Ryan, Evan, Holly, & Tyler** (*The Stardust Engine*, Class of `'89*)

Jordan stared down at the five signatures at the bottom of the screen. His throat tightened with a warm, fierce pride. He tapped his `mPad`:

<aac>"They never forgot what it felt like to be twenty years old in Blacksburg. We HAVE to go to Gate 1 on Wednesday afternoon and get the ceremonial ticket stubs for all sixteen of us—especially for Daniel and Laura!"</aac>

***

#### February 24, 2016 • 2:30 PM — The Gate 1 Box Office Confrontation

On Wednesday afternoon, February 24, 2016, at `14:30`, the sun broke through the crisp mountain clouds as **Jordan**, **Aubrie Jean**, **Madison**, **Zoë**, **Isabel**, and **Mark** made the walk down Washington Street toward **Gate 1 of The Crucible** so the four `Poly Pass` cell leads could pick up all sixteen embossed souvenir tickets.

Even from the outside plaza, standing at the base of the towering limestone stadium walls made Jordan’s fingers tighten slightly around the armrest of his power wheelchair (*S.S. Freedom*). The last time he had been near Gate 1 was September 2014—the afternoon of the Homecoming football game against the `VDU Admirals`, when sixty-five thousand screaming voices and the stadium cannon had overloaded his auditory cortex.

Right away, Aubrie Jean noticed the micro-tension in his shoulders. She reached down, brushed her knuckles gently across the back of his hand, and smiled warmly. "No cannon today, J. Just us, the sunshine, and sixteen gold-foil tickets."

Jordan took a slow breath, felt his healed sternum rise and fall without a trace of pain, and nodded with a grateful smile.

A cheerful line of CPI students snaked along the accessible brick ramp leading to the Gate 1 Box Office windows. As Jordan, Aubrie Jean, Madison, Zoë, Isabel, and Mark reached the front of the queue at Window 2, however, an older man in an expensive camel-hair overcoat at the adjacent Window 1 was loudly berating the student box-office clerk.

"What do you mean you can't sell me four field-level passes if I pay cash right now?!" the man barked, slapping a platinum credit card against the stainless-steel counter tray. "I'm a Maroon Club donor! I offered five hundred dollars a seat on TicketSphere this morning and found out your system blocks transfers! Meanwhile you're handing out front-row field seats to kids for fifteen dollars?!"

He spun around, his eyes landing on Jordan in his wheelchair and the five students standing beside him as the Window 2 clerk slid four crisp white CPI Box Office envelopes under the glass.

"Look at this!" the man scoffed, gesturing rudely toward Jordan’s wheelchair bay reservation printed on the top manifest sheet. "Sixteen front-row seats in Section 104 Row A tied up for fifteen bucks apiece! Kid, I’ll give you two thousand dollars cash right now for four of those seats. You can sit up in the upper deck!"

For a split second, Mark’s jaw clenched and Madison took half a step forward, her eyes flashing—but Jordan raised his left hand gently to stop them.

He didn't flinch. He didn't shrink back into his chair the way he would have in August 2014.

Instead, Jordan guided *S.S. Freedom* six inches forward until he was looking calmly up at the man. With steady, deliberate precision, Jordan typed on his `mPad` and tapped `Speak` at `100%` volume:

<aac>"No thank you, sir. Those sixteen seats belong to my family. And The Stardust Engine didn't come back to Blacksburg to play for your wallet. They came back for us."</aac>

Behind the glass of Window 1 and Window 2, both student box-office clerks fought back huge grins. Five CPI students standing behind them in line burst into applause.

Flushing bright red, the man in the camel-hair coat snatched his credit card off the counter, muttered under his breath, and stormed off across the brick plaza toward the parking lot.

At Window 2, the student clerk beamed at Jordan, stamped the verification receipt against Jordan’s `Poly Pass` (`Jordan Fuller`), Mark’s `Poly Pass`, Zoë’s `Poly Pass`, and Isabel’s `Poly Pass`, and slid the four thick archival envelopes across the accessible counter.

"Here you go, Jordan," the clerk said warmly. "Section 104, Row A, Seats 1 through 16. Sixteen ceremonial keepsake tickets, courtesy of **[The Stardust Engine](https://music.raggiesoft.com/artists/the-stardust-engine)**."

Jordan opened the top envelope right there in the February sunlight. Inside lay four heavy, midnight-blue cardstock tickets embossed in shimmering gold and electric-cyan foil with the constellation crest of **[The Stardust Engine](https://music.raggiesoft.com/artists/the-stardust-engine)**, the limestone towers of **The Crucible**, the date **`SATURDAY, MAY 21, 2016`**, and the words **`30TH ANNIVERSARY HOMECOMING • SECTION 104 • ROW A`**.

Aubrie Jean leaned over his shoulder, resting her cheek against his temple as Madison, Zoë, Isabel, and Mark gathered around to admire the gleaming gold foil.

"May twenty-first," Aubrie Jean whispered softly against his ear. "First Isabel walks across the stage in her cap and gown... and then we bring our whole family right back through Gate 1 together."

## Live at the Crucible & Senior Commencement

### Part 1: The Crucible Shuttle & The Forger Nation Tailgate

**Date:** 2016-05-21 at 15:00 America/New_York

![Outside the towering Gothic limestone arches of The Crucible stadium at golden hour inside the Forger Nation Tailgate Plaza, Jordan Fuller sits smiling in his Vanguard Pro wheelchair wearing rectangular glasses, a Foundry Maroon CPI shirt, and a gold-foil ticket lanyard with a plate of Smokin' Anvil pulled pork BBQ and his mPad, surrounded by Aubrie Jean Kelly, Madison Scott, Zoë Wren Brooks, and Mark Anderson near an Engine Room Records filming notice sign.]({{CDN}}/raggiesoft-books/images/scenes/aubrie/e007/c004/p001/forger-nation-tailgate-plaza.jpg)

#### 3:00 PM — The Crucible Shuttle

May 2016 arrived in Blacksburg in a burst of warm Appalachian sunshine, blooming dogwoods, and the bittersweet magic of the end of Sophomore Year.

Eight days earlier, on Friday, May 13, 2016, the entire household had cheered until their voices were hoarse as **Isabel Dawson** walked across the CPI Spring Commencement stage in her maroon-and-orange regalia, officially graduating *cum laude* with her Bachelor of Science in Human Development on the Pre-Occupational Therapy and Nursing track. With her Senior Resident Advisor duties in `Allegheny Commons` formally concluded and her post-graduation clinical rehabilitation position in the New River Valley beginning in June, the remaining boxes from `Apartment 101` had been moved permanently into `414 Geneva Street`—and would soon move with the whole family into the nearly completed U.S. 11 compound at the start of July.

Now, on Saturday afternoon, May 21, 2016, at `15:00`, all sixteen members of their extended family stood on the sunny front lawn of `414 Geneva Street`, dressed in their concert best and wearing their commemorative `$5.00` gold-foil ticket stubs in clear lanyards around their necks:
* **Jordan** sat in his `Vanguard Pro` wearing a Foundry Maroon **`CPI`** T-shirt—proudly wearing his own school colors back into the stadium where his freshman Homecoming had ended in tears—with his custom high-fidelity `Vibe-Filter` acoustic earpieces tucked securely into his ears and his over-ear defenders clipped to his push-handles just in case.
* Around him stood all eight women of his constellation—**Aubrie Jean**, **Madison**, **Zoë**, **Lauren**, **Sarah**, **Jessica Gallagher**, **Isabel**, and **Megan**—alongside **Mark**, **Hannah**, **Daniel**, **Laura**, **Elana**, **Stephen**, and eighteen-month-old **Stella**, who was sporting tiny baby-sized pink earmuffs and a miniature `FORGER NATION` jersey in her folding stroller.

"Nobody in their right mind is driving a car anywhere near Stadium Woods today," Mark said with a grin as the sixteen of them made the short one-block walk down the hill from `414 Geneva Street` to the **Christiansburg Transit Center**, where the commuter lot had been transformed into a bustling sea of Foundry Maroon and Molten Orange. "Just like CPI home football Saturdays or big games at **The Furnace**, **Blue Ridge Transit** suspends *all* regular route service for major special events at **The Crucible** and presses every single available bus in the fleet into nonstop **Crucible Shuttle** loops from commuter lots across Blacksburg, Christiansburg, and all of Montgomery County. No fares collected—just load and go!"

Right on cue, a sixty-foot articulated **Blue Ridge Transit** shuttle pulled up to the Christiansburg Transit Center curb. Its digital destination sign alternated between two high-energy messages:

```
CRUCIBLE SHUTTLE
```

```
GO FORGERS!
```

The front door stood open, the front suspension kneeled to the curb, the flip-out wheelchair ramp deployed with a fast, simple mechanical clack, and the external speaker called out on a repeated loop for the crowd:

*"Crucible Shuttle. GO FORGERS! ... Crucible Shuttle. GO FORGERS!"*

"Afternoon, folks!" the BRT operator beamed—wearing a vintage **Stardust Engine** tour shirt over his uniform shirt—and tipped his cap to Jordan and Mark. "All sixteen of you headed up to see **[The Stardust Engine](https://music.raggiesoft.com/artists/the-stardust-engine)**?"

<aac>"Yes sir! Section 104, Row A! Thank you for the lift!"</aac> Jordan tapped on his `mPad`. Pivoting his `Vanguard Pro` 180 degrees on the wide concrete sidewalk so his back faced the open front bus doors—a veteran transit technique he had taught himself over the past year so his large rear drive wheels could climb the incline first and glide straight into the wheelchair bay without having to execute a tight multi-point U-turn between the front wheel wells—Jordan gripped his push-rims, backed himself smoothly up the front-door ramp, and locked into the forward securement bay right next to Stella’s folded stroller.

Nobody pulled out a wallet, swiped a pass, or dropped a coin; with zero fare collection on the **Crucible Shuttle**, the crowd simply loaded and went. As soon as every seat and standing handrail on the sixty-foot coach was full, the doors hissed shut. The shuttle didn't make the usual local stops or wind through town—it roared straight up U.S. Route 460 into Blacksburg and turned onto the dedicated transit-only lane leading directly into the **Crucible Bus Loop**. Looking out the wide window as they glided right to the foot of the stadium gates, Jordan spotted private lawn lots along the side streets waving hand-painted cardboard signs reading **`EVENT PARKING: $50. CASH ONLY`** while frustrated out-of-town drivers sat bumper-to-bumper in gridlock handing wads of cash to parking attendants.

"And that," **Zoë** noted dryly, adjusting her glasses as their shuttle breezed right past the traffic jam along the coned-off busway and opened its doors at the stadium curb without a single fare swiped, "is a fifty-dollar tax on poor logistical planning. Suspend regular routes, press every bus in Montgomery County into load-and-go shuttle loops, and you move sixty-five thousand people without breaking a sweat."

***

#### 3:45 PM — The Forger Nation Tailgate Plaza

The shuttle dropped them off less than two hundred feet from the accessible west entrance of Gate 1. Outside the stadium, the atmosphere was nothing like the chaotic, drunken frenzy that had terrified Jordan during the September 2014 Homecoming game.

Instead, the tree-lined plazas around **The Crucible** felt like a massive, joyful homecoming spanning three generations of **Forger Nation**. Because tonight was the final stop on the band's 2015–2016 ***Reignition* World Tour**, the entire South Endzone concourse lawn had been cordoned off as the **Forger Nation Tailgate Plaza** for fans whose tickets were bound to a student, faculty, or alumni `Poly Pass`.

At the entrance to the plaza and the Gate 1 accessible tunnel, Jordan paused his chair to read one of the large silver-and-black A-frame placards bearing the emblem of **Engine Room Records**:

> **NOTICE OF FILMING AND LIVE AUDIO RECORDING**<br>
> Tonight's performance by **[The Stardust Engine](https://music.raggiesoft.com/artists/the-stardust-engine)** at **The Crucible** is being recorded on 96kHz/24-bit multitrack audio and 4K cinema cameras for the upcoming live album and concert film, [***Live at the Crucible***](https://music.raggiesoft.com/artists/the-stardust-engine/2016-live-at-the-crucible). By entering these premises, you consent to be part of Blacksburg music history.

One by one, the sixteen of them tapped their `Poly Pass` cards (and guest passes) against the green optical pedestals. Inside the **Forger Nation Tailgate Plaza**, there was no pushing, no scalper chaos, and no sensory crush—just wide, level pathways, shaded picnic tables, acoustic guitars, and a long row of local Blacksburg food trucks beneath a maroon banner reading **`ALL PLATES $5.00 FLAT — COURTESY OF ENGINE ROOM RECORDS`**.

"Smell that hickory smoke," **Mark** breathed, leading the group straight toward the flagship **`Smokin' Anvil BBQ`** pit trailer. "Pulled pork platters, hushpuppies, and sweet tea for five bucks before a rock show. Does it get any better than this?"

While Mark, Daniel, and Stephen carried over trays piled high with hickory-smoked pulled pork sandwiches, mac-and-cheese, and cold lemonade to a shaded accessible table, a two-person documentary film crew wearing black **`ENGINE ROOM FILMS`** vests strolled past, capturing B-roll of the three-generation crowd. Spotting Jordan in his Foundry Maroon **`CPI`** shirt beside Daniel’s vintage 1989 *Neon Hearts* tour shirt and little Stella’s tiny pink ear defenders, the camerawoman smiled and gave them a thumbs-up, filming a warm five-second panning shot as Jordan grinned and raised his lemonade cup alongside Aubrie Jean and Madison.

***

#### 6:00 PM — Section 104, Row A

At `18:00`, as the gates to the stadium bowl officially opened, the sixteen of them passed through the accessible security lane—where the ushers handed every person a white plastic wristband fitted with an LED module—and rolled down the wide, cool concrete ramp of the Gate 1 field-level tunnel.

Jordan’s heart beat a little faster as the tunnel opened onto the bright green expanse of the stadium floor.

`Section 104, Row A` was an elevated, zero-obstruction concrete terrace positioned directly at the front edge of the lower bowl on the fifty-yard line, looking straight across the field toward the massive custom stage framed by twin orbital truss towers and a 120-foot curved LED starfield screen.

Jordan locked his wheel brakes in `Seat 1`, with **Aubrie Jean** in `Seat 2`, **Madison** in `Seat 3`, and **Megan** in `Seat 4`, followed in an unbroken row by **Mark**, **Hannah**, **Daniel**, **Laura**, **Zoë**, **Lauren**, **Sarah**, **Jessica**, **Isabel**, **Elana**, **Stephen**, and **Stella**.

![At 6:00 PM golden hour inside The Crucible stadium from the Section 104, Row A accessible terrace behind the front railing, Jordan Fuller sits happily in his manual wheelchair wearing a maroon CPI shirt, rectangular glasses, and a gold ticket lanyard alongside Aubrie Jean Kelly, Madison Scott, Zoë Wren Brooks, and Mark Anderson looking across the green turf toward the concert stage on the front-left.]({{CDN}}/raggiesoft-books/images/scenes/aubrie/e007/c004/p001/section-104-row-a-arrival.jpg#fullwidth)

Jordan looked up at the towering limestone stands rising against the golden early-evening sky of Blacksburg. Then he looked down the row at the fifteen people laughing and adjusting their concert lanyards beside him. He tapped his `mPad`:

<aac>"In September 2014, I had to be carried out of this stadium at halftime because I thought my mother's world was going to crush me. Tonight I am in Row A with everyone I love."</aac>

Daniel leaned across Mark’s shoulder, his eyes glistening behind his glasses as he clapped a warm hand on Jordan’s armrest. "You were never broken, Jordan. You just needed the right crew—and the right night to take this house back."

***

### Part 2: The Anvil Strike & The Marching Forgers

**Date:** 2016-05-21 at 19:55 America/New_York

![From the Section 104, Row A accessible terrace inside The Crucible at night, Jordan Fuller sits in his wheelchair beside Madison Scott, Aubrie Jean Kelly, Zoë Wren Brooks, and Mark Anderson cheering up at a sweeping cinema camera jib overhead while on the main stage all 300 members of the CPI Marching Forgers perform alongside Ryan and Cassidy O'Connell under molten-orange and foundry-maroon spotlights.]({{CDN}}/raggiesoft-books/images/scenes/aubrie/e007/c004/p002/act-i-ignition-marching-forgers.jpg)

#### 7:55 PM — Smile for the Camera

At `19:55`, as twilight deepened into a clear, indigo Appalachian night over the Blue Ridge Mountains, the giant steel-truss camera jibs along the field perimeter swung into position.

Sweeping smoothly along the fifty-yard line in front of `Section 104, Row A`, a twenty-four-foot counterweighted cinema crane glided three feet above the front railing, its wide-angle 4K lens banking across the accessible terrace.

Two seats down in the neighboring row behind them, a middle-aged man in a pressed golf polo—clearly an out-of-town guest who had been brought along by a relative rather than a CPI alumnus—scowled and waved a hand irritably at the passing boom arm.

"Are they seriously going to swing that camera rig right in front of our faces all night?" the man grumbled loudly. "I paid to watch a concert, not stare at the back of a camera crane!"

Before Mark or Daniel could even turn around, **Madison** spun in `Seat 3`, her maroon `FORGER NATION` earrings catching the stadium lights and her face splitting into a radiant, unapologetic grin.

"Are you kidding?!" Madison beamed at him, throwing one arm around **Aubrie Jean**’s shoulder and the other around **Jordan**’s push-handle as the camera lens swept back across their row. "That's the **Engine Room Films** crew shooting [***Live at the Crucible***](https://music.raggiesoft.com/artists/the-stardust-engine/2016-live-at-the-crucible)! Every time that crane passes `Section 104`, we're getting immortalized on the concert Blu-ray forever! We're Forger Nation—*smile for the camera!*"

Right on cue, as the red tally light on the matte box blinked directly in front of `Row A`, Madison, Aubrie Jean, Megan, Zoë, Lauren, Sarah, Jessica, Isabel, Mark, and Hannah all threw up their hands in the CPI *Forger Hammer* salute while Jordan grinned from ear to ear and raised his wristband toward the lens. Even the grumbling guy behind them couldn't help cracking a sheepish smile and raising his cup.

***

#### 8:00 PM — The Anvil Strike & The CPI Marching Forgers

At `20:00` on the dot, every floodlight inside **The Crucible** cut to pitch black.

Sixty-five thousand voices erupted into a deafening roar—softened by Jordan’s linear-response `Vibe-Filter` earpieces into a warm, thrilling ocean wave that vibrated right through the titanium frame of his `Vanguard Pro` without a trace of pain.

Jordan leaned forward slightly against his chest strap, his heart thumping as he looked across the dark field toward the empty stage, wondering which song from *Reignition* the band would use to kick off the night.

Instead, through the darkness of the stadium bowl, the massive field-level gates at the North and South tunnels swung wide.

"Wait—look at the tunnels!" **Mark** shouted, pointing toward the end zones as a low rumble of marching drums rolled across the turf.

Filing down the wide sidelines and climbing the flanking stage ramps in locked six-to-five military precision came all **three hundred uniformed members of the CPI Marching Forgers**—thirty gleaming brass sousaphones, rows of trumpets, mellophones, and trombones, and **"The Engine Room"** Kevlar snare and bass drum battery—filling the upper tiers of the stadium stage.

"No way!" **Daniel** gasped, standing up in `Seat 7` and adjusting his glasses in disbelief. "Why is the entire marching band coming out on stage before the band even takes the field?!"

Over a faint, warm analog synthesizer pad humming from **Cassidy O'Connell**’s center-stage riser, a solitary spotlight illuminated **Ryan O'Connell** as he rolled his manual wheelchair out to the front edge of the stage. When Ryan leaned into the center microphone, his gravelly voice echoed intimately across the sixty-five-thousand-seat valley:

> *"Thirty years ago... We were just five kids in a garage on Progress Street. We didn't have a record deal... We didn't have a tour bus... All we had was a cassette tape... and an idea."*

Across `Section 104, Row A`, **Mark** grabbed **Daniel**’s sleeve with wide eyes as Ryan’s voice rose to a commanding roar:

> *"We entered a contest to write a song for this stadium. We wanted to make something loud enough... To scare the HELL out of anyone who dared to come into our house!"*

The entire stadium bowl erupted in a tidal wave of cheers as Ryan grinned out at the sea of maroon and burnt orange:

> *"For thirty years... you guys have been stomping your feet to our song every single Saturday. So tonight... for the 30th Anniversary... Let's see if we can break the seismographs!"*

**Tyler Wright** unleashed a massive, thundering drum fill across his double-kick kit, and Ryan threw his head back and screamed into the microphone:

***"IGNITION!"***

Sixty-five thousand voices roared back as one:

***"IGNITION!"***

Then came the solitary, earth-shaking sound that echoed across the dark valley like the heartbeat of a foundry—Tyler’s sledgehammer striking the salvaged steel brake-drum anvil (`TING...`) followed by the synchronized stomp of sixty-five thousand pairs of boots on the galvanized steel bleachers of **The Anvil** (`BOOM!`):

***TING... BOOM!***

Across all sixty-five thousand seats, every white wristband flashed molten orange on the strike.

***TING... BOOM!***

In `Seat 1`, Jordan felt the heavy, slow-stomping industrial riff and the rhythmic vibration travel straight up from the concrete terrace through his caster forks and into his chest. Twenty months ago, the roar of this stadium had terrified him into silence. Now, with **Aubrie Jean**’s left hand laced through his fingers and **Mark** and **Daniel** stomping the concrete beside his right wheel, the thunder of the stadium felt like sixty-five thousand friends standing guard around his chair.

Stage pyrotechnics detonated in twin columns of Foundry Maroon and Molten Orange as **Tyler Wright**’s double-kick drums and **The Engine Room**’s thirty Kevlar marching snares slammed in together, **Evan Wright**’s bass locked into the heavy industrial groove, **Cassidy O'Connell**’s analog synthesizer brass blazed across the night sky, and **Ryan O'Connell**’s custom sunburst guitar screamed out the iconic 1986 stadium entrance riff of [**"Ignition: The Forger's Call"**](https://music.raggiesoft.com/artists/the-stardust-engine/2016-live-at-the-crucible?track=1-01-ignition-the-forgers-call) (later released alongside the concert album on the 30th-Anniversary companion compilation [***The Forger's Call***](https://music.raggiesoft.com/artists/the-stardust-engine/2016-the-forgers-call), featuring both the [1986 Crucible Stadium Version](https://music.raggiesoft.com/artists/the-stardust-engine/2016-the-forgers-call?track=1-01-ignition-the-forgers-call) and the original [1986 Progress Street Cassette — Demo Take 3](https://music.raggiesoft.com/artists/the-stardust-engine/2016-the-forgers-call?track=1-16-ignition-the-forgers-call-demo-take-3)):

> *"The lights go dark... the tension builds...*
> *A single pounding heavy sound...*
> *The hammer striking on the steel...*
> *It shakes the air... it shakes the ground!*
> *The pressure's on... the time is now...*
> *We're here to forge our name!*
> *The spark is lit... the fire burns—"*

Ryan leaned into the microphone and shouted a ferocious live ad-lib straight at the scoreboard above the South End Zone:

> ***"We're taking the Anchor BACK to the Mountains!"***

"Are you kidding me?!" Daniel yelled over the roar to Mark and Jordan, his face lit up like a freshman again. "For thirty years you could only hear the 1986 stadium recording of *'Ignition'* over the PA at CPI home football games when the team ran out onto the field! They've NEVER put it on an album or played it at a concert before!"

> *"IGNITION!"*
> ***"IGNITION!"***
> *"This is the Forger's Call!*
> *IGNITION!"*
> ***"IGNITION!"***
> *"We're standing ten feet tall!*
> *We are the hammer, we're the flame—*
> *This is our house, this is our game!"*

As the final pyrotechnic burst of *"Ignition"* echoed off the upper deck, Jordan half-expected the marching band to wave and file back down the ramps—but Tyler didn't even pause for a breath. He snapped four crisp snare rimshots, and the four members of **[The Stardust Engine](https://music.raggiesoft.com/artists/the-stardust-engine)** fused with all three hundred **CPI Marching Forgers** to tear straight into the official university fight song, [**"CPI Tech Triumph: The Marching Forgers"**](https://music.raggiesoft.com/artists/the-stardust-engine/2016-live-at-the-crucible?track=1-02-cpi-tech-triumph-the-marching-forgers).

Every student, professor, and alumnus in the stadium knew every syllable by heart. Down the entire sixteen-seat length of `Section 104, Row A`, Aubrie Jean, Madison, Megan, Isabel, Zoë, Lauren, Sarah, Jessica, Mark, and Hannah linked shoulders, spelling out **`C-P-I! FORGERS!`** at the top of their lungs while Jordan’s left hand pumped in the air and his right hand tapped the preset cheer button Mark had programmed onto his `mPad`:

<aac>"GO FORGERS!"</aac>

As the fight song crashed to a triumphant brass finish, the stadium lights shifted from Foundry Maroon to deep cosmic violet.

"Keep the Marching Forgers right here with us!" **Cassidy** called into her microphone as orbital telemetry coordinates ticked upward from `1986` to `2016` on the 120-foot curved LED screen behind the Marching Forgers.

**Ryan** wheeled forward to his center-left mic and grinned out across the turf:

"Thirty years ago in 1986, Evan and Tyler walked into our basement and we wrote our very first song together about the cosmos and the rockets that get you there! Let's hear it, CPI!"

Jordan’s breath caught as a low, familiar analog synthesizer arpeggio rolled across the turf, opening [**"The Stardust Engine"**](https://music.raggiesoft.com/artists/the-stardust-engine/2016-live-at-the-crucible?track=1-03-the-stardust-engine)—the eponymous 1986 anthem from which the band took its name.

When all three hundred brass horns of the **CPI Marching Forgers** joined Cassidy’s soaring vocal (*"We are the Stardust Engine! / Racing through the night / We're burning on the fuel of a brand new light!"*) and Ryan’s lead guitar on the chorus, Jordan’s eyes shone behind his glasses.

![On stage inside The Crucible during 'The Stardust Engine', Ryan O'Connell plays a soaring lead on his sunburst electric guitar from his manual wheelchair on stage-left while Cassidy O'Connell sings and plays her wraparound analog synthesizer rig at center-right, backed by Evan Wright, Tyler Wright, and the 300 uniformed brass and percussionists of the CPI Marching Forgers under deep cosmic-violet nebula projections.]({{CDN}}/raggiesoft-books/images/scenes/aubrie/e007/c004/p002/stardust-engine-300-marching-forgers.jpg#fullwidth)

At halftime of the September 2014 Homecoming game, the **CPI Marching Forgers** had played *"The Stardust Engine"* on this exact turf while Jordan sat frozen in terror staring at a `24–0` scoreboard. Tonight, hearing the Marching Forgers play *"The Stardust Engine"* alongside Ryan, Cassidy, Evan, and Tyler while he sang along with his family in `Row A`, the first piece of that September 2014 ghost dissolved into the warm night air.

As the final brass chord of *"The Stardust Engine"* rang out across the valley, Ryan and Cassidy saluted the three hundred student musicians:

"Give it up for our alma mater's pride and joy—the three-hundred-strong **CPI Marching Forgers**!" Cassidy cheered as the stadium roared and the marching band filed proudly down the flanking ramps, waving to the lower bowl as they disappeared back into the North Field Tunnel.

***

> **Companion Perspective (*The Stardust Engine* — Ryan O'Connell's POV):** Read Act I from onstage as Ryan spots Jordan in `Section 104, Row A, Seat 1` on the camera-crane monitor and rolls out into the spotlight in [**The Stardust Engine — Book 6, Chapter 1, Part 2: *Act I: The Anvil Strike & The Marching Forgers***](https://books.raggiesoft.com/stardust-engine/book-6-reignition-live-at-the-crucible-2015-2016/chapter-1-live-at-the-crucible-may-21-2016/part-2-act-i-the-anvil-strike-the-marching-forgers) (or at [**`stardust.raggiesoft.com/novel`**](https://stardust.raggiesoft.com/novel)).

### Part 3: Not Your Doll & Fifty-Two to Nothing

**Date:** 2016-05-21 at 20:25 America/New_York

![Inside The Crucible at night during 'Fifty-Two to Nothing: The Norfolk Reckoning', massive glowing Foundry Maroon and Molten Orange numerals on the North End Zone scoreboard display 'CPI 52 — VDU 0' while in the foreground on the Section 104, Row A accessible terrace, Jordan Fuller raises his fist in triumph from his wheelchair as Mark Anderson claps his shoulder and Aubrie Jean Kelly, Madison Scott, and Zoë Wren Brooks cheer wildly around him.]({{CDN}}/raggiesoft-books/images/scenes/aubrie/e007/c004/p003/fifty-two-to-nothing-scoreboard.jpg)

#### 8:25 PM — Not Your Doll

While the main body of the **CPI Marching Forgers** exited into the tunnel, Jordan noticed a sharp twenty-piece brass and drumline honor guard stay behind on the upper back tier, standing at attention alongside five touring musicians stationed on the stage-left riser.

Wheeling up to his center microphone, **Ryan O'Connell** gestured toward the stage-left riser.

"Before we go any further tonight," Ryan told the sixty-five thousand fans filling the bowl, "there's a rule the four of us made in 1986 that we've never broken: **you will never hear a pre-recorded backing track at a Stardust Engine show.** Every synth pad, every harmony, every horn blast, and every drum fill you hear tonight is played live by human hands! Make some noise for our **Orbital Crew**—**Marcus Vance** on rhythm guitar and twelve-string, **Darius 'Doc' Holloway** on second kit and percussion, **Claire Lindqvist** on auxiliary analog synthesizers, and straight out of the CPI Music Department faculty, **Professor Julian Vance** on trumpet and **Elena Rostova** on saxophone!"

The student section roared for their own faculty professors as a rocket-launch countdown clock flashed across the 120-foot screen behind them.

"There's no opening act tonight, Blacksburg, and we aren't pacing ourselves!" Ryan called out, grinning into his mic. "Hold onto your seats! *Guidance is internal. T-minus ten... nine... eight... Seven... six... Main Engine Start! Four... three... two... one... Zero! Liftoff!*"

There was no filler and no holding back. From the explosive ignition roar of [**"Main Engine Start"**](https://music.raggiesoft.com/artists/the-stardust-engine/2016-live-at-the-crucible?track=1-04-main-engine-start) straight into the heavy, grinding industrial-rock thunder of [**"Hard Reset"**](https://music.raggiesoft.com/artists/the-stardust-engine/2016-live-at-the-crucible?track=1-05-hard-reset), the band tore across the stage with relentless intensity.

When the final chord of *"Hard Reset"* echoed off the upper deck, Jordan watched **Claire Lindqvist** step over into Cassidy’s main wraparound synthesizer rig—while **Cassidy O'Connell** did something Jordan had never seen her do on any of Daniel’s older concert videos.

Shrugging a studded black leather biker jacket over her maroon CPI tee, Cassidy stepped completely out from behind the keyboards, strode all the way out to the front-center lip of the stadium stage, and gripped the chrome stand microphone with both hands.

Above the stage, the 120-foot curved LED wall flickered with a giant, glossy 1980s neon-pink porcelain doll mask bound in golden chains.

"Back in nineteen eighty-seven," Cassidy’s voice rang out across the stadium—raw, fierce, and razor-sharp, "a record executive in a three-thousand-dollar suit looked at my brother and me and decided that a girl from Blacksburg wasn't allowed to play heavy rock and roll! They pointed at Ryan and called him the Engine... and they pointed at me, handed me a pink plastic script, and told me to smile, stay quiet behind the keyboards, and be their little *Stardust*! Well, tonight I'm standing front and center in our house—and nobody puts a cage around this voice ever again!"

On a thunderous dual-kit drum detonation from **Tyler Wright** and **Darius "Doc" Holloway**, twin fountains of white-hot gold and crimson pyrotechnic sparks erupted thirty feet into the night air along the stage edge, the porcelain doll mask on the 120-foot LED screen shattered into roaring flames behind bold rock lettering reading **`NOT YOUR DOLL`**, and **Ryan** and **Marcus Vance** locked into a crunching, palm-muted twin-guitar riff.

"That's [**'Not Your Doll'**](https://music.raggiesoft.com/artists/the-stardust-engine/2016-live-at-the-crucible?track=1-06-not-your-doll)!" **Daniel** shouted over the roar as **Laura** threw her fist in the air beside him.

![Cassidy O'Connell takes the stage front and center at the lip of The Crucible stage in a fitted black leather jacket over a maroon CPI rock tee, gripping a tilted chrome stand microphone with both hands and belting with fierce hard-rock intensity as Ryan O'Connell shreds his electric guitar in his manual wheelchair to her left, twin fountains of gold and crimson pyrotechnic sparks erupt along the stage edge, and the 120-foot curved LED screen shatters a neon-pink doll mask into roaring flames reading NOT YOUR DOLL.]({{CDN}}/raggiesoft-books/images/scenes/aubrie/e007/c004/p003/not-your-doll-cassidy-front-and-center.jpg#fullwidth)

Tilting the chrome microphone stand at a defiant angle at the very edge of the stage—channeling pure, unvarnished hard-rock ferocity—Cassidy tore into the verses with a grit-soaked rock belt that shook the limestone arches of **The Crucible**:

> *"You painted on a smile and you locked the door*<br>
> *Said a girl shouldn't roar on the stadium floor*<br>
> *You wanted sugar-coated, polite and tame*<br>
> *While you cashed every check written out in our name!*<br>
> *Tear up the contract, shatter the glass!*<br>
> *Watch your little empire crumble and pass!*<br>
> *I'm stepping out from behind the keys—*<br>
> *Down on the front line, off of my knees!*<br>
> *'CAUSE I'M NOT YOUR DOLL!*<br>
> *I'M NOT YOUR PRETTY TOY!*<br>
> *I'M NOT JUST A PICTURE FOR A POSTER BOY!*<br>
> *I'M NOT YOUR DOLL!*<br>
> *I'M HERE TO MAKE A CHOICE—*<br>
> *AND I'M GONNA MAKE YOU HEAR MY VOICE!"*

Down at the `Section 104, Row A` rail, **Aubrie Jean**, **Madison**, **Megan**, **Zoë**, **Lauren**, **Sarah**, **Jessica**, **Hannah**, and **Isabel** were all on their feet screaming the chorus at the top of their lungs—and right beside them in `Seat 1`, **Jordan** hit the custom concert page on his `mPad` as Cassidy dropped the guitars out to pounding dual stadium drums and yelled: *"Let me hear every voice in The Crucible tonight—if nobody owns you, scream it back to me!"*

Sixty-five thousand voices—and Jordan’s `mPad` speaker—roared back as one:

> **`"NOT YOUR DOLL!"`**

For nineteen years inside the `Fort Norfolk Compound`, **Aubrie Sinclair** had treated Jordan like a silent, programmable possession who wasn't allowed to have a voice, a choice, or a life of his own. Watching **Cassidy O'Connell** stand front and center before sixty-five thousand people and shatter every cage ever built around her sent a wave of pure electric adrenaline straight through Jordan’s chest.

And the band didn't slow down for a second. Right as the final cymbal crash of *"Not Your Doll"* rang out, Ryan’s raw, unvarnished guitar tore straight into the gritty garage-rock pulse of [**"Static"**](https://music.raggiesoft.com/artists/the-stardust-engine/2016-live-at-the-crucible?track=1-07-static), followed immediately by golden highway-headlight beams sweeping across the field for [**"Midnight Drivers"**](https://music.raggiesoft.com/artists/the-stardust-engine/2016-live-at-the-crucible?track=1-08-midnight-drivers).

Seated in a custom-cambered black manual wheelchair built for the stage, Ryan didn't just play lead guitar—he commanded the entire sixty-five-thousand-seat stadium from his chair, spinning effortlessly on his rear wheels during his guitar solo on *"Midnight Drivers"* and locking eyes with Evan and Tyler on the drum riser. For Jordan, watching a man in a manual wheelchair headline a sold-out football stadium while sixty-five thousand people screamed his name was a revelation he could feel in his bones.

***

#### 8:45 PM — Fifty-Two to Nothing

As the final highway chord of *"Midnight Drivers"* faded into the night air, Jordan wondered where they would go next.

Instead of counting off another song, Ryan wheeled to the front edge of the stage and pointed the neck of his guitar straight across the stadium bowl toward the towering **North End Zone LED Scoreboard**—the exact scoreboard that had displayed **`HOME: 0 — VISITOR: 24`** when **Virginia Dominion University (`VDU`)** from Norfolk had routed CPI on Homecoming Saturday in September 2014 and triggered Jordan’s catastrophic stadium collapse.

"Hey, Forger Nation," Ryan said into his microphone, a wicked, knowing grin spreading across his face as the crowd began to buzz. "Two autumns ago, in September 2014, a certain football team from down in Norfolk walked into this house on Homecoming and put an ugly number up on that North End Zone board. And then last October, when our guys traveled down Interstate 64 to Norfolk for *their* Homecoming... their student section had the nerve to print up ten thousand T-shirts with that old score on their chests."

Sixty-five thousand CPI fans booed in gleeful, unified indignation.

In `Section 104, Row A, Seat 1`, **Mark** grabbed **Jordan**’s right shoulder, his eyes wide with excitement. "J—look up at the North End Zone board!"

High above the Gothic limestone arches of the North End Zone, the giant stadium scoreboard suddenly flickered to life. For two seconds, it displayed the ghostly, hated numerals from September 2014:

```
HOME: 0 — VISITOR: 38
```

And then, on a thunderous marching snare roll from **Tyler Wright**, digital flames of Foundry Maroon and Molten Orange shattered the old numbers off the screen, replacing them in thirty-foot-tall blazing gold digits with the final score from October 2015 in Norfolk:

```
CPI FORGERS: 52 — VDU ADMIRALS: 0
```

"How'd those T-shirts look by the fourth quarter, Forger Nation?!" **Cassidy** roared into her mic as the stadium erupted into one of the loudest ovations of the night. "This is [**'Fifty-Two to Nothing: The Norfolk Reckoning'**](https://music.raggiesoft.com/artists/the-stardust-engine/2016-live-at-the-crucible?track=1-09-fifty-two-to-nothing-the-norfolk-reckoning)!"

```

As Tyler’s thunderous marching snare cadence and Ryan’s stomping arena riff shook the stadium floor, Jordan looked straight up at the glowing **`52 — 0`** numerals on the North End Zone scoreboard that had haunted his nightmares Freshman Fall.

With **Aubrie Jean**, **Madison**, **Megan**, **Zoë**, and **Mark** cheering wildly around his wheelchair, Jordan raised his right fist high into the warm May night as sixty-five thousand Forgers roared the chorus in unison—and from across the turf, Ryan lifted his right hand off his guitar strings for two beats and pointed a direct salute straight toward `Section 104, Row A, Seat 1`:

> ***"FIFTY-TWO TO NOTHING! PUT IT ON THE BOARD!***<br>
> ***HEAR THE MIGHTY THUNDER OF THE FORGER CHORD!***<br>
> ***YOU WORE THE OLD NUMBERS ON YOUR HOMECOMING CHEST—***<br>
> ***TILL THE MOUNTAINS CAME DOWN AND PUT THE TALK TO REST!"***

When the stadium finally finished roaring the `52–0` chorus, Cassidy walked over toward the stage-right wing and pointed down into the monitor bunker, where Jordan could see **Holly O'Connell** standing in a tailored blazer beside the recording engineers.

"This next one is from the *Lost Sounds* vault—for our little sister Holly, who took a one-dollar bill in nineteen eighty-six and saved our lives!" Cassidy called out, launching the band into two blistering rarities from [***Lost Sounds***](https://music.raggiesoft.com/artists/the-stardust-engine/2007-lost-sounds): [**"The Contract"**](https://music.raggiesoft.com/artists/the-stardust-engine/2016-live-at-the-crucible?track=1-10-the-contract) and [**"Steel and Synthetics"**](https://music.raggiesoft.com/artists/the-stardust-engine/2016-live-at-the-crucible?track=1-11-steel-and-synthetics).

On the final ten-second guitar-and-synthesizer chord of *"Steel and Synthetics"*, a deep, sub-bass power-down sweep echoed through the stadium PA—and every floodlight tower around **The Crucible** abruptly plunged into total darkness.

***

> **Companion Perspective (*The Stardust Engine* — Ryan O'Connell's POV):** Read Act II from onstage as Ryan points his guitar neck at the North End Zone scoreboard for *"Fifty-Two to Nothing"* and salutes Jordan in `Section 104, Row A, Seat 1` in [**The Stardust Engine — Book 6, Chapter 1, Part 3: *Act II: The Orbital Crew, Not Your Doll & Fifty-Two to Nothing***](https://books.raggiesoft.com/stardust-engine/book-6-reignition-live-at-the-crucible-2015-2016/chapter-1-live-at-the-crucible-may-21-2016/part-3-act-ii-the-orbital-crew-not-your-doll-fifty-two-to-nothing) (or at [**`stardust.raggiesoft.com/novel`**](https://stardust.raggiesoft.com/novel)).

### Part 4: Escape Velocity (Ad Astra), Tidal Lock & Mile Marker 98

**Date:** 2016-05-21 at 20:55 America/New_York

![Cassidy O'Connell stands front and center at the edge of The Crucible stadium stage singing 'Escape Velocity (Ad Astra)' with soaring emotion while Ryan O'Connell plays a zero-gravity solo on his sunburst electric guitar from his manual wheelchair to her left, backed by a 120-foot curved LED screen and 65,000 synchronized LED wristbands glowing in the crimson reds, sapphire blues, ultraviolet purples, and solar gold of a deep-space nebula.]({{CDN}}/raggiesoft-books/images/scenes/aubrie/e007/c004/p004/escape-velocity-ad-astra-cassidy-nebula.jpg)

#### 8:55 PM — Escape Velocity (Ad Astra)

In the sudden, breathless darkness after *"Steel and Synthetics"*, all four towering stadium floodlight banks remained completely out.

Sitting in `Section 104, Row A, Seat 1`, **Jordan** looked up at the open Appalachian night sky above the Gothic limestone arches and then back across the dark field toward the stage, wondering what the band was setting up in the dark. Beside him, **Aubrie Jean** and **Madison** leaned forward against the terrace rail, squinting into the dim blue work lights on the stage deck.

Out on the auxiliary riser, keyboardist **Claire Lindqvist** stayed behind the main wraparound synthesizer rig—while **Cassidy O'Connell** walked out alone to the very center edge of the stage, holding a wireless handheld microphone in both hands.

Nobody said a word into the microphones.

Instead, a low sub-bass synthesizer drone and a lonely, haunting woodwind melody began to drift out across the silent turf—followed seconds later by Cassidy raising the microphone to her lips and singing a soaring, wordless operatic vocalise that echoed off the upper decks into the mountain night.

Down in `Seat 7`, **Daniel Brooks** froze so suddenly that his hands clamped white-knuckled onto the aluminum railing.

"Wait a minute..." Daniel whispered, turning his head toward **Mark**, **Zoë**, and **Jordan** with his eyes wide behind his glasses. "Do you hear that woodwind and that vocalise?!"

**Mark**’s jaw dropped. "Wait—that's the opening of [**'Ad Astra'**](https://music.raggiesoft.com/artists/the-stardust-engine/2016-live-at-the-crucible?track=escape-velocity-ad-astra-live-at-the-crucible)!"

"No way," **Laura** gasped beside Daniel, her hand flying to her mouth. "They've *never* played *'Ad Astra'* at a concert! The studio recording on *Hard Reset* is over fifteen minutes long! Are they just doing a short intro teaser for another song, or are they actually going to play it?!"

Across every section of **The Crucible**, a wave of stunned, electric murmurs rippled through sixty-five thousand fans as the same realization hit the entire stadium at once. Even Jordan felt his pulse jump in his throat—he knew from listening to Daniel’s CDs in the Geneva Street basement that [*"Escape Velocity (Ad Astra)"*](https://music.raggiesoft.com/artists/the-stardust-engine/2016-live-at-the-crucible?track=escape-velocity-ad-astra-live-at-the-crucible)—commonly known to Stardust Engine fans simply as *"Ad Astra"* when referring to it informally—was Cassidy’s monumental four-part progressive rock epic from the band's Wilderness Years, and that conventional wisdom among Forger Nation fans was that it was far too massive and intricate to ever be performed on a live stage.

Nobody in the stadium knew whether Cassidy was just singing a sixty-second opening prelude before transitioning into *"Tidal Lock"*, or if the band was about to attempt the unthinkable.

Then the gentle woodwind shattered into a blistering 16th-note analog synthesizer pulse and **Tyler Wright**’s driving double-kick drums.

Cold, stark white searchlights dropped straight down from the overhead truss, boxing Cassidy in at the front lip of the stage like the bars of a courtroom cage. Standing completely exposed at the edge of the stage without a keyboard in front of her, Cassidy tore into the opening verses with raw, trembling intensity:

> *"The Shark was right, the nuke went off!*<br>
> *We won the battle, but at what cost?!*<br>
> *We're radioactive, we're litigious!*<br>
> *We're just the joke, the victim-saints!*<br>
> *I'm trapped inside this Wilderness!*<br>
> *This Fortress built on bitterness!*<br>
> *This isn't freedom... this is a cell...*<br>
> *This righteous hell..."*

In `Seat 1`, Jordan’s breath caught as the heavy drums dropped away and Cassidy’s voice softened to a quiet, aching confession in the dark: *"The fight is over, the dragon's slain / So why am I still in chains?"*

Jordan felt a chill run all the way down his spine. Anyone who had ever survived a long war—whether it was a predatory lawsuit that nearly destroyed your family or nineteen years locked inside a compound in Norfolk—knew that terrifying quiet after the courtroom gavel fell, when the doors were finally unlocked on paper, and you had to figure out how to stop living inside the fortress of what had been done to you.

Suddenly, a dark, pulsing bass sequencer began to throb through the stadium floor.

The white searchlight cage snapped off. **Ryan O'Connell** wheeled his manual chair right up beside his sister at center stage and locked into a roaring, high-gravity guitar riff with **Marcus Vance** as twin pillars of crimson and solar-gold light shot straight up into the Appalachian sky. Striding across the stage edge with her microphone, Cassidy belted the explosive launch chorus:

> *"I'm climbing! Climbing! Past the point of no return!*<br>
> *The engines screaming, watch the bridges burn!*<br>
> *Pushing through the max-Q, the violent shake!*<br>
> *Every single promise that I had to break!*<br>
> *I'm reaching for the sky, I'm breaking the hold!*<br>
> *A story that has never been told!*<br>
> *Escape velocity! I'm finally free!*<br>
> *Ad astra! (To the stars!)*<br>
> *That's where I'll be!"*

"They aren't just playing an intro!" Mark shouted over the thunder of the drums, grabbing Jordan’s shoulder in disbelief as Ryan’s sunburst electric guitar and Claire’s synthesizers traded breathless, high-velocity solos while the 120-foot screen behind them showed the horizon of the Earth curving away into the black of space. "They're really doing it!"

As Cassidy hit the soaring, sustained high note of *"Into the silent, endless night!"*, every guitar, bass, and drum on stage cut out at the exact same instant.

Dead, weightless silence fell over the stage.

Around the stadium bowl, sixty-five thousand people erupted into a massive, deafening roar—half the crowd leaping to their feet cheering, convinced the band had just brought a six-minute concert arrangement of the song to a triumphant finish.

"Wait—look at Ryan and Cassidy!" **Aubrie Jean** whispered, squeezing Jordan’s hand and pointing toward center stage.

Out on the darkened stage, neither Cassidy nor Ryan had moved an inch to take a bow. They stood completely still in the dark as the roar of the crowd echoed off the mountains.

And then, rising underneath the cheering stadium, a slow, floating fretless bass pulse from **Evan Wright** and liquid, zero-gravity synthesizer pads began to swell through the night air.

Across the 120-foot curved LED wall behind the stage—and across all sixty-five thousand wristbands in the stands—the entire stadium bowl suddenly bloomed into a breathtaking, three-dimensional deep-space nebula of crimson reds, sapphire blues, ultraviolet purples, and radiant solar gold.

"Oh, my God," Daniel breathed, his voice cracking as he wiped his eyes behind his glasses. "That was just Main Engine Cutoff. We're in orbit. They're playing the whole epic!"

![Cassidy O'Connell stands front and center at the edge of The Crucible stadium stage singing 'Escape Velocity (Ad Astra)' with soaring emotion while Ryan O'Connell plays a zero-gravity solo on his sunburst electric guitar from his manual wheelchair to her left, backed by a 120-foot curved LED screen and 65,000 synchronized LED wristbands glowing in the crimson reds, sapphire blues, ultraviolet purples, and solar gold of a deep-space nebula.]({{CDN}}/raggiesoft-books/images/scenes/aubrie/e007/c004/p004/escape-velocity-ad-astra-cassidy-nebula.jpg#fullwidth)

Standing front and center in the glow of sixty-five thousand stars, Cassidy looked up at the glowing tiers of her alma mater and sang the weightless cosmic chorus—*"I'm loved by the sun! I'm held by the void! / An orbit just begun! A life not destroyed!"*—before her voice rose into the bridge that every lifelong fan knew by heart:

> *"I see the colors of the nebula*<br>
> *A place I've only seen in dreams*<br>
> *The reds, the blues, the purples call*<br>
> *Flowing in majestic streams...*<br>
> *This is the place I was meant to be!*<br>
> *This is the Stardust that is me!*<br>
> *The cosmos and the rocket's fire!*<br>
> *My one, my only true desire!*<br>
> *Loved by the sun!"*

Beside Jordan in `Section 104, Row A`, **Aubrie Jean** wiped a tear from her cheek and held her glowing violet-and-gold wristband up beside Jordan’s as **Ryan** closed his eyes in his wheelchair and played a long, weeping, zero-gravity guitar solo that seemed to hang suspended in the mountain air without a single tether to the ground.

Nobody in the stadium was checking a watch or counting minutes anymore; sixty-five thousand people were completely lost inside the music. When the floating nebula pads finally gave way to a crisp, syncopated acoustic-and-electric groove from Ryan, Evan, Tyler, and the touring section, the entire stadium surged back to life as the song angled homeward through the atmosphere and splashed down into the warm ocean of a healed new world:

> *"The Cage is broken, the victim-saint is gone!*<br>
> *A new clean script is in my head!*<br>
> *The friction burned away in the fire!*<br>
> *Leaving only my true desire!*<br>
> *I'm not escaping anymore!*<br>
> *I'm coming home to a brand new shore!"*

Stepping right up to the front edge of the stage, Cassidy held her microphone out with both hands toward the stands—and all sixty-five thousand fans in **The Crucible**, along with Jordan’s `mPad` and everyone in `Row A`, roared the four words back at the top of their lungs:

> **`"HELD BY THE SUN!"`**

Riding a joyous, full-band stadium-rock outro through three final cries of ***"Ad astra!"***, the entire nine-piece band slammed down together on a massive final chord.

For a full minute, the sixty-five-thousand-seat stadium shook with a standing ovation so loud Jordan could feel the concrete terrace vibrating beneath his wheels. Standing at the front lip of the stage with tears shining behind her rectangular glasses, Cassidy raised a hand to her heart, leaned into her microphone, and whispered a breathless, overwhelmed:

> *"Thank you so much..."*

```
